DON’T TOUCH MY SANCTUARY ! (Guess what happens to a church when the very doctrine that became its miraculous lifeline nearly two centuries ago and over the years its most distinctive hallmark... could now end up to be its most biblically unjustifiable millstone ?)

There is a sanctuary in heaven, the true tabernacle that the Lord set up and not humans. In it Christ ministers on our behalf… In 1844, at the end of the prophetic period of 2300 days, He entered the second and last phase of His atoning ministry… It is a work of investigative judgment which is part of the ultimate disposition of all sin, typified by the cleansing of the ancient Hebrew sanctuary on the Day of Atonement.

Adventist fundamental beliefs (1980)

Seventh-day Adventists accept the Bible as their only creed and hold certain fundamental beliefs to be the teaching of the Holy Scriptures. These beliefs, as set forth here, constitute the church’s understanding and expression of the teaching of Scripture. Revision of these statements may be expected at a General Conference Session when the church is led by the Holy Spirit to a fuller understanding of Bible truth or finds better language in which to express the teachings of God’s Holy Word.

Adventist fundamental beliefs (2015)

As Adventists, many of our "unique" doctrines are not, really, unique. After all, other Christians (not many, admittedly) into greater focus. keep the seventh-day Sabbath, as well. Though a majority of the Christian world believes in the immortality of the soul, other Christians understand that the dead sleep in the grave until the resurrection, either the first or second. Various "Adventist" teachings, i.e., eternal destruction (as opposed to eternal torment) or the nature of the millennium, can be found elsewhere too. In fact, almost all our doctrines are scattered throughout Christendom.  Except one: the 1844 pre-Advent judgment. For some, this fact is worrisome; Why don't more Christians see it, as well? For others, the uniqueness of the doctrine points even more powerfully to the special calling of the Seventh-day Adventist Church. It's precisely because no one else teaches this judgment that we have been raised to do so. From this doctrine, perhaps more than any other, our distinct identity as Seventh-day Adventists arises.

Sabbath School quarterly (The Gospel, 1844, and Judgment, 2006)

The [sanctuary] doctrine is, to me, the most colossal, psychological, face-saving phenomenon in religious history. … We personally do not believe that there is even a suspicion of a verse in Scripture to sustain such a peculiar position, and we further believe that any effort to establish it is stale, flat, and unprofitable.

Donald Grey Barnhouse (Are Seventh-day Adventists Christians? A New Look at Seventh-Day Adventism, Eternity magazine, 1956)

With the traditional Adventist interpretation of Daniel 8:14 as thesis, the historic-linguistic-contextual method of exegesis, which stands in opposition to it at practically every point, is its antithesis. (…) Our interpretational thesis and methodological antithesis are as impossible and mutually exclusive as matter and anti-matter and have the potential of mutually destroying each other, and the church as well. While Adventist Bible scholars have adopted the historical method, the church, as a whole, still basically practices the proof text method. Unresolved this dichotomy could have unfortunate consequences. The only way to resolve a problem such as this, is to find synthesis on a higher level of understanding.

Raymond F. Cottrell (A Hermeneutic for Daniel 8:14, unpublished manuscript, 1980)

Raymond has suggested to us a "way out" from the "dilemma" our denomination is now supposed to be caught in.  That is an escape mechanism based on a theory of the most "miraculous" our Church has ever been placed in front of.” (…) “By way of introduction, Elder Cottrell tries to convince us of the unqualified benefits our denomination has enjoyed as a direct result of one great historical event:  A new generation of Seventh-day Adventist scholars were finally blessed with the golden opportunity of education, which had been denied to our Bible students in former days.  According to Cottrell, we observed a marked improvement in the accuracy of conclusions arrived at in Adventist Bible research precisely at the time when those new scholars, with their more sophisticated knowledge, started making their impact in our offices and class rooms. Of course he does not, in this order of ideas, put any personal blame on the older researchers.  They just had the misfortune of not being properly educated.  So they were bound to come out as self-educated men, that is, men of mediocre scholarliness.  The new enlightenment we are now enjoying, as a denomination, is alleged as the positive reason for a new hope for the future.  Infallible evidence of this is a new awareness of problems our previous men of Biblical research were never confronted with.  Cottrell is referring to the increasing impossibility of harmonizing the actual contents of some contents of some Biblical texts with what our pioneers and the Spirit of Prophecy writings were once induced to put down, firmly and securely, as landmarks of our official creed. Brother Cottrell never tires of repeating that the large majority of these modern SDA Bible scholars agree wholeheartedly with him regarding the problem aspect of fundamental statements made by Ellen White in, for instance, absolutely decisive chapters of the Great Controversy.  Here Cottrell is not one bit less emphatic than Brinsmead and Ford, that objective scholarliness opens a gulf of disparity between The Bible and Ellen White.But it is in the suggested "remedy" to this situation Cottrell manifests the uniqueness of his spirit.  It is his "solution" that is without a rival in the history of Seventh-day Adventism. By and large, Protestants have never acquired any fame comparable to that of Catholics for what theology and philosophy have called "reconciliatio oppositorum"* or "complexio oppositorum"**.  In fact it is rather secular philosophy -- and not at all traditional religion -- that has developed the habit of astonishing the world of thinking men by having the boldness to blow up the virtual problem of mutually exclusive stand-points into thin air. (…) But what is his "solution" really like then, in this concrete instance?  How does Cottrell manage to still defend the doctrine of inerrancy regarding the teachings coming to us through Ellen G. White's ministry?  Nobody, you see, is more emphatic in extolling Ellen White as the great prophetess par excellence of the people of God in the endtime.  Therefore, he says, we must accept what her message has handed down to us in terms of basic landmarks for our faith as the very truth, the full truth and nothing but the truth. But then how come that Ellen White apparently can permit herself to go so boldly against certain things the Bible says about Christ's ministry in the sanctuary?  For here, as we recall, Cottrell is more emphatic maybe than anybody else, pointing out the great superiority of, according to Cottrell, the modern research method.  The modern researchers' accurate knowledge was, according to Cottrell, arrived at for the simple reason that they applied the historicolinguistic method of exegesis.  This has led them to conclusions quite opposite to those expressed solemnly and categorically by Ellen White in the Great Controversy.  But how then can the Prophetess, with "her" now classical doctrines about 1844 and the Investigative Judgement dare to go contrary to the "evident" testimony of the Scriptures?Cottrell's explanation is scaringly simple and straightforward:  Ellen White, in her capacity as the great Prophetess of the endtime has a right to do all this.  She is divinely entitled to reinterpret prophecies of the Bible in accordance with God's special intentions in the endtime.  "Parallel instances" of this kind are referred to, for instance Paul's "innovating interpretations" of statements in the Old Testament.  To the first century Christians such OT prophecies constituted the treasury from which they had to draw. 

Carsten Johnsen (Omega II, 1982)

Time and again competent non-Adventist Bible scholars have acknowledged that there is a biblical basis for cardinal points of Adventist faith such as the Sabbath, the second Advent and the nature of man. But without exception… they denounce our interpretation of Daniel 8:14 as eisegesis of the worst sort… Seventh-day Adventists identify the sanctuary mentioned in Daniel 8:14 as the sanctuary in heaven… and they understand its cleansing as the blotting out of the confessed sins of God’s repentant people during the course of an investigative judgment, on an antitypical day of atonement that began in 1844. … Adventist teachings that cluster around Daniel 8:14 have proved to be an impassible barrier to the thoughtful consideration of the Advent message… The date 1844… is pivotal of SDA faith. Destroy these and certain conclusions are self-evident. There would be no adequate basis for the existence of SDA. … The invariable rule appears to be that the more a non-Adventist knows about the Bible, the less disposed he is to look with favor on the Adventist interpretation of Daniel 8:14… The first major incentive to devote serious attention to the problem in Daniel 8:14 arose during the course of editing the Seventh-day Adventist Bible Commentary… Within a few months after the publication of Volume 4… came the series of protracted doctrinal discussions with Walter R. Martin and Donald Grey Barnhouse. … Finally, in 1958… I wrote to 27 leading Adventist Bible scholars… All 27 responded… A careful analysis… made evident that we had no satisfactory answer to the criticisms… Not one of the 27 believed that there was a linguistic or contextual basis for applying Daniel 8:14 to the heavenly sanctuary, an antitypical day of atonement, or 1844. As a result… a select “Committee on Problems in the Book of Daniel” [was appointed]… The majority and the minority both reached the same conclusions, but by different routes. … As a result of this impasse, the committee finally agreed to issue no formal report… My study… concluded that… the sanctuary of Daniel 8:14 is the same sanctuary referred to in verses 11-13, that is, the ancient temple in Jerusalem; that the “cleansing” or “restoration”… constituted its purification and rededication after desecration by the little horn… I believe that the hermeneutical principles outlined above provided an adequate inspired basis for applying the 2,300 evenings-mornings to 2,300 literal years terminating in 1844… Let it be clearly understood that the hermeneutic here proposed in no way alters the teachings we have traditionally based on Daniel 8:14. It does not affect the content of these teachings, but the method by which they are established as truth… In arriving at these conclusions, William Miller and other early Adventists basically followed the proof text method… The proof text method is basically what Bible scholars call eisegesis… During the 1930s Adventist college Bible teachers began to make consistent use of the historical-linguistic-contextual method… By the mid-1930s we were far up a theological cul de sac… For 25 years or more, the Bible scholars of the church have been well aware of the exegetical problems our conventional interpretation of Daniel 8:14… encounters… Non-Adventist critics… object that it cannot be derived from the words of Scripture but is superimposed upon them. … The problem is clear, especially if one remembers the unanimous acknowledgment of leading Adventist biblical scholars, clearly expressed in the 1958 poll, that there is no linguistic or contextual basis for our traditional interpretation of this passage. … A conclusive case for the heavenly sanctuary and a pre-Advent judgment can be made directly from Scripture, wholly apart from Daniel 8:14 and Hebrews 9… Can we not be willing to rely on these other passages…?"

Raymond F. Cottrell ("Sanctuary Debate: A Question of Method", Spectrum, 1980)

"The traditional interpretation of Daniel 8:14 with its sanctuary and investigative judgment, which gave birth to Seventh-day Adventism and accounts for its existence as a distinct entity within Christendom, has been the object of more criticism and debate, by both Adventists and non-Adventists, than all other facets of its belief system combined. (...) There can be no question as to the sincerity, diligence, and integrity of those who formulated the traditional Adventist interpretation of Daniel 8:14. It is equally obvious that they were following the flawed principles of the prooftext method: (1) In four major instances they adopted translation errors where the KJV misrepresents the Hebrew text. (2) They completely ignored the literary context in which Daniel 8:14 occurs. (3) They likewise ignored the historical context specified by the first six chapters and chapter 9:1-19 of the book. (...) In the years immediately following October 22, 1844 the traditional sanctuary doctrine was an important asset for stabilizing the faith of disappointed Adventists. Today it is an equally significant liability and deterrent to the faith, confidence, and salvation of biblically literate Adventists and non-Adventists alike. It was present truth following the great disappointment on October 22, 1844. It is not present truth in the year of our Lord 2002. Quod erat demonstrandum! »  

Raymond F. Cottrell (The Sanctuary Doctrine – Asset or Liability?,  2002)

Then I heard one saint speaking, and another saint said unto that certain saint which spake, How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot? And he said unto me, unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed.

Daniel 8: 13-14

Then I heard one angel ask another, “How long will these things that were seen in the vision continue? How long will an awful sin replace the daily sacrifices? How long will the army of heaven and the Temple be trampled on?” I heard the other angel answer, “It will continue for 2,300 evenings and mornings, during which sacrifices will not be offered. Then the Temple will be restored.”

Daniel 8: 13-14 (Good News Translation) 

And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day. 

Genesis 1:5

And he shall make an atonement for the holy place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Israel, and because of their transgressions in all their sins… 

Leviticus 16 

Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary. (...) But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people. (...) But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands… Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.

Hebrews 9: 1-12

But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles: and the holy city shall they tread under foot forty and two months. And I will give power unto my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and threescore days, clothed in sackcloth.

Revelation 11:2–3

And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they should feed her there a thousand two hundred and threescore days. And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness, into her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent.

Revelation 12:6, 14

And there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given unto him to continue forty and two months.

Revelation 13:5

But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.”

Jesus (Matthew 24:36)
 
But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.

Jesus (Mark 13:32)

It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power.

Acts 1: 7

The king had sent letters by messengers unto Jerusalem and the cities of Juda that they should follow the strange laws of the land, And forbid burnt offerings, and sacrifice, and drink offerings, in the temple; and that they should profane the sabbaths and festival days (…) Now the 15th day of the month Casleu, in the 145th year, they set up the abomination of desolation upon the altar, and builded idol altars throughout the cities of Juda on every side; And burnt incense at the doors of their houses, and in the streets. And when they had rent in pieces the books of the law which they found, they burnt them with fire. And whosoever was found with any the book of the testament, or if any committed to the law, the king's commandment was, that they should put him to death. (…) Now the 25th day of the month they did sacrifice upon the idol altar, which was upon the altar of God.

1 Maccabees 1:44–59

Now on the 25th day of the 9th month, which is called the month Casleu, in the 148th year, they rose up betimes in the morning, And offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings, which they had made. Look, at what time and what day the heathen had profaned it, even in that was it dedicated with songs, and citherns, and harps, and cymbals.

1 Maccabees 4:52–54

These things were done on the very same day on which their Divine worship had fallen off, and was reduced to a profane and common use, after three years’ time; for so it was, that the temple was made desolate by Antiochus, and so continued for three years. This desolation happened to the temple in the 145th year, on the 25th day of the month Apeliens… but it was dedicated anew, on the same day, the 25th of the month Apeliens, on the 148th year.

Josephus (Jewish Antiquities 12.316–320)

Antiochus, called Epiphanes, on defeating the Jews had entered the innermost sanctuary of the god’s temple… he sacrificed before the image of the founder and the open-air altar of the god a great sow, and poured its blood over them. Then… he ordered that their holy books… should be sprinkled with the broth of the meat; that the lamp… which burns continually in the temple should be extinguished; and that the high priest and the rest of the Jews should be compelled to partake of the meat.

Diodorus Siculus (Library of History 34/35.1.3–5)

Unto two thousand and three hundred evenings, mornings] i.e. successive evenings and mornings: cf. Daniel 8:26 -the vision of the evenings and the mornings." The expression is peculiar; but it seems to have been suggested by the fact that the burnt-offering (Daniel 8:11; Daniel 8:13) was offered morning and evening daily (Exodus 29:38-42); the meaning consequently is that this offering would cease for 2300 times, i.e. during 1150 days (...). In Daniel 7:25 (...), Daniel 12:7, the period of persecution is to last 31/2 years, i.e. (if the year be reckoned at 360 days) 1260 days, or, if account be taken of the varying possibilities of the Calendar in use in the 2nd century b.c., 1274 or 1309 days; and, according to 1Ma 1:54; 1Ma 4:52-53, the interval which actually elapsed between the erection of the heathen altar upon the altar of burnt-offering, on the 15th of Chisleu, b.c. 168, and the dedication of the new altar on the 25th of Chisleu, b.c. 165, was 3 years and 10 days (i.e. 1090, 1102 3, or 1132 3 days). The period assigned here is some months less than 31/2 years; it is not however identified with the entire period of the persecution, but only with that part of it during which the daily sacrifice was interrupted and the Temple desecrated. It seems therefore (cf. Daniel 12:11) that 15 Chisleu b.c. 168 must be the terminus a quo, the end of the period assigned not agreeing precisely with the event.  By some commentators the expression -evening, morning" has been understood as equivalent to day (cf. Genesis 1:5, Genesis 1:8)

Cambridge Bible for Schools and Colleges

The phrase ʿereb bōqer (“evening morning”) in Daniel 8:14 is widely understood by critical commentators as referring to the interruption of the daily morning and evening sacrifices. 2,300 such offerings equal 1,150 days (roughly three years), matching the historical desecration of the temple under Antiochus IV Epiphanes (c. 167–164 BCE). (...) The Greek and Latin versions mistakenly read twenty-three hundred days.

John J. Collins (Hermeneia, 1993)

Twenty-seven of our top men in language and exegesis. All twenty-seven replied that it was impossible to make a linguistic connection between Dan. 8:14 and Lev. 16. There is no Biblical basis for assuming that the year-day be applied to Dan. 8 and 9. 

Desmond Ford (Glacier View Manuscript, 1980)

Thus Dan 8:14 has nothing to do with the high priestly ministry of Christ or an extended chronology ending in 1844. In the context of Daniel, it is a forecast of how long the Jerusalem Temple would linger in a desecrated state… during the reign of Antiochus IV. 

Jerry Gladson

You have been misinformed “that the only correct translation of Dan 8:14 is ‘until 2,300 days.’” The Hebrew phrase can only mean ‘For 2,300 evenings and mornings,’ which equals 1,150 days. I know of no one who translates the phrase 2,300 days. Genesis 1 is not relevant to this phrase…. the reference is to the 1,150 evening and 1,150 morning sacrifices.

Alexander A. Di Lella (Catholic University of America)

When Antiochus IV and the Greeks arrive, and they conquer Jerusalem, they defile the temple, as we know from the proper story of Hanukkah. They bring the knowledge with them. Why do they have the knowledge? Because these roof tiles, or at least modern roof tiles, were invented in the seventh century B.C., in the middle of Greece itself, and then spread around the world, but never to the Middle East." (…) We can date each strata about the contents of that strata. And, for the most part, it depends on the pottery itself. We know that during certain periods, certain types of pottery, meaning vessels, pottery vessels were used. In this case, it was really both the coins and the pottery itself that showed us that the strata or the layer where these roof tiles were found was sealed in the second century B.C.E., so we know that couldn't have been later. (…) Weinberger proved that the material is local, the clay is local, from an area west of Jerusalem called the Motza … with the addition of sand and straw, which are also local. (…) Other than the Acra, this fortress, these roof tiles are also very clear proof for the presence of the Greeks during the same time period. The first book of Maccabees describes the arrival of the Greeks, Antiochus IV and the struggle. And then much later tradition talks about the defilement of the temple and the miracle of the oil and eight days. That's why today all the Jews celebrate Hanukkah, but we have never really had real material proof for the presence of the Greeks themselves.

Dr. Filip Vukosavović (2023)

During archaeological excavations operated by the Israel Antiquities Authority and Tel-Aviv University, 16 pieces of ceramic roof tiles were discovered. (…) The tiles discovered (...) in City of David National Park date back to the time period of Greek Seleucid King Antiochus IV Epiphanes. (…) Antiochus IV is known widely from the story of Hanukkah as the oppressor. He was a ruler who spread Greek culture to other territories. He enforced Hellenistic views in Jerusalem and desecrated the sacred temple in Jerusalem, causing a revolt of the Jewish people, known as the Maccabean revolt, according to the story in the book of the Maccabees. (…) To obtain his power, Antiochus IV built a fortress known as the "Acra." There has often been mystery surrounding the fortress, especially regarding its exact location, a question pondered for decades. A few years ago, there were walls discovered belonging to an ancient fortress. This provided good material evidence proving its existence but could not stand as proof alone. The discovery of roof tiles near these walls makes a strong argument that the fortress was, in fact, in that location, according to Vukosavović. Ceramic roofing tiles were invented in Greece and became popular due to their durability and water resistance. They weren't commonly used in Israel until hundreds of years later. The presence of these materials in the city can be connected to Antiochus IV himself.

Fox News (2023)

text:
The Tirupparankundram Temple, widely revered as the first of the six sacred abodes of Lord Murugan, was originally conceived as a Shiva–Vishnu shrine and subsequently incorporated Shakta elements. The arrangement of the shrines in the accompanying layout offers fascinating insights into this architectural and religious evolution.

1. Vishnu Durga Shrine
4. Gajalakshmi Shrine
5. Bhuvaneswari Shrine
6. Jyeshta Devi Shrine

The unnumbered shrine originally housed the Saptamatrikas, whose images have since been relocated to the Gajalakshmi shrine.

What makes the Pandyan rock cut temples particularly fascinating is their remarkable integration of multiple worship traditions within a single sacred complex. Shaiva, Vaishnava and Shakta traditions coexist in a carefully conceived architectural arrangement, reflecting the rich diversity of religious practices within our Dharma.

Tirupparankundram stands as a beautiful testimony to this multidimensional character of early Pandyan temple architecture.

15 TIMES A SHRINKING PROFIT: PENSKE AUTOMOTIVE $PAG'S OWNERS ARE PAYING FULL PRICE TO TAKE IT PRIVATE:

The Growth Len5 is watching Penske Automotive Group (PAG) at $212.00, +$17.21 / +8.84% on Thursday, and $212.59 after hours, +$0.59 / +0.28% from that close. It is #6 of 30.

The Michigan company runs car dealerships in the US, Britain and five other countries, is one of North America's biggest Freightliner truck dealers, and owns 28.9% of the truck-leasing company Penske Transportation Solutions. On Thursday its two largest owners, Roger Penske's private Penske Corporation and a Japanese trading house, agreed to buy out every other shareholder for $212 a share in cash:

Mitsui & Co. (MITSY) at $625.51, +$1.29 / +0.21% on Thursday.

Mitsui sits on none of the six Len5 watchlists; here it is only a buyer. With affiliates, the two own about 72.6% of Penske Automotive.

The verdict: by the numbers, $212 is a full price, paid for a profit that has shrunk three years running. The one case against it is the case Roger Penske made himself in July: a truck recovery the buyers will own and the public will not.

The buyers offered $210 on July 22. The stock closed above that for two months, then slid as dealer stocks fell. On Wednesday it closed at $194.79, 40 cents under July 21, the last close before any offer. Read through the prices, the market had stopped believing in a deal. The signed price is $2 above July's offer.

A rival with no offer on the table:

AutoNation (AN) at $159.80, +$6.61 / +4.31% on Thursday.

From July 21's close to Thursday's (arithmetic):
- AutoNation: -19.5%.
- Penske Automotive: +8.6%.

Price against the past year's profit (arithmetic):
- Penske Automotive, at $212: about 15 times.
- AutoNation: about 7 times.

The offer, not the business, held Penske Automotive up while its big rival fell. AutoNation fits none of the six Len5es; the nearest, Deep-Value & Special-Situations, counts value only after debt, and a low multiple of one year's profit does not earn a seat by itself.

The case against $212 lives in trucks. "I am encouraged with the trends we are experiencing across the commercial truck market from an improved freight environment," Roger Penske said on July 29. North American orders for the heaviest trucks more than doubled in the first half, by the industry count Penske Automotive cited, and its truck-leasing stake earned it $98.5M, +14%. Whatever that upswing is worth past $212 goes to the buyers.

The deal still needs a vote the buyers cannot cast. Their 72.6% is pledged, but approval also needs a majority of the votes cast by shareholders with no tie to them, who own the other 27.4%. Those holders would receive about $3.8B in cash (arithmetic). The headline $16.3B values the whole company, debt included.

How Penske Automotive reads through each Len5:

- Growth: PARTIAL, #6 of 30. This Len5 hunts years of profit growth at a price that does not assume more. The long record looks like the half that fits: profit per share more than doubled from 2020 to 2025, to $14.13. The recent direction looks like the half that does not. It peaked at $18.55 in 2022, fell every year since, and slipped again in the first half of 2026, $7.52 vs $7.89. What would knock it off the Growth Len5: the deal closing, which ends public trading; before that, another profit drop on October 28 would thin the fit further.

- Momentum: NOT A FIT. This Len5 hunts stocks climbing to new highs. It is 6.6% under its July 29 high of $227 (arithmetic), and a stock tied to a cash offer has nowhere to climb. What would put it on the Momentum Len5: a rival bid above $212, and the owners of 72.6% have agreed to vote against any.

- Quality-Value: NOT A FIT. This Len5 wants a durable business at a discount. The durable half has support: dealerships in seven countries, the truck-leasing stake, and a dividend raised again on Thursday. At about 15 times profit, the discount is missing. What would put it on the Quality-Value Len5: the deal failing and the price falling well under $212 with truck leasing still growing.

- Deep-Value & Special-Situations: NOT A FIT. This Len5 hunts a sound business priced below a cautious value, or a dated event that could unlock one. A signed cash deal is that kind of event, but Thursday's close left no gap between the share price and the $212 the deal pays. What would put it on the Deep-Value & Special-Situations Len5: the price sliding well under $212 while the vote and the regulators stay on track.

- Hypergrowth: NOT A FIT. This Len5 hunts very fast growth at real scale. June-quarter revenue, the money coming in the door, rose 6% to $8.51B. What would put it on the Hypergrowth Len5: growth many times that pace.

- Income: NOT A FIT. This Len5 hunts cash returns a business can keep paying. It can pay: the new $1.46 quarterly dividend is about 2.75% a year at $212 (arithmetic), and in July the company put its payout at 41% of profit. But the deal caps each raise at 2 cents a quarter, and public holders' payments end at closing. The only route onto the Income Len5: the deal falling apart.

What comes next:

- Wednesday, October 28, before the open: July-September results, with no call.
- Friday, November 13: shareholders of record that day get the $1.46 dividend, paid December 1.
- The vote of unaffiliated shareholders: no date set yet.
- First quarter of 2027: expected close. The deadline is October 15, 2027, and the buyers owe $488M if they fail to close.

The key risk: the deal failing at the vote or with regulators. Wednesday's $194.79 shows where the market put Penske Automotive when it doubted the deal.

Penske Automotive's public owners are being offered 15 times a falling profit, and the two buyers are the ones betting it rises again.

text:
$TSLA 

The next-generation Tesla Roadster, revealed in October 2026 at a SpaceX facility event in Texas, is an extreme electric supercar developed with SpaceX collaboration. It emphasises unprecedented performance through active aerodynamics, a multi-mode suction/fan system, and cold-gas thrusters, going beyond conventional tire grip limits. Production is targeted for 2028 at Giga Texas.
It is offered in three configurations (Thrust and Rocket are treated as augments on the base car):
•Performance (by reservation): Road-ready, 2 seats. Features active aerodynamics and multi-mode suction system for high downforce. 0-60 mph under 1.6 seconds.
•Thrust (limited release): Race-ready, 2 seats. Adds rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters. 0-60 mph under 0.9 seconds.
•Rocket (invite-only): Air-ready, 1 seat. Adds perimeter-mounted thrusters for lift, forward thrust, and rotational control. 0-60 mph under 0.59 seconds and top speed over 230 mph. Explicitly noted as not approved for public road use; “So…yes, it can fly.”
Shared performance and technical features across trims include more than 300 miles of range and top speeds exceeding 230 mph. The multi-mode fan and ground-sealing system generates extreme downforce (reportedly up to ~2G), sufficient to hold the car upside down even when stationary, enabling demonstrated inverted driving and hard cornering. Cold-gas thrusters (SpaceX-derived, using compressed gas stored in carbon-fiber overwrapped pressure vessels/COPVs that can be recharged while driving) provide additional force—claimed to be 4–5x what tires alone can deliver—for acceleration, short hops/flights, and stabilisation. Active wings, steer-by-wire (with a yoke), and Track Mode that lowers the car further enhance handling. Lightweight materials such as magnesium, titanium, and carbon fibre are used.
Design and interior: Angular, technical styling with concealed headlights, a full-length taillight, and flush surfaces. Ano White paint draws from aerospace coatings (with UV, cryogenic, and corrosion resistance). Gold-tinted glass mimics spacesuit visors. Interior is Ultrawhite with grey microsuede, a central touchscreen, and smaller forward displays.

Demos at the reveal showed sub-1-second 0-60 runs (around 0.81 seconds in testing), inverted ramp driving, short flights/hovers, and jumps over other Tesla vehicles. Musk has described it as “the best of the last of the human-driven cars” and a halo product rather than a major volume or revenue driver; he has also noted it is not safety-optimised. Reservations are open (around $50,000 for Performance; higher for Thrust).
Note that some earlier 2017 concept targets (e.g., 620-mile range, 4 seats, >250 mph) have been superseded by these updated figures.

"CNN’s September 28, 2026 press release announced the “CNN & Jubilee Town Hall with James Talarico,” moderated by CNN anchor Erin Burnett. The release stated that the event would air live on CNN, stream for CNN’s All Access and pay-TV subscribers, remain available on demand across CNN’s platforms and cable operator platforms, and be made available on Jubilee’s YouTube channel after the live broadcast.

The same day, Axios reported that Jubilee provided input on the event’s format, including interactions between Talarico and voters designed to appeal to younger audiences, and that CNN stated voters would have opportunities for one-on-one interactions with the candidate. Axios reported a planned in-person audience of about 60 Texas voters and that both CNN and Jubilee would distribute clips on social media. A CNN spokesperson told Axios that the partnership would help set the stage for CNN’s next generation of tentpole live events, which Axios described as a growth lever for CNN’s new subscription product.

The event was a commercial product. CNN used it to drive subscriptions, viewership, and advertising. Jubilee used it to drive YouTube viewership and audience growth on a channel it monetizes.

On October 14, 2026, on CNN’s Inside Politics, CNN correspondent Jeff Zeleny told viewers from the Fort Worth venue... “a very different part of tonight’s town hall is a segment called, change my mind. James Talarico is going to be sitting directly across from undecided and other voters, just a few feet across from them and engaging in a dialog and trying to persuade those voters.”

The same day, on CNN News Central, Zeleny again promoted “a change my mind segment” and told viewers that voters “literally will be sitting right across from James Talarico.”

The same day, on CNN’s The Arena, CNN told viewers that “the idea is called change my mind,” that Talarico intended to persuade the undecided voters in the room and a larger audience, and that the question was whether he could “win over enough undecided voters and some independents and Republican voters to come to his side.”

Upon information and belief, CNN referred to the segment as “Change My Mind” at least ten times in its coverage leading up to the broadcast. In every instance, CNN used CHANGE MY MIND as the name of its own segment.

Upon information and belief, during the broadcast Defendants displayed a large sign reading “Change My Mind” behind Talarico as he debated voters. Press accounts of the broadcast reported the sign.

The segment reproduced the core presentation of Plaintiff’s series... a challenger seated directly across from the featured figure, a few feet away, tasked with changing his mind on contested political issues, under the words CHANGE MY MIND.

Within a day of the broadcast, press accounts referred to the town hall itself by Plaintiff’s mark, describing it as titled “Change My Mind.” Defendants’ branding succeeded in attaching Plaintiff’s mark to Defendants’ event.

Defendants distributed, and upon information and belief continue to distribute, the segment and clips of it through CNN’s television network, CNN(.)com, CNN’s applications, on-demand platforms, YouTube, and social media."

CNN is one of the largest news organizations in the world. Jubilee is a professional media company whose business is political debate video. Both maintain legal and clearance resources and both understand trademark rights in program titles.

Plaintiff’s mark has been on the Principal Register since January 14, 2020. Under 15 U.S.C. § 1072, that registration gave Defendants constructive notice of Plaintiff’s claim of ownership.

Defendants also had actual knowledge. CHANGE MY MIND is among the most recognized phrases in American political video. CNN covers political media for a living, and Jubilee competes for the same audience of viewers who watch political debate content online. Upon information and belief, Defendants knew that CHANGE MY MIND identified Plaintiff’s series when they chose it.

Defendants chose the identical mark anyway. They repeated it on air, upon information and belief placed it on the set, and paired it with a debate presentation that mirrors Plaintiff’s series. They sought no license, gave no attribution, and offered no disclaimer. Upon information and belief, Defendants selected the mark deliberately to capture the recognition and goodwill Plaintiff built.

On October 15, 2026, Crowder publicly objected to Defendants’ use, invoked Plaintiff’s registration, and announced legal action. Every distribution of the segment under Plaintiff’s mark after that objection is knowing and deliberate."

text:
One of Sabinal’s biggest and sometimes overlooked industries is actually located outside our city limits, but within Sabinal’s surrounding extraterritorial jurisdiction.

Ranching has been part of our community’s history and heritage for generations. From cattle operations and livestock production to hunting, wildlife management, land conservation, and recreational ranches, this industry plays an important role in our local economy.

What many people may not realize is just how much ranching contributes to the City of Sabinal, even when these properties aren’t located within our city limits.

Our ranches attract hunters, business owners, investors, outdoor enthusiasts, families looking for a weekend getaway, retirees, and folks simply wanting to escape the hustle and bustle of city life and enjoy the peace and beauty of rural Texas.

Those same visitors bring economic opportunities right into Sabinal

They stop at our restaurants, fill up at our gas stations, shop at our local boutiques and businesses, purchase groceries and supplies, and support the hardworking people who call Sabinal home. That spending helps keep our businesses open, supports local, and generates sales tax revenue that can be reinvested into our community.

Recently, Regina and I had the pleasure of touring the newly established LL Ranch, located just five minutes outside of Sabinal! We enjoyed seeing the beautiful Sabinal River, taking in the scenery, learning more about the property, and even getting in a little target practice with my AR-15 and a Magnum revolver! It was a great afternoon enjoying some of the things that make this part of Texas so special.

As Mayor, I believe we need to recognize the tremendous economic opportunities that exist all across Sabinal and our ETJ.

We should be looking at ways to strengthen our relationship with ranch owners, hunting operations, landowners, and the many visitors they bring to our area. That includes encouraging new restaurants, lodging accommodations, retail stores, outdoor recreation businesses, sporting goods stores, and other small businesses that give visitors more reasons to stop, shop, eat, and spend their money right here in Sabinal.

Imagine more hunters stopping for breakfast before heading out to the ranch, families spending an afternoon shopping downtown, or visitors staying overnight and enjoying everything our community has to offer. Those are opportunities that help Sabinal thrive.

Economic development isn’t always about bringing in a massive corporation or factory. Sometimes it’s about recognizing the resources and industries we already have, supporting them, and finding ways to build and expand upon their success.

A stronger ranching community can mean a stronger Sabinal economy. More visitors, more customers for our small businesses, more opportunities for entrepreneurs, and additional sales tax revenue to help fund improvements to our streets, parks, infrastructure, and public services.

I’m proud of our ranching heritage, and I want Sabinal to be a community that welcomes and supports the ranchers, landowners, entrepreneurs, and visitors who contribute so much to our area.

Thank you to Dr. Doug at LL Ranch for welcoming Regina and I today and for investing in the Sabinal area!

Let’s continue supporting our ranches, shopping local, encouraging new businesses, and working together to make Sabinal a place where our traditions and economic growth go hand in hand! 🇺🇸

text:
In Feb 1959, a 37 year old American boarded an Air India flight out of Prague, headed for Calcutta. And in Calcutta, P.C. Mahalanobis had a job waiting at the Indian Statistical Institute. 

Two intelligence agencies believed he was a spy. The problem was, they were on opposite sides: the FBI thought he spied for the communists, and communist Czechoslovakia thought he spied for America.

Morton Nadler had joined the US Communist Party in 1936, lost a radio engineer's job in Chicago over his politics, and in 1948 told his parents he was leaving for a PhD in Paris. 

He went to Prague instead. In 1950 the American embassy seized his passport, accusing him of betraying radar secrets and "inventing weapons for a potential enemy". 

Furious, he gave up his American citizenship and went to work at Czechoslovakia's top computer institute.

Then came Oct 1956. Soviet tanks crushed the Hungarian uprising, and Nadler wanted out. 

Prague refused: he knew too much...

Washington refused him a visa: he might be a spy. He was a de facto prisoner.....

Czechoslovakia finally set one condition for his exit: he 1st had to finish designing a machine called NUDA. He finished it. 

His design was later presented at an international conference, he wrote, "down to the last detail, without my name even once appearing."

The escape route came from Calcutta. P.C. Mahalanobis of the Indian Statistical Institute offered him a job. 

Prague could not object to India, a Soviet friend. 

America could tolerate India, a non-aligned democracy. 

During a refuelling stop in Greece, Nadler thought of walking up to a counter and declaring himself an escaped American. Fear for those who had vouched for him in Prague kept him in his seat.

He landed in Calcutta and joined ISI, then home to India's only two electronic computers, on a two-year contract. 

That December, the world's leading computing journal carried his paper on East European computer research, bylined "Indian Statistical Institute, Calcutta". He stayed 15 months.

From Calcutta he went to Paris. In 1960 he joined the computer company Bull as OCR product line engineering manager, and stayed until 1972. He later became a prof. at Virginia Tech, working on reading machines for the blind. 

By the end he had about 200 publications and 40 patents. He died in 2013, aged 92.

India gave him the first safe job he had had in 10 years.

Sources: Nadler's papers in Communications of the ACM (1959).Virginia Tech ECE obituary (archived); VUMS Czech veterans' site.

3. Yarrow (Achillea millefolium)

Yarrow does not resolve grief. Its medicine, in this framing, is closer to the teaching embedded in the Achilles story: the possibility of remaining in honest relationship with a wound that does not fully close. 

For Grief, Deep Sorrow, and the Processing of Wounds. A Plant of Boundaries, Protection, and the Wounded Healer. 

The Latin name of yarrow, Achillea millefolium (many leaves) is a reference to the Greek Achilles and the primary source of yarrow’s association with the wounded-healer archetype. 

One variant of the story says that his mother dipped him in a bath of yarrow (holding him by the heel) to make him impossible to wound. The unwashed heel became the site of his eventual fatal downfall. Chiron, the wise centaur and teacher of healing who carried an incurable wound of his own, is said to have taught Achilles to use Yarrow for treating and healing  wounds on the battlefields of Troy.

The wounded healer is someone who remains in relationship with their own injury or loss and, from that place, can offer presence or service to others. 

Spiritually, this plant is often described as supporting the ability to face deep pain or sorrow inside oneself without being permanently opened or dissolved by it. 

I myself have found this plant in graveyards and at the cracks of deep loss. It seems to know where closure is needed.  

As you can tell by now, yarrow’s most enduring reputation is as an herb that heals wounds, both physical and otherwise. 

It is a powerful herbal styptic: a plant that stops bleeding. Trust me when I say how tremendously effective yarrow is at stopping bleeding. (So much so that it was the primary first-aid remedy during WW1). 

Physically, we have a classic vulnerary and styptic: capable of sealing wounds and supporting tissue repair. It is astringent (tissue tightening and toning), mildly bitter, aromatic, and has a reputation for regulating flow internally (it can both reduce excessive bleeding and support healthy circulation or menstrual flow depending on the context). 

These same qualities shows up in how people have worked with it emotionally: the sense of being cut open by loss, the leaking of vitality or presence that can accompany profound grief, or the difficulty of containing sorrow without either collapsing into it or numbing it off entirely. Grief or old pain can leave someone feeling too open, too porous, or like waters that are bleeding through, not knowing where one starts and ends. 

Some herbalists describe it as useful for “staunching a bleeding heart,” not by shutting feeling down, but by helping the system regain enough tone and boundary to process the pain without being completely overwhelmed by it. (I’m a big proponent of decided on, intentional, and contained times to process difficult emotion. Like releasing the pressure from a pressure looking, you can work in bits if the emotion is too big to hold.)

Grief is itself a threshold experience: the old shape of a relationship or a life has ended, and the new shape has not yet fully arrived. A plant long linked to both wound-sealing and the marking of endings can serve as a companion for that in-between space.

Plants generally with strong boundary actions on the body like skin, mucous membranes, tissues and blood vessels - frequently show corresponding energetic uses for emotional and psychic boundaries. Yarrow is one of the clearest examples of this. 

It can facilitate the distinction between “what is mine and what is not.” Classic enmeshment scenarios.

Researchers found a further  31 previously unknown Arctic petroglyphs in Russia.

The Pegtymel Petroglyphs are an extraordinarily remote, 2,000-year-old archaeological site located along the Pegtymel River in northwestern Chukotka, Russia (the border region to Alaska).

Discovered by Soviet geologists in the mid-1960s, they are celebrated as the only known prehistoric rock art complex located above the Arctic Circle in Russia.

Etched into dark rock surfaces using quartz lines and metal tools, the petroglyphs offer a vital look into ancient Arctic survival and spiritual life. They include:

Hunting & Wildlife: 
Explicit scenes depicting people tracking reindeer, hunting whales and seals from boats, and using dogs to corner bears.

The "Fly Agaric" People: 
The most famous motifs feature ritualistic anthropomorphic figures with massive, mushroom-shaped heads. These are widely believed by archaeologists to represent shamans or ritual dancers performing ceremonies tied to the hallucinogenic Amanita muscaria (fly agaric) mushroom.

THE EVIDENCE™

FREE-FORM THURSDAY | OCTOBER 15, 2026
THE GREAT SPORTS JOURNALISM EMBARRASSMENT

When Getting Paid to Have an Opinion Replaced Doing the Work to Support It

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

There was a time when readers could expect a writer paid to cover professional football to understand the game, know the personnel, and defend an opinion with more than a provocative headline. Coaches and general managers misjudge players despite having information the public never sees, so nobody expects perfection. But a professional sportswriter should at least investigate the questions that determine whether a recommendation holds up.

The latest exhibit is Duncan Day's October 15 Heavy article, “Seahawks Urged to Trade for $52.5 Million Pro Bowl WR,” which builds on Matt Legros's October 14 Seahawks Wire proposal that Seattle consider acquiring Cleveland Browns receiver Jerry Jeudy as a complement to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, potentially for a mid-to-late-round draft choice.

The proposal raises several questions that should have been examined before publication. Who would Jeudy replace? What does he offer that Seattle does not already possess? What would the transaction cost? And which of Seattle's offensive deficiencies would he address?

The larger indictment is not that one writer likes one trade. It is that the recommendation remains unconvincing because essential personnel questions are left unanswered, while an increasingly crowded sports-media marketplace continues producing articles built around similar hypothetical transactions.

EXHIBIT ONE — WHEN 81 YARDS BECOMES THE SOLUTION TO A RECEIVING PROBLEM

Through five games in 2026, Jeudy has caught eight of 15 targets for 81 yards without a touchdown. He finished 2025 with 50 receptions for 602 yards and two touchdowns, following his 2024 Pro Bowl season of 90 receptions, 1,229 yards, and four touchdowns.

That represents a significant decline, although Cleveland's offensive circumstances and Jeudy's reduced playing time require consideration. He has participated in approximately 58 percent of Cleveland's offensive snaps this season, with his share falling to about 38 percent against Pittsburgh. Fewer opportunities can certainly produce fewer receptions.

But consider the reasoning behind Seattle's alleged need.

Cooper Kupp has 11 receptions for 129 yards on 15 targets, while Rashid Shaheed has nine receptions for 96 yards on 19 targets. Those numbers are offered as evidence that Seattle should acquire another receiver.

Jeudy has fewer receiving yards than either player, yet his acquisition is presented as a potential solution because he made the Pro Bowl two years ago.

Why should Seattle's receivers be evaluated primarily by their first five games while Jeudy receives the benefit of his strongest season from 2024?

If historical accomplishments are the standard, perhaps someone should remind the writers that Kupp won the receiving Triple Crown and Super Bowl MVP award following the 2021 season.

Of course, past accomplishments do not establish current effectiveness. That principle applies equally to Kupp and Jeudy.

There may be evidence on Jeudy's current film that supports a revival under different circumstances. There may also be evidence that Seattle's receivers are struggling because of their assignments, the quarterback's decisions, or the offense's limited opportunities to distribute the football.

A responsible analysis would examine those possibilities before recommending a personnel change.

The published case acknowledges Jeudy's diminished production but does not establish why he would outperform the players Seattle already employs.

EXHIBIT TWO — PERHAPS SEATTLE SHOULD RELEASE JSN

Jaxon Smith-Njigba dropped a third-down pass on Seattle's final possession against San Francisco. Perhaps the Seahawks should release him.

Absurd, of course, considering that he caught 37 passes for 583 yards and seven touchdowns through five games, including 102 yards and a touchdown against the 49ers.

But the exaggerated suggestion illustrates what happens when individual mistakes or narrow statistical samples become substitutes for comprehensive player evaluation.

Kupp's production has been modest, but his 15 targets suggest limited opportunities. Shaheed has received 19 targets, raising legitimate questions about his efficiency and the offense's ability to exploit his speed. His role as a vertical threat and return specialist also deserves consideration.

A receiver who stretches the field may influence coverage even when he does not catch the ball. A veteran who blocks effectively, recognizes coverage adjustments, or provides reliable route execution can contribute to successful plays without recording a reception.

These are identifiable football responsibilities, not mysterious contributions that escape measurement.

Jeudy's diminished role in Cleveland deserves the same examination. The point is not that Kupp and Shaheed are beyond criticism, but that their performance should be assessed through consistent standards.

Smith-Njigba should not be judged by one dropped pass. Neither should the rest of Seattle's receiving corps be judged without understanding what the offense asks them to do.

EXHIBIT THREE — WHO GETS CUT TO MAKE ROOM?

Perhaps the most elementary question missing from the trade discussion concerns Seattle's roster.

The NFL permits 53 players on the active roster. Unless the Seahawks have an available opening or create one through another transaction, adding Jeudy requires removing someone.

Who loses his job?

Should Schneider release a developing receiver who earned his roster position through training camp? Should Seattle sacrifice a special-teams contributor? Should it reduce depth at another position, potentially exposing the team when injuries occur?

And if Jeudy becomes part of the receiving rotation, whose opportunities diminish? Kupp's? Shaheed's? Tory Horton's?

A reserve receiver may cover kickoffs, block on returns, or execute particular offensive assignments. If Seattle releases that player, somebody must take over those responsibilities. If Jeudy replaces an offensive contributor, the front office must establish that the expected improvement justifies reducing the other player's role.

The Seahawks could create a vacancy through a transaction involving another position. That alternative still requires examining the consequences.

A professional football roster is not an unlimited collection of interchangeable players. The addition of one player affects the opportunities, responsibilities, and security of others.

Jeudy might justify those adjustments. The difficulty is that the recommendation provides no persuasive examination of them.

EXHIBIT FOUR — THE CONTRACT IS AFFORDABLE. DOES THAT MAKE THE TRADE WORTHWHILE?

The $52.5 million figure in Heavy's headline refers to Jeudy's original three-year contract extension with Cleveland. It is not the amount Seattle would assume in a trade.

This distinction is important because the financial terms may actually favor the acquiring team.

Most of Jeudy's 2026 compensation was structured through an option bonus already paid by Cleveland. According to A to Z Sports' October 12 analysis, an acquiring club would be responsible for only the remaining portion of his $1.5 million base salary.

His approximately $22.9 million in scheduled 2027 compensation is not guaranteed, providing the acquiring team an opportunity to evaluate whether retaining him would justify the expense. Published 2027 cap figures differ because scheduled compensation and salary-cap accounting are not interchangeable.

Those terms make Jeudy a financially plausible acquisition. Ignoring them would be as misleading as presenting the entire $52.5 million extension as Seattle's prospective expense.

But favorable contract terms do not establish that the transaction improves the team.

Cleveland reportedly seeks compensation around the third- or fourth-round range, while Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox projected a conditional 2027 fifth-round selection. Heavy previously published a separate Washington proposal involving Jeudy and a 2027 fifth-rounder.

Seattle would still surrender draft capital, occupy a roster position, and allocate playing time to Jeudy. Those are costs even when the remaining salary is manageable.

A draft selection also represents an opportunity to acquire a younger player under a cost-controlled contract or facilitate another transaction. Schneider must weigh those alternatives against Jeudy's anticipated contribution.

The relevant question is not whether Jeudy can be acquired cheaply.

It is whether Seattle would receive more football value than it surrenders.

EXHIBIT FIVE — THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR ANOTHER RECEIVER

There is evidence supporting the concern that Seattle needs greater production from its receiving personnel, and ignoring it would repeat the selective reasoning being criticized.

In an October 8 Sports Illustrated analysis, Brendon Nelson examined Seattle's performance through its first four games under offensive coordinator Brian Fleury.

The findings were troubling.

Seattle used heavier formations featuring fewer wide receivers on approximately 62 percent of its plays. From those formations, the Seahawks generated positive offensive efficiency, including a 52.7 percent success rate.

With three or more wide receivers on the field, however, the success rate fell to 38.2 percent. Expected points added per play dropped into negative territory.

The problems with lighter formations also help explain Seattle's third-down difficulties. The Seahawks have converted approximately 31 percent of their third downs through five games, ranking 31st in the league.

That is meaningful evidence that the passing offense needs improvement.

But what is causing the breakdown?

Are Seattle's secondary receivers failing to separate? Are protection failures disrupting route development? Is Darnold struggling to identify blitzes or deliver the football before defenders reach him? Is Fleury relying on predictable formations that make defensive assignments easier?

Adding another receiver might improve three-receiver formations if the existing personnel cannot execute the required routes. But replacing one of those players without first identifying the cause of the inefficiency risks exchanging personnel without correcting the problem.

Nelson's analysis identifies improving the offense's response to blitzes as a priority. That is a specific football issue involving protection, quarterback decisions, route adjustments, and play design.

Before recommending Jeudy, the writer should establish whether he is demonstrably better suited to those assignments than Seattle's current receivers.

Otherwise, the trade addresses a statistical symptom without establishing that it remedies the underlying cause.

EXHIBIT SIX — THE PROBLEMS THAT COST SEATTLE THE SAN FRANCISCO GAME

Seattle's 32-29 loss to San Francisco on October 11 provides an additional examination of the offense's deficiencies.

The Seahawks committed four turnovers, including two Darnold interceptions and fumbles by running backs George Holani and Emanuel Wilson. San Francisco converted those mistakes into 21 points.

Seattle also surrendered five sacks, despite the 49ers playing without Nick Bosa.

Those breakdowns were consequential. They surrendered scoring opportunities, created favorable field position for the opponent, and forced Seattle to overcome disadvantages of its own making.

Jeudy could conceivably improve the passing attack, but acquiring him would not independently correct failures in ball security, blocking assignments, or quarterback decision-making.

A front office considering a trade must prioritize the problems most directly affecting winning and losing.

This does not establish that Seattle should never acquire another receiver. It establishes that a recommendation should compare the projected improvement from that acquisition with what might be accomplished through other personnel moves, coaching adjustments, or changes in offensive execution.

The distinction is essential when every transaction consumes resources that cannot be used elsewhere.

EXHIBIT SEVEN — WHEN ONE TRADE PROPOSAL BECOMES ANOTHER HEADLINE

The larger sports-media problem becomes more apparent when examining how frequently Jeudy has appeared in similar proposals.

On May 6, Heavy published “Commanders Trade Pitch Lands $52.5 Million Pro Bowl WR,” written by Tony Adame and describing a proposal from Max Dible to send Jeudy to Washington for a 2027 fifth-round pick.

On October 15, Heavy published “Seahawks Urged to Trade for $52.5 Million Pro Bowl WR,” identifying another team as a potential destination for the same Cleveland receiver.

Other coverage has floated Jeudy as a possibility for the Eagles, Chiefs, and Rams.

Different teams can have legitimate interest in the same available player. These articles do not prove that anyone copied another writer's work or that their authors neglected research.

But the pattern illustrates how easily an available player can generate a series of stories connecting him to different franchises. The names change, the hypothetical destinations change, and the headlines remain remarkably familiar.

The question is how much independent personnel evaluation accompanies each new proposal.

One publication suggests a trade. Another reports the suggestion. Additional outlets compare proposed compensation or offer different destinations. As the number of articles increases, readers can encounter the same hypothetical transaction repeatedly without receiving much additional evidence that any particular team is pursuing the player.

The appearance of a developing story should not be confused with confirmation that a transaction is being negotiated.

And the repetition of an argument does not improve the quality of its supporting evidence.

EXHIBIT EIGHT — WHAT PROFESSIONAL ANALYSIS SHOULD LOOK LIKE

There are examples of more substantive work on this very subject.

Wendell Ferreira's October 12 article for A to Z Sports examined five potential solutions to Seattle's receiving difficulties, including Jeudy. His discussion distinguished the player's contract obligations from the extension's headline value, considered Cleveland's decision to emphasize younger receivers, and compared multiple alternatives.

That does not mean his conclusions must be accepted. It means the article provided information that allows the reader to evaluate the proposition.

Likewise, Nelson's examination of Seattle's offensive formations supplied evidence about where the Seahawks have struggled and offered a possible explanation involving their response to defensive blitzes.

That is the work readers should expect from sports analysis.

Professional football is too complicated to evaluate through isolated receiving totals and remembered accolades. Personnel decisions involve the interaction of contracts, coaching systems, blocking assignments, defensive tendencies, player development, and roster constraints.

A knowledgeable writer can disagree with a general manager and still make an excellent argument. A speculative proposal can identify an opportunity the front office has overlooked.

But the argument must withstand examination.

Sports journalism should not become an endless succession of hypothetical transactions whose primary distinction is the franchise named in the headline.

Readers deserve enough evidence to determine whether an idea has merit.

THE VERDICT — DO THE WORK BEFORE WRITING THE ARTICLE

The Jerry Jeudy proposal may ultimately prove worthwhile. His contract could make him an inexpensive short-term acquisition, and his earlier production demonstrates that he has performed at a high NFL level.

But before recommending that the defending Super Bowl champions surrender assets to acquire him, the argument should address six fundamental questions.

What deficiency does Jeudy correct? What current evidence demonstrates that he would improve Seattle's offense? What does the complete transaction cost? Who loses a roster spot or playing time? What alternatives are available? And why is Jeudy the preferable investment?

Those questions distinguish an informed personnel recommendation from a hypothetical transaction built around a recognizable name.

The problem is not that sportswriters occasionally reach the wrong conclusions. Football evaluation is uncertain, and legitimate disagreements are inevitable.

The problem is that too much published commentary appears willing to present a recommendation without sufficiently investigating the facts necessary to support it.

Journalism is a profession, and professional compensation should carry professional expectations. That means researching the circumstances, examining competing explanations, acknowledging contradictory evidence, and showing readers how the conclusion was reached.

If a proposed trade cannot withstand the elementary questions any competent general manager would ask, perhaps the article advocating it should not have been published in its present form.

The reader should not have to perform the analysis the writer was paid to provide.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

SOVEREIGN INDIAN TRIBES FIRST, EVERYONE ELSE LAST

Washington tribes get boost from state arts and culture grant program

The Quileute Tribal School has taught language and cultural preservation in La Push, Clallam County, since the 1930s. The school’s newer, larger building is at a higher ground location a few miles up the road. 

James Jaime, cultural director of the Quileute Tribe, leads the Quileute Language Revitalization team from his office at the Quileute Tribal Administration building in La Push, Clallam County. 

Oct. 15, 2026

Some consider Quileute an extinct language. James Jaime says it’s “just sleeping.”

As cultural director of the Quileute Tribe on the western coast of the Olympic Peninsula, Jaime leads a small but passionate team trying to wake up the language of his ancestors. Part of that effort is adding about 4,000 words to the Quileute (kʷòʔlí·yot̓ísk̓ʷa) dictionary, an undertaking made possible by Tribal Cultural Affairs, a Washington State program that provides grants for tribal arts and culture projects. 

The Washington State Arts Commission, known as ArtsWA, launched Tribal Cultural Affairs with $1.7 million in legislative funding in 2023. Three years later, ArtsWA says it remains the only state-led program in the nation that offers grants and other resources to support cultural preservation and pathways into the creative economy for tribes. This year, the program completed its strongest grant cycle yet: All 29 of Washington’s federally recognized tribes applied and collectively received $551,000, or $19,000 each. 

The money has supported dozens of projects, from weaving classes to ethnobotany books to museum planning. This grant cycle, 18 projects focus on cultural classes or workshops, three include large community ceremonies and two involve cultural space development. The Tulalip Tribes have used grant money for their youth-focused Lushootseed learning app, the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation have put money toward Camp Chaparral, and the Muckleshoot Indian Tribe has partnered with Cannonball Arts Center in downtown Seattle to showcase canoes and other cultural works. 

All projects incorporate some language learning and preservation, which TCA Founding Manager Cheryl Wilcox and other program leaders said helps restore and reclaim “a layer of culture, identity and history that was lost or taken.” The Quileute Tribe has received money from all grant cycles so far for a total of about $83,000, and is one of four tribes using the money primarily on language preservation and revival. 

“This project is so much more than a dictionary,” Jaime said. “People want to feel whole. Language is a way for them to get to a place of wholeness.”

Reclaiming what was lost

On the Quileute Indian Reservation in La Push — home to about half of the tribe’s 850 or so members — few people speak Quileute. Jaime is hoping his team’s project will eventually change that. He’s continuing the work of his late grandfather, Fred Woodruff Sr., and other Quileute elders who in the late 1960s began working with linguistic anthropologist Jay Powell to preserve and teach the Quileute language through a written alphabet, several books, thousands of audio recordings and an ever-evolving dictionary. 

“I know that we're going to have Quileute speakers once again,” Jaime said. “Maybe not fluency, but certainly some proficiency, and that's our goal.”

Quileute is an isolate language, the last standing member of the small Chimakuan language family spoken historically along the western coast of the Olympic Peninsula. Once, hundreds of people spoke Quileute.

🔴| Vultures feed only on the dead, but these monsters prey on the living: Syrian tribes pledge allegiance to the Saudi royal family, betraying Syria, Yemen, and the entire Muslim world.

October 16, 2026 | Damascus / Riyadh

Standing before the camera, Sheikh Muhammad Saleh Al-Marshid representing the so-called "Syrian tribes" and the "Akidat Qahtani tribe," pledged allegiance to Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. He declared "unconditional support for Saudi Arabia in its confrontation with the Houthi forces."

This is not a statement from the tribes. It is an act of betrayal.

💥 To whom are they pledging their allegiance?

What kind of regime is this Saudi Arabia to which they have pledged their loyalty?

For twelve years, Saudi Arabia has been bombing Yemen. It has struck hospitals, schools, marketplaces, weddings, funerals, and water treatment plants. It has imposed a blockade that has left millions to starve. It has killed hundreds of thousands of Yemenis. It has reduced Yemen to ruins and then labeled this "deterrence."

Saudi Arabia has purchased Israeli spyware to track and suppress its own dissidents. It has signed arms development agreements with Israel and opened its airspace to Israeli aircraft. Its F-15 fighter jets are equipped with Israeli-made combat helmets supplied because the United States refused to provide them. It coordinates its air defense with CENTCOM, the very entity that simultaneously arms Israel.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman ordered the dismemberment of journalist Jamal Khashoggi using a bone saw. He imprisoned hundreds of Saudi princes and businessmen at the Ritz-Carlton, subjecting them to torture and extorting $107 billion from them funds he then used to pay for American weaponry.  A sheikh of a Syrian tribe has pledged allegiance to a certain individual, declaring his "absolute support" for Saudi Arabia in its conflict against Yemen.

This is not support; it is submission. This is not tribal honor, it is tribal disgrace.

🎯 Vultures and Monsters: Whose Appetite Is Greater?

You are right. Vultures feed only on the dead. They circle above a corpse, waiting for death to occur, before swooping down to feast. They do not create corpses; they do not kill the living. They consume only what is already dead.

But these "tribal leaders"? They are not vultures they are hyenas. They do not wait for death; they actively deliver the living to it. They drag the tribes of a nation, a nation currently being swallowed up by Israel into a war that is not their own; a war that serves the interests of Riyadh, Washington, and Tel Aviv.

Syria’s Daraa province has fallen under Israeli occupation. Israel has established military outposts in southern Syria. Israeli tanks have advanced to within 20 kilometers of Damascus. Israeli aircraft have struck Syrian arms depots in over 1,000 separate air raids. The Syrian Golan Heights have been annexed, a move Trump labeled as "Israeli sovereignty."

Yet, this Syrian tribal sheikh says nothing about Daraa. He says nothing about the Golan. He says nothing about Israel’s annexation of southern Syria. Instead, he pledges his loyalty to the Saudi royal family to fight against the people of Yemen.

While his country is being dismembered by Israel, he offers his allegiance to the Saudi monarchy. While his land is being annexed, he vows his support to another American client state.

This is not tribal honor, it is the auctioning off of a tribe.

⚔️ Who Is the True Enemy of the Syrian Tribes?

For the tribes of Syria from the Akidat to the Shammar, from Deir ez-Zor to Al-Hasakah, from As-Suwayda to the Damascus countryside the true enemy is:

◾Israel, which is currently annexing southern Syria.  · The United States occupies Syria’s oil fields and controls its food supply.
◾ Turkiye maintains a military presence in northern Syria.
◾The Julani regime is sending Syrian soldiers to Yemen to serve as cannon fodder in a war waged by Saudi Arabia and Israel.
◾ Saudi Arabia is buying off Syrian tribal leaders, enlisting them to fight on behalf of Riyadh.

Yemen is not Syria’s enemy; it is a mirror of Syria.

Yemen has been under Saudi bombardment for twelve years; Syria has been bombed by Israel. Yemen faces a U.S. blockade; Syria is subjected to U.S. sanctions. Yemenis are killed by the Saudis; Syrians are killed by the Israelis.

Yemenis are Arabs, and so are Syrians. The children of Yemen and the children of Syria share the same blood, endure the same nightmares, and lie buried beneath the same ruins.

Yet, this Syrian tribal sheikh aligning himself with Saudi Arabia treats the Yemeni people as enemies.

📡 Who is he, and whom does he represent?

Sheikh Mohammed Saleh al-Marshid represents the "Aqidat Qahtani" tribe an Arab tribe in eastern Syria, primarily located in the provinces of Deir ez-Zor and al-Hasakah. Throughout the Syrian Civil War, various branches of the Aqidat tribe have maintained complex, shifting relationships with both the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) and the regime. In Deir ez-Zor, factions of the Aqidat tribe have fought against ISIS, collaborated with the regime, and at times joined the opposition.

But this sheikh is not speaking from Deir ez-Zor; he is speaking from Saudi Arabia. He represents a version of "Syrian tribes" purchased by the Saudis, a "tribal leader" handpicked in a Riyadh boardroom, a puppet who has been paid, filmed, and featured across Saudi media.  He represents Saudi Arabia, not the tribes of Syria.

🔻 Conclusion: This is a disgrace to the tribe, not an honor.

In Arab tradition, tribal honor is the highest value. The primary duty of a tribal sheikh is to protect his people, his land, and his dignity. He has no right to send the youth of his tribe to die for foreign interests, all for the sake of money from a foreign patron.

Saudi Arabia is not protecting Syria; it is exploiting Syria.

Saudi Arabia has failed to achieve victory in Yemen in fact, it has been defeated. Its airports have been shut down, its gas facilities bombed, its mercenaries are fleeing, and its officers have been struck by missiles while inside a palace in Aden. Its "Vision 2030" is collapsing.

Now, it turns to the tribes of Syria, begging them to send their young men to die in Yemen and a Syrian tribal sheikh has agreed.

This is not loyalty; it is a transaction.

text:
Today I stepped inside a 600-year-old Catholic chapel. In Milwaukee, Wisconsin.

Built around 1420 in a small French village near Lyon, the chapel was already standing when St. Joan of Arc was fighting to save France.

For centuries, the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass was offered within its walls. Then came the French Revolution, abandonment, and ruin.

In the 1920s, a wealthy American woman devoted to St. Joan purchased the chapel, had it dismantled stone by stone, shipped across the Atlantic, and rebuilt on her Long Island estate.

She also acquired a 13th-century Gothic altar and a stone kissed by St. Joan herself after praying to the Blessed Virgin before battle. That stone now rests behind the altar.
Then, in 1962, disaster struck. A fire ravaged the adjoining French château.

The medieval chapel survived.
It was eventually dismantled AGAIN, loaded onto trucks, and painstakingly reconstructed on the campus of Marquette University, where it stands today.

Six centuries. The Hundred Years' War. The Protestant Reformation. The French Revolution. Two world wars. An ocean crossing. A devastating fire. Two relocations.

And today, the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass is STILL offered within these  ancient walls.

Kings have come and gone. Empires have fallen. The Church remains.
St. Joan of Arc, ora pro nobis. ⚜️
