text:
[EDITORIAL, 16 FEBRUARY 2026]

Imagine traveling across the ocean just to tell the homeowner his house isn’t that big.

That’s how Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan chose to introduce himself to Filipinos.

“One may easily win a confrontation with a smaller neighbor [like the Philippines]… but nobody wants force.”

That’s the reassurance: “We could hit you, but we’re being nice.”

Nothing warms the ears faster than being called “small” by someone currently enjoying your hospitality.

Ambassador, welcome. Truly. We are famously gracious. We offer coffee, beaches, smiles, and even patience, for a limited time.

But let’s clarify something gently. You are a guest. A respected diplomatic guest, but a guest nonetheless.

Driving on our roads. Holding receptions on land protected by Filipino police. Powered by our grid. Served by Filipino staff. Explaining, under our flag, how easy it would be to buy the house.

Here’s a really hospitable suggestion: take a little walk. Step outside the gates. Come see what a “small neighbor” looks like up close. Look people in the eye when you call them small.

You said we’re not talking enough. You said this while talking. In Manila.

Embassy gates open because this country allows them to open. Dialogue is stalled? What are you doing here?

How confident someone can sound when he’s protected by the very sovereignty he’s sizing up.

You can “easily win.” Maybe. Big navy. Big economy. Big everything. Very impressive.

Here’s what’s more impressive: We didn’t sail thousands of kilometers to remind anyone who we are.

We are smaller. We are also the ones who wake up with those seas outside our windows.

You can sail in. Sail out. We can’t sail away from our own coastline. That’s the difference.

If size determined ownership, the Pacific would belong to whoever bought the biggest ship. The richest country would own the planet.

When you keep reminding us how big you are, it starts sounding like you need the reminder more than we do.

First, pressure at sea. Then pressure over our tone. If you can convince a country that speaking firmly is “escalation,” you’ve already reduced it without firing a shot.

Very clever. Almost hypnotic. “We are small. We are calm. We are small. We are calm.”

Suddenly, the conversation isn’t “what happened,” but “Why is Jay Tarriela disrespecting China?”

To the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and to President Xi, if he’s listening: Gentlemen, if this tone is the plan, fine. But if you truly want stability, then send the message like you mean stability. “Nobody wants confrontation.” OK, then send your warships back to China.

Jing Quan would prefer we speak more softly. Smaller. More grateful. But gratitude is for guests. Sovereignty is for hosts. And this, in case there was confusion, is home.

#DAILYTRIBUNE

text:
■30秒彼氏目線動画のプロンプト

Create a 30-second video in 1920×1080, with the realism of an ordinary recording a boyfriend made of his girlfriend during a summer walk in Japan.

The small story:
They have no particular destination. She has just opened a can of fruit juice, and he starts recording without announcing it. Over the next half-minute, she gradually notices the camera, gets a little embarrassed, and begins including him in the moment. Their familiarity should come through in how she waits for him, looks at him, and closes the distance between them.

The woman:
A beautiful Japanese woman around 24 years old, with an approachable, individual face rather than a polished model appearance. Dark brown eyes, natural skin texture, light everyday makeup, and straight black hair loosely gathered in a low ponytail. A few short strands around her temples have escaped in the summer humidity.

She wears a faded navy cotton T-shirt, loose ivory trousers, comfortable gray sneakers, and a small rust-colored crossbody bag. A plain elastic hair tie is around one wrist. Keep her facial features, hair, outfit, bag, and proportions consistent in every shot.

Her expressions are understated and responsive. Sometimes she looks distracted or squints in the light. Her smile develops because of something between them, rather than appearing on cue.

The place:
A residential neighborhood in a regional Japanese city, near a narrow canal. Late afternoon in midsummer, with warm sunlight still reaching the upper parts of the houses.

Use ordinary local details: patched asphalt, short concrete bridges over the canal, metal railings warm from the sun, compact houses with tiled roofs, frosted entrance windows, outdoor air-conditioning units, bicycles tucked beside gates, and plants growing in mismatched pots. Utility wires cross the sky. A striped fabric awning hangs outside a closed shop farther down the street.

Avoid famous landmarks and postcard compositions. The location should feel like somewhere the couple already knows.

How the camera behaves:
The boyfriend holds a small consumer camera at his own eye or chest level. Most of the time he is beside her or only a step behind. The viewpoint should feel like her companion's attention, with no third-person shots of the couple.

Let framing respond to their interaction. When she suddenly looks at him, he may take a fraction of a second to correct the composition. When he laughs, the camera moves slightly. When they walk, his footsteps create a gentle, uneven rhythm.

Use ordinary consumer-camera rendering: restrained detail, modest dynamic range, occasional clipped highlights, a little shadow noise, and slight focus hesitation when she moves closer. Preserve natural skin color.

Keep the camera's attention on her face, gestures, and shared surroundings. Avoid fashion poses, body-scanning shots, elaborate camera moves, slow motion, or a glossy advertising finish.

Suggested edit — six short memories from the same walk:

0:00–0:05
She stands beside a low canal railing with a small, unbranded can of mandarin orange juice. The recording begins just as she finishes lifting the pull tab. She takes a sip, lowers the can, and notices that he is filming.

She looks directly at him with a briefly puzzled expression, then gives a small, amused smile, as though silently asking, “Really, you're filming this?”

Begin with a slightly loose frame that includes her hands and the canal, then let the boyfriend adjust it toward her face.

0:05–0:10
A cut to the two of them walking side by side along the narrow lane. She carries the can naturally in one hand.

She gets half a step ahead, realizes he has slowed down while filming, and turns back. Instead of posing, she waits with a mildly impatient but affectionate look. Once he catches up, she resumes walking beside him.

Her gaze should meet the person holding the camera, not an imaginary audience.

0:10–0:15
They pause near a house entrance where a small glass wind chime hangs beneath the eaves.

A breeze makes it ring. She glances upward and listens for a moment. Loose strands of hair move against her cheek; she brushes them aside with her free hand.

She notices him still watching her through the camera and suppresses a smile before looking back toward the wind chime.

Keep this moment quiet and unhurried.

0:15–0:20
On a short concrete bridge, she stops to look down at the canal. The camera first catches the rippling water, then tilts back toward her after she has already turned around.

She leans slightly toward him to see what he is recording. Her face briefly comes too close for the camera's focus, making her laugh softly and step back.

The laugh should feel like a shared interruption, with a small answering movement from the camera.

0:20–0:25
They rest beside the bridge in the shade. She is closer to the camera now, relaxed enough to stop paying attention to being filmed.

She takes another small sip of juice, then holds the can toward him as an offer. Leave the can clearly visible in the foreground, separate from her face.

He does not take it during the shot. She gives a tiny questioning lift of her eyebrows, then draws it back with an affectionate smile.

0:25–0:30
She steps toward him and gently touches his free forearm, inviting him to keep walking. Only a small, natural part of his arm may enter the lower edge of the frame.

As they start moving together, he lowers the camera. The view drifts from her smiling face to her bag, their moving shadows, and the sunlit pavement.

Let the last second settle on the overlapping shadows of two people walking close together. End with an ordinary recording stop, without a dramatic transition or title.

Sound:
Use the sound that would actually reach the camera microphone: cicadas, the juice can opening, a few footsteps, a wind chime, faint canal water, distant tires on the road, and their quiet laughter.

A single softly spoken Japanese remark such as “撮ってたの？” may occur when she first notices the camera, but speech is optional. Do not add explanatory dialogue.

No music, voiceover, or added dramatic sound effects.

Continuity and physical detail:
There is one juice can, carried by her throughout the sequence. Its color, size, opening, and remaining shape stay consistent. The crossbody strap stays on the same shoulder. Her ponytail remains tied.

Hands should hold objects with believable contact and weight. Walking speed, foot placement, shadows, and reflections must agree with the surroundings. Keep the canal, bridge, houses, sunlight direction, and summer weather coherent between cuts.

Emotional direction:
The viewer should feel that she knows and trusts the person behind the camera. Build that feeling through small changes in distance and attention: noticing him, waiting for him, leaning in, offering a drink, and asking him to walk beside her.

Let ordinary pauses remain. Her beauty is something her boyfriend happens to notice during their time together.

The finished video should feel like a personal memory he would keep because of the way she looked at him that afternoon.

Thank you! My Dad always wanted to live in the west. He worked for Georgia Kaolin Company in middle Georgia almost his entire life. He worked there long enough to be able to get three weeks vacation annually. And he packed up our Volkswagen van every year and took us on a tour. We went out West into Colorado one year. We drove from Georgia to Nova Scotia another year, driving down the St. Lawrence River to end up in Quebec. Another year we drove across the southern US. We saw the White Sands park, where my brother and I slid down the sandunes.

That’s when Dad fell in love with the Davis mountains. He wanted to move there. He was actually talking to real estate agents to see if he could buy property down there. 

Because my Dad took us to all of these places, I have seen more of America than most. And I continued the tradition by becoming part of the GA Tech outdoor program, running rivers across the southeast. 

And when I moved to Dallas and became part of a sailing team, we competed in Washington state, New Orleans, New York, Key West FL, and many other places. 

My Dad started this quest in the 1960’s. I have been to every state except for Hawaii, Alaska, and the Great Lakes states. I drove there, I camped there, and I have seen so much of the beauty our country has to offer.

Thanks for appreciating my Dad.

text:
Yes. Sitting Bull rejected the 1868 Fort Laramie Treaty and later demands that non-reservation Lakota report to agencies. After the 1876 victories at the Rosebud and Little Bighorn, where he served more as a spiritual and political leader than a battlefield commander, he led his band into Canada in 1877 rather than surrender. 

He stayed roughly four years, turning away U.S. offers of pardon and amnesty until the near extinction of the buffalo and resulting starvation forced him back. He surrendered at Fort Buford in July 1881 and said he was the last of his tribe to surrender his rifle.   

By then it was the U.S. though, not colonies.

text:
⚡Funding Brief⚡

Anduril has launched an employee tender offer at $94.80 per share, implying a valuation of roughly $90B, up from $61B in May, when it raised $5B in a round led by Thrive Capital and a16z.

The tender is capped at about $1.3B and is open to current and former employees across 16 countries. It closes November 9.

Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Costa Mesa, California, Anduril was co-founded by Oculus founder Palmer Luckey. Its products, built around its AI software platform Lattice, include drones, counter-drone systems, autonomous underwater vehicles and surveillance towers, serving the US Department of Defense and allied governments. CEO Brian Schimpf has said revenue has passed $1B and continues to roughly double each year. Headcount reached about 8,200 by the end of 2025.

Source: Bloomberg, CNBC

text:
About 80 km from Temple 23, Yakuoji.
After a long journey, you finally arrive at Temple 24, Hotsumisakiji.

Perched high above Cape Muroto, this temple offers spectacular views over the Pacific Ocean.
Nearby are places connected to Kobo Daishi, including Mikurodo Cave, where the young Kukai is said to have trained.

The temple gate is unusual, with four Nio guardian statues on its front and back. Another highlight is the “Bell Stone,” which makes a clear ringing sound when tapped with a small stone.

The coastal route from Yakuoji is a breathtaking journey best experienced on foot.
Leaving Tokushima behind, the pilgrimage now continues into Kochi.
Surrounded by the sea and sky of Muroto, why not take a moment to reflect on your journey so far?

#ShikokuPilgrimage #Zen

text:
Fun but true story 

And fuck anyone who disbelieves. 

I fucked around for couple years after college.  Then worked in asset mgmt at first union while I got mba at night.   Cap markets.   Loan syndications.   Got cfa.   3/3. 

Worked with some amazing people that went on to work at best bank and hedge funds in world in this timeframe.   CDS.   The focus.   

2003-ish I tell my boss hey dude these pollution control revenue bonds that remarked weekly or monthly use a letter of credit.  You have a bank backstop the remarking.   But CDS was inefficient at the time.    For many reasons.   

My boss and I created a CDS backed letter of credit facility.   Cheaper.   

The first one we did was Ohio Edison.   A subsidiary of first energy at the time.    They were paying like 250 bps on a 200 million syndicated LC faculty.   We said we’d take it at 200 bps.   CDs market was at 150 bps.    Found buyers.   

Then txu.   Hahaha I’m a dummy.   Left the group after doing txu deal.   $400 mil pollution control revenue bonds that were remarkably weekly I think.  We saved them 50 bps a year on 400 mil but the catch was if they wanted out earlier than 5yrs there was make whole.   Me and my boss Mike created it all.  

So we offered bilateral lines cheaper. 50 bps for the issuer.    50 bps for us.    Locked in.    By the structure.   +/- 

That started at first union / Wachovia that is now Wells Fargo.    I went to hf before txu lbo happens 

I ofc have friends that were there.   When txu lbo happens they still had my trade on.  400+/- lc facility.    Long CDs meaning short the credit.   Make whole.  LBO  needed to take those bonds out.    Trade paid hundred plus million for the bank.

text:
The $CRWV CDS situation not what you want to see of course but a few points 

- I cut my teeth on CDS circa 2003.  Created first time CDs structures.    Traded a ton.   Billion up cdx ig.   Was Wild West.   Tons of liquidity.   Through Gfc.   Now is not then.    
-Bonds also getting hit but capital structures can be complex.   
- don’t really know crwv but if they have hyperscalers backing on debt from some facilities and not on other debt the cost of capital will of course vary.  
- CDS market is a cheapest to deliver market.    Can deliver the worst bond in capital structure.    Can have secured debt with IG counter parties.   Unsecured debt with guarantors.    Unsecured or jr debt below that.   You can deliver shittiest bond. 
-until the curve flattens then inverts nobody in credit markets believes bankruptcy is imminent.

text:
I Refuse to Call Vampires                    .......            "Civilized"             ........

They speak of civilization. They speak of universal values. They speak of a "rules-based international order." They speak of democracy, freedom, and human rights. They paint their missiles white, package their bombs as "precision strikes," label massacres as "counter-terrorism," rebrand plunder as "development," and call occupation "security."

They claim to be civilized.

Very well, let us define civilization.

💥 The Vampiric Ritual

What is civilization?

It is a system that requires the blood of others consumed every single day, every hour, every minute, every second to sustain its own existence. Without blood, it cannot function. Without corpses, it cannot advance. Without ruins, it cannot build.

This is the very description of United States, Britain, France and Israel.

The United States killed over a million people in Iraq not in the course of war, but through sanctions, blockades, and the systematic destruction of water treatment plants, hospitals, and power grids. When asked whether the deaths of half a million Iraqi children were "worth it," Madeleine Albright replied, "We think the price is worth it." She said those words. She never apologized. Instead, she was promoted.

This is a vampiric ritual. The death of every Iraqi child is tallied as a "price worth paying." The death of every Iraqi child is a dish served at the empire’s table. Without these deaths, the empire’s appetite cannot be sated; without them, its self-assurance cannot be maintained.

This is a ritual that feeds upon children not civilization.

🎯 The Doctrine of Plunder

They claim the West represents the pinnacle of civilization. Let us examine how this pinnacle was constructed.

How much did King Leopold II of Belgium plunder from the Congo? It is estimated that ten million Congolese people were killed during his reign not in battle, but through the severing of limbs, enslavement, and being beaten to death. The reason? Rubber. Europe needed rubber. The Congo had rubber. The Congolese people were simply in the way.

And what did the British do in India?  It is estimated that under British rule, over 100 million Indians perished due to famine, epidemics, and state repression. These were not natural deaths; they were deaths caused by policy. During the Bengal Famine of 1943, Winston Churchill continued to export grain from India, justifying it by claiming that Indians "breed like rabbits." Three million people died and Churchill blamed them for it.

And what did France do in Algeria? According to Algerian records, more than five million people were killed during 132 years of French rule. To this day, the French parliament has issued no formal apology. French President Emmanuel Macron has refused to apologize for the crimes of colonialism, stating: "Colonialism is a part of French history, but it is not France."

This is what they call "civilization."
Plundering resources, they call it civilization.
Massacring people, they call it civilization.
Starving children to death, they call it civilization.

⚔️ Poisoning the Youth

They send the youth to the battlefield and call it patriotism.
They cast the youth into prison and call it justice.
They flood the veins of the youth with opioids and call it medicine.
They fill the minds of the youth with social media and call it connection.

Purdue Pharma marketed OxyContin to American doctors, insisting it was safe. The result? Over a million people died from opioid overdoses. This was no accident; it was a calculated plan. The Sackler family knew the risks of addiction, yet they concealed them and kept on selling. They raked in over $10 billion.

And where are they now? Their names adorn the walls of museums and galleries; their "philanthropic" contributions are etched onto university buildings. They never went to prison. They never offered an apology. Instead, they have been treated with "civility."

This is what they call "civilization."
Poisoning their own people and calling it medicine.
Then, using "charitable" donations to launder their own crimes.

📡 Domination at Home, Plunder Abroad

But that is not all. And it is not the darkest part.

The darkest part is this: they do not only inflict these things upon other nations.  They do the same to their own people.

While the United States bombs the Middle East, it turns its own cities into war zones Skid Row in Los Angeles, the ruins of Baltimore, the despair of Appalachia. They didn’t send bombers to Detroit; instead, they sent factory relocations, deindustrialization, and disinvestment. The ruins of Detroit were not created by bombs; they were the result of abandonment abandonment by those who claim that "the market decides."

In the Iraq War, the United Kingdom used its own soldiers as cannon fodder while simultaneously gutting the National Health Service (NHS). As they carried out bombings in Afghanistan, they drove domestic poverty rates to their highest levels since the Second World War. They use the term "austerity" to mask the plunder of their own people.

This is not a civilization that cares for its own citizens. It is the same ritual of bloodletting—only this time, the blood is drawn from the necks of their own kin.

🕯️Another Kind of Civilization

And then, there is another kind of civilization.

It does not feed on blood. It does not plunder. It does not poison. It does not slaughter. It does not impose blockades or sanctions. It does not bomb hospitals, starve children, dismember journalists, or imprison dissidents. It does not sell arms to despotic regimes, fund genocides, confine refugees in concentration camps, or heat the planet to the brink of destruction.

This civilization exists in the mountains of Yemen. Its people have been under bombardment for twelve years, yet they have not collapsed. They manufacture their own missiles; they build their own drones. They have shot down F-15s and shut down Saudi airports. They have no money, no weaponry, and no international support they have only themselves.

This civilization exists within the ruins of Gaza where 21,976 children have been slaughtered. Yet, they have not ceased to exist. They have not been erased from history. They are still breathing. They are still crying out. They are still resisting.  This kind of civilization exists in the villages of Lebanon. The people there are subjected to daily Israeli bombardment. Yet, their olive trees have not been uprooted; their valleys have not been leveled; their homes have not been destroyed beyond the possibility of reconstruction. They remain standing upon their own land.

This kind of civilization does not feed on the blood of others. It sheds its own blood,, its own, not that of others.

       So, I say: If what you call "civilization" is a system that must consume the blood of others every single day just to survive that is not civilization. That is parasitism.
If what you call "civilization" is a system that must plunder every plot of land, every oil well, and every marketplace to sustain itself that is not civilization. That is predation.
If what you call "civilization" is a system that must poison the youth, starve children, and dismember journalists to protect itself that is not civilization. That is criminality.
If what you call "civilization" is a system that must be maintained through bone saws, missiles, sanctions, and blockades that is not civilization. That is terror.

I refuse to label vampires as "civilization."
I refuse to label ogres as "civilization."
I refuse to label a system that feeds on children as "civilization."

True civilization is found in those who refuse to kneel. It is found in those who remain standing even after twelve years of bombardment. It is found in those who rebuild amidst the ruins, who produce goods despite blockades, and who survive while under siege. It is found in those who though abandoned by the entire world have never abandoned themselves.

Long live the resistance. Long live the Axis of Resistance.

text:
There is no moral case for the Ukraine war. It ended in 2023.

Putin's calculation is that Ukraine will collapse. He can just wait until they run out of men.

Ukraine either believes Russia will collapse, or Zelensky still has political competitors to purge, or both.

My math here is that Ukraine is *very* short manpower. They are likely only being kept afloat by UGVs and a (small) drone capability advantage at the moment.

The drone war is (of course) a two way street. Ukraine seems to have maintained a slight tech edge here, but this edge is at most a month or two. There is no reason to believe that Ukrainian drone teams are more capable than Russian teams. Every edge in this domain (outside of StarShield) is small tech/ergonomic/software advances, and the gaps close quickly regardless of which side opens them.

On the home front, every single man in Ukraine is either in uniform or making weapons. This is a total mobilization. There aren't many examples of nations mobilized this much. Last days of Nazi Germany? Rome after Cannae?

To put into perspective, none of the WWI era nations struggled this hard to conscript. None of the WWII nations struggled this hard to conscript. The Ukrainian men in the weapons industry are pushing 20hr days bc if they drop production a tiny bit they'll be hauled off and sent to the front.

I think a lot of western commentators underappreciate how quickly things can collapse. Germany in WWI never collapsed. It surrendered *the moment* before the western front collapsed. The 'transparent battlefield' existed back then too, and it exists until you cannot sufficiently man 1km of front.

The best deal Ukraine gets is almost certainly going to be the one offered to it today.

Blood, Iron, and Bytes: Technological Democratization as the Catalyst of Systemic Collapse

Traditional scholarship often views the transition from the Bronze Age to the Iron Age as a passive consequence of the Late Bronze Age collapse (circa 1200–1150 BCE). 

In this conventional narrative, the disruption of elite trade networks carrying rare copper and tin forced desperate communities to turn to a less prestigious, locally available alternative: iron. 

However, contemporary historical analysis offers a compelling counter-perspective, suggesting that iron metallurgy was not a mere byproduct of collapse, but an active, long-term decentralizing force. Rather than triggering the initial palace burnings of 1200 BCE, the gradual spread of cheap, ubiquitous iron ore over the subsequent centuries democratized military capability. 

This structural shift doubled political fragmentation and permanently locked in a multi-polar world order by preventing the re-emergence of centralized mega-empires. This ancient systemic restructuring directly mirrors today’s shift from centralized cloud computing monopolies to decentralized, open-source artificial intelligence and edge technologies. 

In both eras, when the barriers to highly disruptive tools fall, the fragmentation of the legacy hierarchy becomes historically inevitable.

The Four Mechanisms of Fragmentation

1. The Democratization of Violence vs. Asymmetric Cyber Power

The spread of iron led directly to the democratization of violence. Archaeological records reveal a measurable spike in skeletal trauma across Iron Age sites, indicating that iron made weapons affordable and locally sourceable. This transition stripped the bronze-wielding elite of their absolute monopoly on physical coercion. 

Today, this shift is mirrored by the democratization of asymmetric digital capabilities. Historically, only nation-states or heavily capitalized corporations possessed the resources to deploy sophisticated cyber-operations or execute global information campaigns. Today, highly optimized, open-source LLMs can run locally on consumer-grade hardware via edge computing. This allows individual actors to generate automated malware or orchestrate synthetic media campaigns without relying on central server infrastructures, effectively shifting disruptive power out of corporate "palaces" and into the hands of the collective.

2. Localized Conflict vs. Digital Market Competition

Historical data reveals sharp increases in localized conflict and competition following technological shifts. Regions adopting iron saw a dramatic rise in battle records as smaller, newly armed peripheral communities aggressively contested borders and refused to bow to distant empires. In the modern context, this translates to the fragmentation of the digital economic landscape. Established tech oligopolies built vast defensive moats around proprietary data centers and cloud monopolies. 

However, open-source AI operates as a decentralized equalizer. Small startups and agile developer collectives can now bypass multi-billion-dollar research and development bottlenecks, creating specialized intelligence tools that aggressively chip away at the market share of legacy tech giants—replacing a stable corporate ecosystem with a hyper-competitive, fluid landscape.

3. Institutional Instability vs. The Crisis of Authority

The lower financial barrier to conflict introduces widespread political instability. The empirical data illustrates this through a striking uptick in ruler turnover—such as the rapid succession of Babylonian kings—immediately following the regional adoption of iron. 

When shifting the balance of power becomes economically cheap, governing elite classes become structurally fragile. In our contemporary landscape, this instability manifests as a crisis of institutional legitimacy. Established corporate hierarchies and regulatory bodies rely on centralized channels to control information. Open-source tools dismantle these legacy gatekeepers by democratizing narrative creation and software distribution. 

Because alternative networks can mobilize instantly and outside of institutional oversight, executive leadership faces volatile market shifts, public trust erodes, and legacy structures find themselves in a state of permanent defensive re-evaluation.

4. Productive Expansion vs. Global Developer Proliferation

Iron acted as a powerful catalyst for demographic and productive expansion. As a dual-use technology, iron forged better weapons, but it also created durable agricultural plowshares that unlocked previously uncultivable land. The resulting agricultural yields triggered population booms, providing smaller communities with the human capital required to field self-sustaining, independent forces. 

The modern analog to the iron plow is the exponential expansion of the global developer base via AI assistance. Free, open-source networks act as an intellectual multiplier, allowing individuals outside of elite tech hubs—particularly in developing markets—to cultivate previously inaccessible technological landscapes. By lowering the cognitive and financial barriers to software creation, billions of people can now build and modify independent digital ecosystems, creating a massive influx of autonomous talent that makes a return to closed-source monopolies structurally impossible.

Ultimately, the structural shifts of the early Iron Age demonstrate that technological democratization is an irreversible solvent to centralized authority. 

Just as the ancient proliferation of iron plowshares and swords broke the rigid monopoly of bronze-wielding palaces—permanently locking the Eastern Mediterranean into a fragmented, multi-polar network—so too does the rise of open-source AI and edge computing shatter the defensive moats of today's tech hyperscalers. The four-fold pressure of individual empowerment, hyper-localized competition, institutional instability, and a massive expansion of autonomous talent ensures that the old hierarchies cannot simply rebuild their monopolies. 

By understanding iron not as a quiet consequence of systems collapse, but as the active structural baseline that prevented empires from ever centralizing again, we gain a predictive lens for our own digital future: when the tools of production and disruption become ubiquitous, the permanent fragmentation of the legacy status quo is a historical certainty.

text:
A MAJOR NEW danger for internet users was revealed today. A “zero-click mercenary spyware” program has been deployed by an Israeli company, researchers at the University of Toronto warned.

It enables the hacking of your phone or computer using ads on your screen—without any need to trick you into clicking anything.

“This is the first-ever public confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered via targeted ads,” said the Canadian research group, known as Citizens' Lab.

It is already in wide use, with millions of cases, and has hit some well known organizations. 

“It was used to infect devices at Al Jazeera with Candiru’s spyware,” said the group. Candiru is a Tel Aviv company specializing in cyber-espionage. The United Nations was also targeted.

.

THROUGH A LOOPHOLE
How does it work? Most people think of ads as just pictures: but they also contain code designed for “targeted advertising” – and it is that invisible step that is taken advantage of by a firm called Discover-Tech.

The Israel firm has a software platform called Controlium which uses ads to harvest your identity and IP address. 

You can then be selected as a target for hacking, in which a mercenary spyware firm sends a malicious code containing spyware to your device, the researchers said in a lengthy report.

.

DATA GOES TO CYBER-ESPIONAGE FIRMS
The Tel Aviv company has relations with a number of cyber espionage groups. 

“Discover-Tech ads are used to infect and profile on behalf of mercenary spyware vendor Candiru,” the report said. 

“We also detail connections between Discover-Tech and another mercenary hacking company, Bindecy, as well as connections with Intelos, a mercenary ADINT firm.” (ADINT stands for advertising intelligence.)

The result is a new type of danger, which the researchers called “AdFection” – because you end up with a computer infected through ads.  

.

MILLIONS OF VICTIMS
While the process is promoted as an ad placement system, the hacking puts ordinary people in danger of industrial or other forms of espionage, researchers at Citizen Lab warned. 

Multiple screens at Al Jazeera were infected by spyware through the system, for example.

“Our research showed large-scale data collection from millions of devices involving Discover-Tech and Candiru,” the report said.

.

STEPS FOR PROTECTION
The Toronto watchdog group say that companies need to take a number of steps to protect themselves from espionage.

- Use ad-blocking software.

- Never click Yes to on-screen offers to give you “targeted ads”.

- Block such ads at your firm's gateway level if you can.

- Get your company cyber-security staff to watch specifically for “adfection” attacks.

- If you use advertising on site, try to limit the ads to those of trusted partners.

- Ad agencies must audit their list of groups whose ads they distribute. 

The researchers contacted Discover-Tech Ltd, Candiru (Integrity Labs), Bindecy, and others, before publishing the report for comment. None of them responded.

A link to the full report is supplied in the comments.
.

text:
For decades, working-class people, anti-imperialists, and socialists have been told a comforting lie by the architects of the American electoral machine: that if we just elect "progressives," "democratic socialists," or "fighters for the working class" into the belly of the beast, they will change the system from within. We are told that figures backed by groups like the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) or branded as progressive champions will stand as an unbreakable wall against militarism, corporate greed, and the crimes of the imperialist state.

Today, that illusion has completely shattered. What we are witnessing across the American political landscape is an epidemic of capitulation. An unprecedented wave of transparent betrayals by DSA-aligned progressives and left-leaning Democrats has exposed a grim reality: the progressive wing of the Democratic Party does not threaten the capitalist, imperialist establishment—it serves as its most effective left-cover.

Nowhere is this moral and political bankruptcy more stark than in the systematic betrayal of the Palestinian struggle. Across the board, figures who once rode waves of grassroots energy by gesturing toward Palestinian human rights have systematically turned around, kissed the ring of the Zionist lobby, campaigned alongside architects of endless war, and normalized the role of the political sellout.

The Anatomy of the Progressive Sellout
To understand how figures on the nominal left morph into lapdogs of the imperialist state, one must examine the structural trap of the Democratic Party. The Democratic Party is a graveyard for social movements. It takes the righteous anger of working people—whether over healthcare, housing, or genocide—funnels it into multi-million-dollar ballot campaigns, and systematically neutralizes any genuine threat to American empire.

For years, politicians have cynically utilized the Palestinian struggle as a moral badge of honor to court anti-war and Arab-American voters, only to abandon those principles the moment power and institutional approval beckon. When politicians align themselves with war criminals, endorse bipartisan imperial consensus, and dilute their platforms to appease the military-industrial complex and the Zionist lobby, they are not merely "compromising"—they are committing an active betrayal of the working class.

The pattern is visible across the entire spectrum of prominent progressive and DSA-aligned figures. From Michigan to New York, and all the way to Capitol Hill, the timeline of capitulation is staggering.

Dr. Abdul El-Sayed: From "Next Obama" to Imperial Campaigning
Few trajectories illustrate this descent into establishment compliance better than that of Dr. Abdul El-Sayed. Once hailed as a visionary progressive champion in Michigan, El-Sayed’s recent political maneuvers have cemented his transition into a standard-issue corporate Democrat.

As detailed in reports by CNN and Middle East Eye, El-Sayed faced intense grassroots backlash after embracing none other than former Vice President Barack Obama for an upcoming campaign rally. To invite Obama—an architect of drone wars, corporate healthcare bailouts, and unconditional military support for the Israeli state—into a progressive campaign space is a direct insult to every anti-war activist.

This alliance was not an isolated incident. As covered by Al Jazeera and AP News, El-Sayed actively campaigned alongside Kamala Harris in a transparent bid to unify the fractured pro-corporate wing of the Democratic Party in a key swing state. By tying his wagon to the central pillars of the Biden-Harris administration—an administration that has funneled billions in bombs and diplomatic cover for the genocide in Gaza—El-Sayed has demonstrated that institutional ambition supersedes any commitment to Palestinian liberation or anti-imperialist solidarity. He has completed his evolution from a grassroots-hopeful physician into a loyal foot soldier for the very empire he once claimed to critique.

Zohran Mamdani: Diluting Solidarity Under Establishment Pressure
In New York City, DSA-backed politician Zohran Mamdani has similarly walked a treacherous path of institutional compromise, culminating in recent actions that have alienated core anti-war and anti-Zionist supporters.

While Mamdani has occasionally faced bipartisan backlash from conservative Democrats for verbal criticisms regarding the devastation in Gaza, his structural concessions to the political establishment tell a more troubling story. As reported by outlets like Politico and The Guardian, Mamdani's rollout of an official policy plan to combat antisemitism in New York City drew sharp rebukes from anti-Zionist Jewish groups and progressive organizers alike. By drafting plans that carefully sidestep or deliberately marginalize the fundamental critique of anti-Zionism—conforming to mainstream political definitions that insulate the Israeli state from legitimate political attack—Mamdani crossed a red line.

When a politician backed by the socialist left begins tailoring their foreign policy and civil rights stances to satisfy the sensibilities of the Zionist lobby and municipal power brokers, solidarity becomes a hollow marketing slogan. The recent backlash from anti-war protesters outside October 7 vigils highlights the growing fury on the ground: working-class activists are realizing that electoral survival within the capitalist state requires sanitizing one's principles until nothing radical is left.

Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez: Brunch with the Establishment and Imperial Realignment
On the national stage, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (AOC) has long served as the poster child for the contradiction of "fighting from within" the Democratic Party. Once associated with democratic socialist politics, Ocasio-Cortez has steadily retreated into the warm embrace of the congressional leadership.

Recent reporting by The Hill and USA Today shed light on a glaring symptom of this ideological drift: Ocasio-Cortez’s tepid and managed responses to high-level establishment maneuvering, such as the quiet convergence of elite interests between establishment figures like Hakeem Jeffries and Trump-aligned operatives like Jared Kushner. Rather than launching a systemic, fire-breathing assault on the bipartisan consensus of war, oligarchy, and real estate corruption, Ocasio-Cortez’s interventions have been reduced to safe, procedural wrist-slaps designed not to rock the boat of House leadership.

On foreign policy, the trajectory has been equally damning. Over successive legislative cycles, AOC and the broader "Squad" have repeatedly voted to fund the Iron Dome, offered procedural cover for military funding bills, and softened their rhetoric on Palestine to align with the Democratic Party's imperial foreign policy. The working-class mandate for international solidarity has been traded away for committee assignments and access to the inner chambers of Washington power.

John Fetterman: From Working-Class Populist to Empire’s Most Vicious Lapdog
Perhaps no political figure in recent memory represents a more grotesque, dizzying betrayal than John Fetterman. Cultivating an aesthetic of blue-collar populism and progressive independence, Fetterman rode a wave of grassroots enthusiasm into the U.S. Senate—only to immediately unmask himself as one of the most vicious, unhinged defenders of the American empire and the Israeli war machine.

As documented by The Guardian and Al Jazeera, Fetterman abandoned even the pretense of progressive values, culminating in jaw-dropping spectacles like making video appearances at Republican midterm conventions and cozying up to right-wing donors. Far from standing with the oppressed, Fetterman transformed into a foaming-at-the-mouth opponent of Palestinian rights, proudly waving Israeli flags, mocking peace activists, and cheering on the extermination of Gaza.

As analytical pieces from independent investigative platforms like Unplug the Empire have noted, Fetterman’s career stands as the ultimate cautionary tale: a clinical demonstration of how easily the electoral apparatus absorbs a supposed outsider and converts them into a barking dog for the ruling class.

Bernie Sanders: The Patriarch of the Sheepdog Mechanism
At the root of this entire epidemic stands Senator Bernie Sanders, the undisputed patriarch of the "progressive" political trap. For decades, Sanders popularized socialist rhetoric while anchoring his entire political strategy to the Democratic Party—the very party responsible for managing American imperialism and crushing working-class movements.

Sanders' role has consistently functioned as a "sheepdog" mechanism: he mobilizes millions of radicalized youth and working-class people with inspiring critiques of billionaire greed, only to herd them back into the voting booths to pull the lever for whichever neoliberal warmonger the Democratic Party establishment crowns.

When it comes to foreign policy, Sanders’ record exposes the fatal flaw of reformist socialism tied to the nation-state. While occasionally offering mild verbal critiques of humanitarian crises, Sanders has repeatedly voted for military budgets, backed foreign interventions, and maintained a cowardly silence on the full scope of U.S. imperial complicity in West Asia. By validating the Democratic Party as a vehicle for social change, Sanders has provided moral cover for a generation of younger politicians—like El-Sayed, Mamdani, and Ocasio-Cortez—to follow his footsteps into total capitulation.

The Weaponization and Sale of the Palestinian Struggle
The most unforgivable crime in this entire dynamic is the cynical, opportunistic exploitation of Palestinian suffering for electoral gain.

During campaign cycles, aspiring progressive politicians readily lean into the grief and anger of Arab-American and anti-war voters. They accept endorsements from Palestinian activists, whisper promises of justice behind closed doors, and use the language of human rights to build their progressive credentials. But the moment the ballots are cast and the office doors close, the calculus changes.

text:
Sergeant tries to steamroll this Uber driver that also happens to be a lawyer. Gets caught in lies. 

When an on-duty police sergeant looks you in the face and fabricates a fake statute just to force your camera off, that isn’t law enforcement, it is pure abuse of power and intimidation.

​We are in Wilmington, North Carolina, Jesse Bright was working a side hustle driving for Uber to pay down his student loans. He picked up a passenger for what seemed like a routine ride to pick up a paycheck.

 Unbeknownst to Bright, the destination was an address under surveillance by local law enforcement. Moments after driving away, his car was surrounded by five officers from the Wilmington Police Department and New Hanover County Sheriff’s Office.

​Recognizing the dangerous escalation of being swarmed, Bright did exactly what any citizen should do to protect themselves: he took out his phone and hit record.
​Instead of conducting a professional investigation, Wilmington Police Sergeant Kenneth Becker immediately resorted to blatant bully tactics.

 Becker marched up to the window and demanded Bright stop filming. When Bright stood firm on his First Amendment rights, Becker went full corrupt, inventing a fictional legal standard on the spot, telling him a "new law" had just passed outlawing filming the police, and explicitly barking: "Turn it off or I'll take you to jail."

​When intimidation failed, the retribution kicked in. Bright calmly told the officers he wasn't just an Uber driver, he was an active criminal defense attorney who practiced right down the street at the local courthouse, knew the statutes inside and out, and offered to show his bar card.

 Sgt. Becker mocked him ("And an Uber driver?") and immediately retaliated by calling in a K-9 drug-sniffing unit to tear into Bright's vehicle after Bright explicitly refused consent to a warrantless search.

​They detained an innocent man just trying to earn an honest living, threatened him with unlawful arrest, lied directly about the law, and subjected him to a retaliatory vehicle search purely because his camera was rolling and bruised their egos. BTW the K-9 search came back completely clean and found nothing, they were forced to release him without another word. 

​After the event occurred, Bright uploaded the raw footage online and exposed the corruption to the public.

Wilmington Police Chief Ralph Evangelous had to issue a public condemnation, explicitly stating that recording police in public is a protected constitutional right and welcoming citizens to film.

 Internal Affairs launched a full investigation, resulting in Sgt. Kenneth Becker being stripped of his rank, demoted back down to a patrol officer, and slapped with a permanent pay cut.

 The department was forced to issue mandatory policy retraining to every single officer on the force regarding citizens' First Amendment right to film.

​Know your rights, never consent to unlawful searches, and always keep the camera rolling when authority figures decide the law doesn't apply to them.

The claim that Christians only care about homosexuality remains false. Scripture treats every sin as serious—adultery, greed, lying, sexual immorality of every kind, hypocrisy, and the rest—because all of it falls short of God’s holiness (Romans 3:23). True Christians do not get to pick and choose which commands matter. We are called to confess and turn from our own sins first (Matthew 7:5; 1 John 1:8–9), not to pretend any category of sin is unimportant.
That said, voting is not the same thing as declaring a candidate sinless or above biblical standards.  NO POLITICAL LEADER IN HISTORY HAS BEEN FREE OF SIN.  David was an adulterer and murderer, yet God still used him. The New Testament does not require Christians to wait for a perfect candidate; it calls us to exercise wisdom in a fallen world, weighing character, policies, competence, and the real-world consequences of different choices. Many Christians who voted for Trump did so while openly acknowledging his personal failings (including adultery), just as they have voted for other imperfect candidates. They did not claim he was a model of Christian virtue; they concluded, on balance, that his policies on issues they care about (life, religious liberty, the courts, borders, the economy, etc.) were preferable to the alternative.
Accusing conservatives of hypocrisy for supporting a flawed candidate while also affirming biblical sexual ethics does not erase the original point. The reason homosexuality receives particular attention is not that Christians ignore adultery, greed, or other sins—it is that one is still widely recognized as wrong while the other is increasingly celebrated, redefined as an identity, and treated as beyond moral critique. Scripture addresses both (1 Corinthians 6:9–11 lists sexual immorality, adultery, greed, and more together). The consistent Christian message remains the same: all have sinned, all need repentance, and the gospel offers forgiveness and transformation to anyone who turns to Christ—regardless of which sins they have committed.

DON’T TOUCH MY SANCTUARY ! (Guess what happens to a church when the very doctrine that became its miraculous lifeline nearly two centuries ago and over the years its most distinctive hallmark... could now end up to be its most biblically unjustifiable millstone ?)

There is a sanctuary in heaven, the true tabernacle that the Lord set up and not humans. In it Christ ministers on our behalf… In 1844, at the end of the prophetic period of 2300 days, He entered the second and last phase of His atoning ministry… It is a work of investigative judgment which is part of the ultimate disposition of all sin, typified by the cleansing of the ancient Hebrew sanctuary on the Day of Atonement.

Adventist fundamental beliefs (1980)

Seventh-day Adventists accept the Bible as their only creed and hold certain fundamental beliefs to be the teaching of the Holy Scriptures. These beliefs, as set forth here, constitute the church’s understanding and expression of the teaching of Scripture. Revision of these statements may be expected at a General Conference Session when the church is led by the Holy Spirit to a fuller understanding of Bible truth or finds better language in which to express the teachings of God’s Holy Word.

Adventist fundamental beliefs (2015)

As Adventists, many of our "unique" doctrines are not, really, unique. After all, other Christians (not many, admittedly) into greater focus. keep the seventh-day Sabbath, as well. Though a majority of the Christian world believes in the immortality of the soul, other Christians understand that the dead sleep in the grave until the resurrection, either the first or second. Various "Adventist" teachings, i.e., eternal destruction (as opposed to eternal torment) or the nature of the millennium, can be found elsewhere too. In fact, almost all our doctrines are scattered throughout Christendom.  Except one: the 1844 pre-Advent judgment. For some, this fact is worrisome; Why don't more Christians see it, as well? For others, the uniqueness of the doctrine points even more powerfully to the special calling of the Seventh-day Adventist Church. It's precisely because no one else teaches this judgment that we have been raised to do so. From this doctrine, perhaps more than any other, our distinct identity as Seventh-day Adventists arises.

Sabbath School quarterly (The Gospel, 1844, and Judgment, 2006)

The [sanctuary] doctrine is, to me, the most colossal, psychological, face-saving phenomenon in religious history. … We personally do not believe that there is even a suspicion of a verse in Scripture to sustain such a peculiar position, and we further believe that any effort to establish it is stale, flat, and unprofitable.

Donald Grey Barnhouse (Are Seventh-day Adventists Christians? A New Look at Seventh-Day Adventism, Eternity magazine, 1956)

With the traditional Adventist interpretation of Daniel 8:14 as thesis, the historic-linguistic-contextual method of exegesis, which stands in opposition to it at practically every point, is its antithesis. (…) Our interpretational thesis and methodological antithesis are as impossible and mutually exclusive as matter and anti-matter and have the potential of mutually destroying each other, and the church as well. While Adventist Bible scholars have adopted the historical method, the church, as a whole, still basically practices the proof text method. Unresolved this dichotomy could have unfortunate consequences. The only way to resolve a problem such as this, is to find synthesis on a higher level of understanding.

Raymond F. Cottrell (A Hermeneutic for Daniel 8:14, unpublished manuscript, 1980)

Raymond has suggested to us a "way out" from the "dilemma" our denomination is now supposed to be caught in.  That is an escape mechanism based on a theory of the most "miraculous" our Church has ever been placed in front of.” (…) “By way of introduction, Elder Cottrell tries to convince us of the unqualified benefits our denomination has enjoyed as a direct result of one great historical event:  A new generation of Seventh-day Adventist scholars were finally blessed with the golden opportunity of education, which had been denied to our Bible students in former days.  According to Cottrell, we observed a marked improvement in the accuracy of conclusions arrived at in Adventist Bible research precisely at the time when those new scholars, with their more sophisticated knowledge, started making their impact in our offices and class rooms. Of course he does not, in this order of ideas, put any personal blame on the older researchers.  They just had the misfortune of not being properly educated.  So they were bound to come out as self-educated men, that is, men of mediocre scholarliness.  The new enlightenment we are now enjoying, as a denomination, is alleged as the positive reason for a new hope for the future.  Infallible evidence of this is a new awareness of problems our previous men of Biblical research were never confronted with.  Cottrell is referring to the increasing impossibility of harmonizing the actual contents of some contents of some Biblical texts with what our pioneers and the Spirit of Prophecy writings were once induced to put down, firmly and securely, as landmarks of our official creed. Brother Cottrell never tires of repeating that the large majority of these modern SDA Bible scholars agree wholeheartedly with him regarding the problem aspect of fundamental statements made by Ellen White in, for instance, absolutely decisive chapters of the Great Controversy.  Here Cottrell is not one bit less emphatic than Brinsmead and Ford, that objective scholarliness opens a gulf of disparity between The Bible and Ellen White.But it is in the suggested "remedy" to this situation Cottrell manifests the uniqueness of his spirit.  It is his "solution" that is without a rival in the history of Seventh-day Adventism. By and large, Protestants have never acquired any fame comparable to that of Catholics for what theology and philosophy have called "reconciliatio oppositorum"* or "complexio oppositorum"**.  In fact it is rather secular philosophy -- and not at all traditional religion -- that has developed the habit of astonishing the world of thinking men by having the boldness to blow up the virtual problem of mutually exclusive stand-points into thin air. (…) But what is his "solution" really like then, in this concrete instance?  How does Cottrell manage to still defend the doctrine of inerrancy regarding the teachings coming to us through Ellen G. White's ministry?  Nobody, you see, is more emphatic in extolling Ellen White as the great prophetess par excellence of the people of God in the endtime.  Therefore, he says, we must accept what her message has handed down to us in terms of basic landmarks for our faith as the very truth, the full truth and nothing but the truth. But then how come that Ellen White apparently can permit herself to go so boldly against certain things the Bible says about Christ's ministry in the sanctuary?  For here, as we recall, Cottrell is more emphatic maybe than anybody else, pointing out the great superiority of, according to Cottrell, the modern research method.  The modern researchers' accurate knowledge was, according to Cottrell, arrived at for the simple reason that they applied the historicolinguistic method of exegesis.  This has led them to conclusions quite opposite to those expressed solemnly and categorically by Ellen White in the Great Controversy.  But how then can the Prophetess, with "her" now classical doctrines about 1844 and the Investigative Judgement dare to go contrary to the "evident" testimony of the Scriptures?Cottrell's explanation is scaringly simple and straightforward:  Ellen White, in her capacity as the great Prophetess of the endtime has a right to do all this.  She is divinely entitled to reinterpret prophecies of the Bible in accordance with God's special intentions in the endtime.  "Parallel instances" of this kind are referred to, for instance Paul's "innovating interpretations" of statements in the Old Testament.  To the first century Christians such OT prophecies constituted the treasury from which they had to draw. 

Carsten Johnsen (Omega II, 1982)

Time and again competent non-Adventist Bible scholars have acknowledged that there is a biblical basis for cardinal points of Adventist faith such as the Sabbath, the second Advent and the nature of man. But without exception… they denounce our interpretation of Daniel 8:14 as eisegesis of the worst sort… Seventh-day Adventists identify the sanctuary mentioned in Daniel 8:14 as the sanctuary in heaven… and they understand its cleansing as the blotting out of the confessed sins of God’s repentant people during the course of an investigative judgment, on an antitypical day of atonement that began in 1844. … Adventist teachings that cluster around Daniel 8:14 have proved to be an impassible barrier to the thoughtful consideration of the Advent message… The date 1844… is pivotal of SDA faith. Destroy these and certain conclusions are self-evident. There would be no adequate basis for the existence of SDA. … The invariable rule appears to be that the more a non-Adventist knows about the Bible, the less disposed he is to look with favor on the Adventist interpretation of Daniel 8:14… The first major incentive to devote serious attention to the problem in Daniel 8:14 arose during the course of editing the Seventh-day Adventist Bible Commentary… Within a few months after the publication of Volume 4… came the series of protracted doctrinal discussions with Walter R. Martin and Donald Grey Barnhouse. … Finally, in 1958… I wrote to 27 leading Adventist Bible scholars… All 27 responded… A careful analysis… made evident that we had no satisfactory answer to the criticisms… Not one of the 27 believed that there was a linguistic or contextual basis for applying Daniel 8:14 to the heavenly sanctuary, an antitypical day of atonement, or 1844. As a result… a select “Committee on Problems in the Book of Daniel” [was appointed]… The majority and the minority both reached the same conclusions, but by different routes. … As a result of this impasse, the committee finally agreed to issue no formal report… My study… concluded that… the sanctuary of Daniel 8:14 is the same sanctuary referred to in verses 11-13, that is, the ancient temple in Jerusalem; that the “cleansing” or “restoration”… constituted its purification and rededication after desecration by the little horn… I believe that the hermeneutical principles outlined above provided an adequate inspired basis for applying the 2,300 evenings-mornings to 2,300 literal years terminating in 1844… Let it be clearly understood that the hermeneutic here proposed in no way alters the teachings we have traditionally based on Daniel 8:14. It does not affect the content of these teachings, but the method by which they are established as truth… In arriving at these conclusions, William Miller and other early Adventists basically followed the proof text method… The proof text method is basically what Bible scholars call eisegesis… During the 1930s Adventist college Bible teachers began to make consistent use of the historical-linguistic-contextual method… By the mid-1930s we were far up a theological cul de sac… For 25 years or more, the Bible scholars of the church have been well aware of the exegetical problems our conventional interpretation of Daniel 8:14… encounters… Non-Adventist critics… object that it cannot be derived from the words of Scripture but is superimposed upon them. … The problem is clear, especially if one remembers the unanimous acknowledgment of leading Adventist biblical scholars, clearly expressed in the 1958 poll, that there is no linguistic or contextual basis for our traditional interpretation of this passage. … A conclusive case for the heavenly sanctuary and a pre-Advent judgment can be made directly from Scripture, wholly apart from Daniel 8:14 and Hebrews 9… Can we not be willing to rely on these other passages…?"

Raymond F. Cottrell ("Sanctuary Debate: A Question of Method", Spectrum, 1980)

"The traditional interpretation of Daniel 8:14 with its sanctuary and investigative judgment, which gave birth to Seventh-day Adventism and accounts for its existence as a distinct entity within Christendom, has been the object of more criticism and debate, by both Adventists and non-Adventists, than all other facets of its belief system combined. (...) There can be no question as to the sincerity, diligence, and integrity of those who formulated the traditional Adventist interpretation of Daniel 8:14. It is equally obvious that they were following the flawed principles of the prooftext method: (1) In four major instances they adopted translation errors where the KJV misrepresents the Hebrew text. (2) They completely ignored the literary context in which Daniel 8:14 occurs. (3) They likewise ignored the historical context specified by the first six chapters and chapter 9:1-19 of the book. (...) In the years immediately following October 22, 1844 the traditional sanctuary doctrine was an important asset for stabilizing the faith of disappointed Adventists. Today it is an equally significant liability and deterrent to the faith, confidence, and salvation of biblically literate Adventists and non-Adventists alike. It was present truth following the great disappointment on October 22, 1844. It is not present truth in the year of our Lord 2002. Quod erat demonstrandum! »  

Raymond F. Cottrell (The Sanctuary Doctrine – Asset or Liability?,  2002)

Unto two thousand and three hundred evenings, mornings] i.e. successive evenings and mornings: cf. Daniel 8:26 -the vision of the evenings and the mornings." Dr. Filip Vukosavović (2023)

During archaeological excavations operated by the Israel Antiquities Authority and Tel-Aviv University, 16 pieces of ceramic roof tiles were discovered. (…) The tiles discovered (...) in City of David National Park date back to the time period of Greek Seleucid King Antiochus IV Epiphanes. Levi'im (Levites), descended paternally from the Jewish tribe of Levi; the forerunner of the Landau family is Rav Yehuda Liva, who lived in the 14th century in the German town of Landau. LANDAU, SAUL RAPHAEL (1870–1943), early member of the Labor Zionist movement and one of Herzl's aides. Landau joined Herzl immediately upon the publication of Der Judenstaat and became one of his close advisers, particularly on the matter of founding Die *Welt. According to Herzl's wishes, Landau took the editorship of the paper upon himself, but held the post only four months (until October 1897). He participated in the First Zionist Congress in Basle. Nearly eight, nine months ago, Jungkook said, “I’m going to live my life my way. Vouch for me.”
And now, watching him live those words so unapologetically, my heart is overflowing with emotions I can barely put into words. 🥹💜💚

People can call them teammates, friends, or whatever makes them comfortable. People can remain in denial, argue over labels, and try to fit their bond into whatever narrative they have chosen to believe. But today, none of that matters to me. Not even a little.
Because what matters is seeing these two boys I have loved so dearly smiling, spending time together, sharing their moments, and living their lives the way THEY want to.
No explanations.
No permission needed.
No obligation to satisfy anybody's curiosity.
And honestly? I am SO proud of them. 😭
You have no idea how emotional this makes me. There is so much love in my heart for these two that sometimes being a fan feels like carrying an ocean inside your chest.
You want nothing more than to see them happy, free, loved, protected, and surrounded by the kind of peace they deserve after everything they have been through and also after all they have given to the world.

My babies, you have given so much of yourselves to us through your music, your art, your laughter, and the little pieces of yourselves you choose to share. You have made so many of us smile through difficult days and found places in our hearts that words could never explain.
And all I want in return is for life to be gentle with you. For you to have beautiful days, genuine happiness, precious memories, and the freedom to live without the world constantly demanding something from you.

You don't owe us explanations. You don't owe the world a confession.
You owe yourselves the freedom to live, to love, to laugh, to make memories, and to be happy in whatever ways make your hearts feel at home. 🥹💚💜

And if sharing these little moments is your way of saying, “This is my life, and I am going to live it my way,” then, Jungkook, baby, I hope you know how many of us are cheering for you with our whole hearts.

Taehyungie, Jungkookie, my precious boys… I hope you always have each other as a source of laughter, comfort, beautiful memories, and happiness.
I hope the world gives you the kindness you have given so many others. 
 hope you never feel that you have to shrink yourselves to make other people comfortable.
Whatever words people use to describe your bond, whatever assumptions they make, and whatever the future holds, I will always wish you both a life filled with happiness, freedom, and love.
The kind of happiness that doesn't need to be explained to anyone.
The kind that lets you wake up every morning knowing you are free to be yourselves.

Today, I am not asking for anything from you. I am simply happy for you. Proud of you. Grateful to witness these little moments of your lives. And sending you both all the love my heart can possibly hold.

LIVE YOUR LIVES, MY BOYS. YOUR WAY. YOUR TERMS. YOUR HAPPINESS. 😭💜💚

May you always have the courage to choose what makes you happy, the freedom to live as you wish, and the peace of knowing that you don't have to prove anything to anyone.

I love you both more than these words could ever express.
Please keep smiling.
Please keep making beautiful memories.
Please keep choosing happiness.

My Taehyungie.
My Jungkookie.
My two precious pieces of heart.
 You deserve every beautiful thing life has to offer.
And today, my heart is just so, so happy for you. 🥹🫂💜💚

text:
The Green Party’s principles may carry a political cost.

The Holborn and St Pancras result gives the debate a concrete shape: Labour retained the seat with 12,292 votes while the Greens received 8,928. Tom Slater and the other *Off the Fence* speakers—Konstantin Kisin, Francis Foster and Winston Marshall—read that setback alongside the controversy surrounding Zack Polanski and the Green Party’s “Zionism is racism” motion.

Their argument is that uncompromising ideological language can energise a committed base while limiting broader appeal. Voters may support stronger action on Israel, climate or social issues but still want a party that appears capable of governing, respects national belonging and applies consistent standards across conflicts. A slogan that treats a complex political dispute as morally settled can therefore create loyalty among activists and discomfort among potential voters.

That opens space for Labour. Figures such as Andy Burnham may attract progressive voters by combining left-wing positions with greater institutional credibility. Labour can present itself as the practical vehicle for policies that Green voters favour, while the Greens remain associated with a narrower activist culture.

But the panel also notes the danger for Labour: moving further left may win some Green voters while alienating traditional working-class or patriotic supporters. The electoral contest is therefore not simply about which party is more progressive, but which one can turn progressive commitments into a coalition broad enough to govern.

Will voters reward ideological clarity, or will they prefer the larger party that offers a more credible route to power?

What do you make of this point?

🇮🇷🇵🇰| The Roofs of Peshawar and Those Who Should Be Held Accountable

On the morning of October 15, 2026, the roof of the Al-Khair Education Center, a three-story private school in the Dir Colony of Peshawar, Pakistan collapsed while students were in class. The roof fell from the third floor, crashing through the second floor and landing on students in the classrooms on the ground floor.

More than 34 schoolchildren and one teacher lost their lives. The victims were between 6 and 14 years old. Over 45 children were injured, some critically. This stands as the deadliest building collapse in Pakistan’s history.

That same week, Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi sent a letter to Sana’a, reaffirming the historical ties between Iran and Yemen. Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei extended condolences to the families of the victims in Peshawar.

Yet, no one is asking: Why did the roof collapse? Who authorized the use of this building? And why are Pakistan’s building standards for schools effectively meaningless?

💥 A Roof Held Up by Makeshift Supports and Children Summoned to Class

Preliminary investigation reports provide the answer. They reveal that the roofs throughout the school were constructed using prefabricated slabs. The roof on the top floor had been severely damaged by rainwater erosion, but the school administration failed to repair it. Instead, they propped up the damaged roof with makeshift supports and continued to hold classes beneath it. The roof fell from a height of approximately 6 to 7.6 meters, crashing down onto the students as they studied.

Peshawar Police Chief Saeed Ahmed put it bluntly: "The building was structurally weak. The roof was overloaded, and the structure itself was unsound this led to the collapse." The owner of the school has been arrested.

This was a completely preventable tragedy. The roof was damaged, so they propped it up with temporary supports. They summoned the children to class. The roof collapsed. The children died.

🎯 Who Is Doing the Inspections?  Who gave the approval? Who signed off on it?

Building standards exist on paper in Pakistan, but in practice, they are rarely enforced. Substandard materials, corner-cutting, and a blatant disregard for safety regulations these are the norms of Pakistan’s construction industry. A report by the Central News Agency (CNA) points out: "Building collapses occur frequently in Pakistan; national construction standards are often ignored, substandard materials are widely used, and safety protocols are bypassed to cut costs."

Dir Colony is a densely packed neighborhood, with narrow streets surrounding the school. When professional rescue teams arrived, local residents were already on the scene parents were digging through the rubble with their bare hands, searching for their children. An injured teacher, who was inside the classroom when the roof gave way, described the moment as if the sky itself had come crashing down.

Nearly a hundred rescue workers eventually arrived. But who approved this building for use as a school? Who issued the operating permit? And who merely went through the motions during past inspections?

📜 A School in Peshawar, a Grave in Peshawar

This is not the first time Peshawar has buried its children.

In March 2025, the Darul Uloom Haqqania, a religious seminary in Peshawar was struck by a suicide bombing, claiming the lives of several students during Friday prayers. Iran offered its condolences at the time.

In 2024, an explosion occurred near a school in Peshawar. In 2022, a mosque in the city was attacked, leaving dozens dead. Peshawar the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, the headquarters of a Pakistan Army corps, and a strategic hub near the Afghan border has seen its children killed time and again: in classrooms, in mosques, and in marketplaces.

Yet, a roof collapse is not a terrorist attack. There are no bombs, no gunmen, and no so-called "martyrs."  It consisted of just one building, a structure that should have been demolished and one person who decided to keep it in operation.

⚔️ The military in Yemen; a school collapsing

This tragedy unfolded against the backdrop of the Pakistani military fighting in Yemen on behalf of Saudi Arabia.

Without the approval of the National Assembly, Pakistan’s Chief of Army Staff, Asim Munir, deployed more than a brigade’s worth of troops along with air force assets to Saudi Arabia. Pakistani fighter jets have reportedly carried out airstrikes against Ansarullah positions within Yemen.

Pakistan’s military resources are being funneled into a war that is not Pakistan’s own.

Meanwhile, in Peshawar, children were attending classes beneath a roof held up by makeshift, temporary supports.

#Conclusion: Who is responsible for the roof in Peshawar?

Families of the victims gathered for the funerals. Hundreds of mourners crowded around the cemetery, while loudspeakers from a local mosque broadcast calls for residents to join in prayer for the deceased. Locals noted that most of the children who perished lived in the very neighborhood where the school was located; they were left not knowing which grieving family to visit first to offer their condolences.

Where, then, should they go to express their grief? To the office of the school’s owner? To the municipal authorities who authorized the building’s use? Or to the officials who allowed building codes and safety standards to become entirely meaningless?

The roof in Peshawar collapsed. Beneath it lay 34 children who would never return home.

Long live the resistance against the empire that neglects its own children.

Red giants are evolved from main-sequence stars with masses in the range from about 0.3 M☉ to around 8 M☉.[13] When a star initially forms from a collapsing molecular cloud in the interstellar medium, it contains primarily hydrogen and helium, with trace amounts of "metals" (in astrophysics, this refers to all elements other than hydrogen and helium). These elements are all uniformly mixed throughout the star. The star "enters" the main sequence when its core reaches a temperature (several million kelvins) high enough to begin fusing hydrogen-1 (the predominant isotope), and establishes hydrostatic equilibrium. (In astrophysics, stellar fusion is often referred to as "burning", with hydrogen fusion sometimes termed "hydrogen burning".) Over its main sequence life, the star slowly fuses the hydrogen in the core into helium; its main-sequence life ends when nearly all the hydrogen in the core has been fused. For the Sun, the main-sequence lifetime is approximately 10 billion years. More massive stars burn their fuel disproportionately faster and so have a shorter lifetime than less massive stars.[14]

When the star has mostly exhausted the hydrogen fuel in its core, the core's rate of nuclear reactions declines, and thus so do the radiation and thermal pressure the core generates, which are what support the star against gravitational contraction. The star further contracts, increasing the pressures and thus temperatures inside the star (as described by the ideal gas law). Eventually a "shell" layer around the core reaches temperatures sufficient to fuse hydrogen and thus generate its own radiation and thermal pressure, which "re-inflates" the star's outer layers and causes them to expand.[15] The hydrogen-burning shell results in a situation that has been described as the mirror principle: when the core within the shell contracts, the layers of the star outside the shell must expand. The detailed physical processes that cause this are complex. Still, the behavior is necessary to satisfy simultaneous conservation of gravitational and thermal energy in a star with the shell structure. The core contracts and heats up due to the lack of fusion, and so the outer layers of the star expand greatly, absorbing most of the extra energy from shell fusion. This process of cooling and expanding is the subgiant stage. When the envelope of the star cools sufficiently it becomes convective, the star stops expanding, its luminosity starts to increase, and the star is ascending the red-giant branch of the Hertzsprung–Russell (H–R) diagram.[14][16]
