Podcast Summary | Financial Audit: Financial Audit's Most Violent Husband

Overview
A 34-year-old couple from the Catskills in New York sits down with seven years of history, three children between born and unborn, and a financial life held together by credit cards, minimum payments, and mistrust. The husband controls every dollar, the wife must text for grocery money and wait, and both describe escalating hostility that has included a flipped plate of tacos, a mother-in-law physically blocking a doorway, and a paternity test request. Beneath the money fight is a deeper fight about dignity, contribution, and whether two people who clearly built a life together can ever trust each other enough to share it. The host's verdict is blunt: without roughly doubling their income and completely rebuilding their spending behavior, bankruptcy is not a last resort, it is the only realistic exit.

Key Themes
- Financial control has replaced partnership: the husband distributes money on request while the wife asks permission for diapers, gas, and pads, turning adulthood into a negotiation.
- The wife frames the issue as dignity, not luxury, arguing that staying home with the children was agreed to and should not mean having no money or autonomy.
- The husband treats her past spending as permanent evidence of irresponsibility, judging her on a higher-income era she says she would adapt away from.
- Their real budget problem is small, frequent spending: repeated $20 to $50 purchases that can total about $1,500 a month, not one dramatic purchase.
- Trust is the relationship's actual fault line, with mutual accusations about exes, a disputed Halloween event, and a paternity test request that cut deeper than any budget argument.
- Communication collapsed into avoidance: kids in the house mean issues go unresolved, resentment builds, and the same fights replay over plates, socks, and paperwork.
- The household earns about $7,300 a month from a cleaning business the husband calls his lowest month ever, barely covering necessities before taxes in New York.
- Debt is stacked across at least 11 credit cards, personal loans, and buy-now-pay-later accounts, with IRS debt over $40,000 looming and a checking balance of $6.71.
- The proposed fix is collaboration, not penance: combined accounts, shared visibility, a joint budget, three months of controlled spending, then likely bankruptcy to clear what behavior alone cannot.

Detailed Summary
Robin and Marshall are both 34 and from the Catskills Mountains in New York. After their first child, he took over the finances completely. She receives grocery money but must ask for exact amounts. She describes times with no money in her account for pads or diapers, texting him and waiting. He can drive into the city for comedy, stay out until 5 a.m., see movies, or browse Home Depot freely. She must ask permission and often feels rushed.

She agreed to stay home until the children are school age, then planned to become a preschool teacher. They have a 6-year-old daughter, a 1-year-old son, and she is pregnant with their third child. She says $400 a month would cover groceries and other needs. He says groceries are separate from that and that she still asks for more. She disputes any claim that $100 a month covers groceries for the whole family, calling it crazy.

He says she spends part of requested gas money on other things and then asks for gas again. The host asks whether he wants her to get a job. He says he does not want children with a stranger at daycare all day. She says daycare would mean 8 to 12 hours a day and that she does not want someone else raising her children. The host says he does not care much about agreed couple dynamics but notes they are obviously in it long term because of the kids.

The husband says her spending becomes a little bit every single day, not a major purchase like a car. The host asks about a past hobby of purchasing vehicles and whether his fear about her spending is evidence-based.

She says she helped build the cleaning business, including using a vehicle she paid for and cleaning while pregnant. He says she sometimes volunteered and tells her not to complain about work she offered to do. He was fired from selling RVs after one customer complaint claiming he posted the customer's phone number online and encouraged harassment. He says the customer provided no proof and that he had previously argued with the customer over a work text-message program. He says he told his job on August 13 that he was going on paid family medical leave, and the complaint arose between the 13th and 20th.

The cleaning business does commercial work for banks and car dealerships, mainly run by him with some contractors. Monthly revenue is about $7,300, which he calls the lowest since starting it. The host argues even $7,500 a month is not enough for a family of four plus a baby in New York after taxes and costs. The husband admits he was not actively seeking new cleaning clients while he had other income, and as clients fell off he had no new work lined up. He says he has applied to jobs and is taking civil service exams.

The wife says when he worked long hours he was stressed and difficult to be around. Now that he is not working as much, he is easier to be around. She describes an argument over taco night: she began cleaning up while he was still eating, he flipped a plate, and food went everywhere. He disputes her account, saying she cleaned up in the middle of his meal and that a napkin was on the plate. She says she thought he was done.

She describes not remembering parts of arguments because she blacks out anticipating his overreaction. He says he has never flipped a plate or thrown a paper plate in arguments with his girlfriend. They have been together seven years. The last year has had fewer or no big arguments according to him, though she references tension around daily behavior.

She says she used to prevent him from leaving because she wanted to solve the problem, but realized she would not get what she needed and now lets him leave. He mentions leaving two weeks ago when their daughter did not want to sleep in there. She says there was no fight and he just left. She says he recently got fired and since being home she has seen him slip back into old behavior.

Complaints include shoes left where people can trip, plates not thrown away, socks everywhere, the house door left open despite animals and children, her water moved, and items lost when she moves them. She says he wants the kitchen table as his office with important paperwork where the children eat spaghetti. He says he cannot do something for five minutes without her moving his things. He describes her as having no patience. She says he insults her and who she is, so she gives back the same energy, which he cannot handle.

The couple has been together about six to seven years, engaged three years, not married. They bought a house instead of having a wedding, citing COVID shutdowns and later her father's illness and death. Her father passed away in May, after they moved into their house, delaying wedding plans. He has been doing stand-up comedy for about two and a half years and says it makes little or no money. The host frames this as unsustainable while he has three kids and household bills. She previously worked as a teacher and has a BBA. Returning to teaching is discussed as a more reliable income and benefits option than comedy.

The pregnancy was initially ectopic and developing in her fallopian tube. A doctor recommended a medical abortion for safety, but she says the medication was not enough and the pregnancy moved into her uterus. He says they changed their anniversary date after a Halloween event, originally September 1st, later changed to when they got engaged. He claims she was talking to her ex, sending photos, saying I love her, and calling one of the girls babe. She says they were both talking to exes when they first got together. She says her ex had been in jail and the relationship fizzled after seven years.

He says she kissed her ex at Halloween and later admitted it. She denies kissing him and says the ex was extremely intoxicated. He claims she told him she may as well have screwed him. She denies saying that. He says she denied the incident for months and then came clean. She says she never had sex with the ex. She says after she had their daughter, he was texting his ex-girlfriend that his soul would forever be for her. He says he was unsure whether the child was his and asked for a paternity test. She says she told him how dare you and warned he would never see the child if he asked again. They agree they coordinated a paternity test in the post-show.

He has been arrested 10 times, including felony weapon possession and sales and a DWI at 19. He says every arrest was dismissed or not charged, and he has a clean record. He says he had taken the LSAT and was applying to law school before an arrest over a gun-business mixup interrupted the process. He is applying again. They are paying $2,750 to an attorney after a February arrest. He was in a parking lot for his cleaning company late at night, an officer asked if he had been drinking or smoking, he refused chemical testing, and he was arrested.

The couple's debt is largely in the husband's name and includes multiple small purchases financed at high interest. The wife has to ask for money for basics like gas, groceries, and diapers while he controls spending and sends money on request. He resists a shared account because he says she previously spent money and asked for more. She says this is now being used to judge her based on old behavior when he did not speak up. The host frames the solution as collaboration: one account, shared budget, and both partners having access, rather than the working spouse acting as dictator.

A lofted bed costing $110 is about to be paid off next month, with a minimum monthly payment around $30. A $138 purchase was borrowed at 16 percent interest. The husband says the actual extra charge is about $12 to $16, but the host says it stacks up. An Amazon purchase of $117.83 was for a dog gate. The minimum payment is around $12, and the host says it will take about a year to pay off. A $443.54 purchase from Meta was for Meta glasses. The husband says he wanted to capture moments with the kids without stopping to take out a phone. The host criticizes the Meta glasses purchase as prioritized over groceries and the wife's request for a hobby.

The husband previously made anywhere from $12,000 to $25,000 a month, which the host calls a crazy downfall from their current situation. The wife asks for about $400 a month in her account for groceries, diapers, and gas. The husband says he sends money when asked but complains that after sending $100 he often gets another request for $20 shortly after, saying there is always one more.

The couple's finances show chronic overspending and reliance on debt: credit cards, personal loans, buy-now-pay-later-style accounts, and overdrafts. His mother initially agreed to buy and live in a house with them, then backed out after they had already changed their rental timeline. The mortgage is in both his and his mother's name. They want to refinance to remove her but say they would wait until rates fall. After consolidating credit card debt with a OneMain loan using the car as collateral, they reportedly ran credit cards back up, so the consolidation did not change behavior.

The reviewer repeatedly argues that spending on DoorDash, Starbucks, Dunkin, Amazon, vending machines, dispensaries, sports betting, and other nonessentials is incompatible with their claimed paycheck-to-paycheck situation. Credit card mentioned with a $2,352 minimum payment and $2,308 payment listed. The reviewer attributes the high amount to late fees, interest, no payment, being over limit, and a 31.74 percent interest rate. Mortgage details stated: $222,000 loan, $393,300 total, 6.2 percent interest rate, $2,442.16 monthly payment. OneMain Financial loan stated at 16 percent interest, described as a consolidation loan using the car as collateral.

The household's minimum necessities equal their income before taxes. Setting aside taxes properly puts them about $25,500 underwater. The proposed path out is to combine accounts, give both partners access, stop credit-card spending, budget together, discuss spending limits, and stabilize for three months. Bankruptcy is framed as the only realistic way out of the debt unless income roughly doubles. The host says not to wait because tackling the IRS is urgent. Bankruptcy alone is treated as insufficient unless spending behavior changes first, or they risk repeated bankruptcies. They already own a house and car, so preserving good credit is presented as less important than getting the budget and IRS situation under control.

Lack of communication is identified as a core problem. Counseling is suggested and would need to be budgeted. House value is stated as $230,000 with $222,000 owed. The Hammer financial score is 1 out of 10, with zeros for budget, debt, emergency fund, and retirement, and 5 out of 10 for real estate. The host says he will allow bankruptcy after three months of controlled budgeting.

text:
After 70 AD - Shift from Sacrifice to Prayer and Study...

The shift from temple sacrifice (korbanot) to prayer (tefillah) and study (Torah) is the central theological axis upon which Judaism spun to survive the post-70 AD world.

Before the destruction, the primary way a Jew sought atonement, expressed gratitude, or drew close to God was through a physical substance - an animal or grain offering brought to a specific altar in Jerusalem.

When that altar was destroyed, the early sages had to answer a terrifying question: How do we maintain our covenant with God if our only means of atonement is gone?

To convince a traumatized nation that they could be forgiven without blood sacrifices, the early rabbis turned to the Hebrew prophets, who had long criticized a purely mechanical approach to the Temple rituals.

- Hosea 6:6: The foundational verse for this shift became Hosea’s declaration: "For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and acknowledgment of God rather than burnt offerings."

- The "Cows of our Lips": The rabbis relied heavily on Hosea 14:2, which states, "Take words with you and return to the Lord... we will offer the calves of our lips." This verse was interpreted strictly to mean that words of prayer could functionally replace the physical offering of calves on the altar.

- Psalm 51:17: They emphasized Davidic theology: "The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise."

text:
The background of Kasun Kularatne, also known as Balangoda Kassapa Thero 

As of today, Balangoda Kassapa Thero, who is staying near the Ministry of Buddha Sasana in Colombo, has once again become a focal point in the country's political and religious discourse. Participating in the 'Justice for Robe' march that came from Kandy, he demands an unconditional presidential pardon for Galagodaatte Gnanasara Thero, stating that if not granted, the President should resign. He has also announced a program to offer one hundred thousand robes (සිවුරු ලක්ෂයක්) on behalf of Gnanasara Thero.
He has decided to stay near the ministry overnight, despite the Fort Magistrate's Court prohibiting protests.

Balangoda Kassapa Thero, who works with groups like the Shakya Putra National Organization, gained widespread public attention during the 2022 Galle Face Aragalaya (struggle). He actively contributed to the struggle by setting up a tent near the Bandaranaike statue at GotaGoGama and became embroiled in a controversy by opposing the singing of the national anthem in both Sinhala and Tamil. Later, he severely criticized the struggle, claiming that Buddhism was not given prominence and the Catholic Church received more space.

Constantly discussed on social media, he is referred to by critics as a politician with racist views who uses the monastic robe. However, his supporters see him as a protector of the Buddha Sasana. Some media reports, such as Lanka E News, have identified his lay name as Munindrage Diluka Kasun Kularatne and stated that he faced a case in the Balangoda Magistrate's Court in 2009 for assaulting his father. However, that court verdict has not yet been independently confirmed.

Since the Aragalaya, Kassapa Thero has had several encounters with the law in the past few years. In August 2022, he was arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department on charges of forcibly entering Temple Trees and was released on a personal bail of five hundred thousand rupees. In February 2023, he was arrested by the police for engaging in a Satyagraha (non-violent resistance) blocking the parliamentary entrance against the Thirteenth Constitutional Amendment, and again in June 2024, when preparing for a hunger strike near Parliament against the proposed Electricity Act.

Among his legal interventions, the most serious incident was reported from Trincomalee in November 2025. Following a complaint by the Coast Conservation Department alleging the unauthorized placement of a Buddha statue in a coastal protected zone near the Sri Sambuddhatva Jayanthi Bodhiraja Viharaya on Fort Road, Trincomalee, severe unrest erupted when the police attempted to remove it.

Following this incident, on January 14, 2026, the Trincomalee Magistrate's Court remanded Kassapa Thero and several other suspects. The Port Police filed eight charges, including membership in an unlawful assembly, unauthorized construction in a coastal zone, and assaulting police officers, and he commenced a hunger strike in prison. Later, with the intervention of representatives from the National Freedom Front, he temporarily suspended it and was admitted to the Trincomalee Hospital due to illness. Even after writ petitions filed before the Court of Appeal were rejected, he was granted bail by the Trincomalee High Court on February 11, under strict conditions, including not obstructing religious or public activities.

Meanwhile, another legal crisis arose when Kassapa Thero publicly declared that the accusation of a monk attempting to sexually abuse a minor girl at a temple in Navatkuli, Jaffna, was a conspiracy by Tamil political parties. An application to file a contempt of court case against him in this regard was rejected by the Chavakachcheri Magistrate's Court in June 2026.

The journey of Balangoda Kassapa Thero, which began with a tent at the protest site, extended to prisons and hospitals, and now to street protests imposing conditions on the President, perfectly illustrates one aspect of the complex conflict between religion and law in modern Sri Lanka.

Timeline of Legal Disputes

September 7, 2009 - Media reports emerged about a case (No. 29844) at the Balangoda Magistrate's Court regarding an assault on his father (this verdict has not been independently confirmed).

August 24, 2022 - Arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department on charges of entering Temple Trees during the Aragalaya.

August 26, 2022 - Released on a personal bail of five hundred thousand rupees by the Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court in connection with the Temple Trees incident.

February 8, 2023 - Arrested by the police while engaging in a Satyagraha at the parliamentary entrance against the Thirteenth Amendment.

June 6, 2024 - Arrested by Talangama Police while preparing for a hunger strike near Parliament against the proposed Electricity Act.

November 16, 2025 - Coast Conservation Department filed a complaint and protests erupted regarding unauthorized construction and the placement of a Buddha statue in a coastal protected zone in Trincomalee.

January 14, 2026 - Remanded by the Trincomalee Magistrate's Court in connection with the Trincomalee Buddha statue incident.

January 28, 2026 - Port Police filed eight charges in court, including membership in an unlawful assembly and assaulting police officers, and the suspects declared innocent. Remand period further extended.

February 3, 2026 - Writ petitions challenging the Magistrate's Court remand order were rejected by the Court of Appeal.

February 11, 2026 - Suspects released by the Trincomalee High Court on a cash bail of Rs. 10,000 and two personal bails of Rs. one million each, with strict conditions.

June 5, 2026 - Request for contempt of court action based on his statement regarding the Jaffna Navatkuli incident was rejected by the Chavakachcheri Magistrate's Court.

October 16, 2026 - Fort Magistrate's Court issued an order prohibiting protests in Colombo demanding a pardon for Galagodaatte Gnanasara Thero.

text:
Bechorot 28 - When Must the Firstborn Animal Be Eaten?
📷The firstborn must be eaten "year by year". What does this mean? If a firstborn was born blemished, it does not have the full holiness of the firstborn and therefore is allowed to be eaten. In that case it must be slaughtered and eaten within a year from its birth.

If the firstborn was born unblemished then in the time of the Temple it becomes eligible to be offered in the Temple after eight days. Within a year after this time it must indeed be brought as a sacrifice, slaughtered, and eaten by a Kohen and his family. Today an unblemished firstborn poses a problem: the owner must care for it and then give it to a Kohen. He cannot force the kohen to accept it, because it is a present, so if he cannot find a Kohen, he continues to care for it until it develops a blemish, however long this takes.

One can only slaughter a firstborn through the permission of an expert. If one first slaughtered it, and then showed it to an expert, Rabbi Yehudah permits it to be eaten, but Rabbi Meir forbids it because of a possible confusion.

text: Good morning. I will have a post tomorrow morning Saturday and then I will not be back on here again until Sunday the 25th. This is going to be a huge challenge. I am not going to open or be on my phone for one solid week. I am hoping you will read why. I am not well enough to travel on my own to go on a retreat by myself and there is a retreat center I wanted to go to not far from me upon the completion of my physical therapy. Brenda, Russell and I have not had extended time with the three of us together rather than in a hospital setting so the three of us have decided we are going to go to the upper peninsula of Michigan on Sunday. I have been longing for quiet time with God. No Russell is not God. Lol. You may relate to my next thoughts. I possess the ability to experience Joy. I also possess the ability to experience shame and survivor's guilt. Living a life as a white man in the United States affords me  privileges that some  others do not have offered to them. That makes me feel guilty. And when I see what is happening in this culture with the undeniable hate and the cruelty, a country where a woman cannot express herself at a rally without being beaten by men and cheered on by the president of the United States, a country without remorse. A country who continues in its   delusion to express to the rest of the world “thank you for admiring us.”  I do not have the capacity to experience joy knowing that down the street my friend a year ago this week was kidnapped and thrown in the back of a van because he was of Arab descent although he was born in Detroit, Michigan. I cannot watch children being ripped from their parents arms and the president saying “well your  mother shouldn't have come here.” I cannot experience joy while being witness to this. I just can't. This does not mean I am depressed. The lack of presently experiencing joy is not the same as having the inability. I can and I will again but don't get me wrong I have happy moments and I have joyful moments but an overall contentment is just not currently possible. The retreat is to focus on something I have been disconnected from. And I'm talking about the appreciation of God. Not gratitude, but  appreciation. I know I am grateful and I feel grateful for God's blessings but to appreciate them I must stop and recognize them. And what I have seen for months is fighting and bickering and injustice, injustice, injustice, injustice and people laughing at the injustices. I live in a country where a man can get shot in the neck in front of a 5 year old and people will say “I voted for this,” and then immediately start talking about Biden. The hardest thing in my almost 70 years is to realize I have been deceived by my own country. I never knew I lived among American terrorists and nazis. People who defend an ice agent shooting a woman in the head and calling her a fucking bitch. People who say she deserves that. A country that practices crime against humanity. This is our current experience and I'm not taking the time to stop and recognize that beyond the evil veil is the presence of God and everything that comes with God.  I don't  readily recognize God's architecture of magnificent miracles one after the other because my vision is blocked by immoral decay . The purpose of my retreat is to reconnect with a total appreciation for God's wonders. And I do not want to get a text message and feel I have to respond to somebody. I don't want to have to check an email to see if a bill has been posted. I will not check the news because if something is earth-shattering somehow I will find out. I cannot and will not allow anything to get in the way of the deep appreciation I once had but is currently blindfolded. I'm taking the blindfold off. God bless.

Jerzy Skolimowski's "The Shout" Blu-ray - Alan Bates, Susannah York, John Hurt, Tim Curry @Criterion
US: https://t.co/6tRL9l8GJj
CAN: https://t.co/q93wB0Cusw
UK: https://t.co/DnFHRsPrJk
BONUS CAPTURES:
https://t.co/HjB6u9RvTT
OUR REVIEW:
https://t.co/ePG2HeB1YL
Jerzy Skolimowski, a Polish émigré working in England, approaches English village life the way an anthropologist might. Crossley is a kind of cuckoo in the nest, a figure familiar from Teorema and similar tales of the stranger who disrupts a bourgeois home. Here, though, the threat is primal rather than spiritual. He represents something old and uncontrollable that the civilized couple can’t reason with and, in Rachel’s (Susannah York) case, can’t resist. The Shout is one of the most unsettling and original British films of the 1970s, a puzzle-box study of dread that never settles whether we are watching memory, invention, or madness. Skolimowski (Moonlighting, EO, Night Train, Essential Killing, Deep End) looks at the English village like an outsider, making the cottage, the church, and the cobbler's shop as strange as Crossley's tales of the outback. Alan Bates (The Running Man (1963), The Wicked Lady, The Go-Between, Tommy, Zorba the Greek, The Pumpkin Eater, The Rose, Secret Friends, Impossible Object, A Day in the Death of Joe Egg, King of Hearts, An Unmarried Woman, Women in Love, Far From the Madding Crowd, The Caretaker, Georgy Girl, Gosford Park) is superb as Crossley, by turns charming, menacing, and pitiful, and he never reveals whether the man is a sorcerer or simply a very persuasive madman. John Hurt (Alien, Melancholia, Watership Down, I, Claudius, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, 1984, The Limits of Control, Perfume: The Story of a Murderer, 10 Rillington Place, Dead Man, Scandal, The Hit, A Man for All Seasons) is a fine match as the composer whose curiosity about sound becomes the very thing that endangers him. Susannah York (Visitors, Images, The Killing of Sister George, Gold, Sands of the Kalahari, Tom Jones, Tunes of Glory, A Man for All Seasons, They Shoot Horses, Don't They?, X Y & Zee, The Silent Partner) conveys Rachel's trance-like surrender with very little dialogue, and Tim Curry (Clue, Alice, The Hunt for Red October) is a quietly wry presence as Robert Graves, keeping score at the asylum cricket match. Mike Molloy's (The Hit) cinematography makes the vast coastal dunes feel like the edge of the known world, while the sound design and the electronic score by Anthony Banks, Michael Rutherford, and Rupert Hine turn listening itself into a source of terror. The Criterion Blu-ray offers a superb, film-like 1080P transfer from a 2K restoration approved by both Skolimowski and Molloy, a lossless 24-bit 2.0 surround track that delivers the titular shout in all its unnerving power, new interviews with Skolimowski and producer Jeremy Thomas, almost an hour of Skolimowski at the 1997 Midnight Sun Festival, a 1977 on-set TV program, and an essay by Leo Goldsmith (Keywords in Subversive Film.) A curious and deceptively entertaining film experience. Absolutely recommended!

text:
🚀 “Alpha Hunt” (Value Discovery) Series #003/100: $SPCX 

I am bullish on SpaceX and am seriously considering acquiring a stake in the coming days. This has nothing to do with Elon Musk making a Tesla “fly.” While I must admit that watching the new Tesla Roadster pull off those wild aerial maneuvers yesterday was impressive—and learning that SpaceX engineers contributed to the underlying technology makes it all the more intriguing—let’s be clear: I would never invest in a company valued at nearly $2 trillion simply because someone sent a sports car into the air. That’s a brilliant PR stunt, not an investment thesis.

My interest in SpaceX stems from its much grander vision. I believe many investors still view it merely as a “rocket company”—which, frankly, overlooks the most valuable part of its business. Starlink is evolving into a global communications platform, and the data speaks for itself. By the end of Q2 2026, Starlink reached 12 million subscribers—doubling its user base from the previous year. Its connectivity business generated $4.29 billion in quarterly revenue (up 66% year-over-year) with an operating profit of approximately $1.66 billion. These are substantial figures. Even more compelling is that SpaceX controls the vast majority of its own infrastructure: they manufacture their own satellites, launch them using their own rockets, and provide connectivity services directly to the end user. For most other satellite companies, replicating this entire ecosystem would require such massive capital investment that it is effectively impossible.

Furthermore, I believe Starlink’s potential extends far beyond providing internet access to remote areas. Over the next decade, sectors such as aviation and maritime communications, military applications, and “direct-to-cell” services are poised to become major growth engines. SpaceX is already actively securing wireless spectrum; I believe this will ultimately position Starlink as a highly competitive player within the telecommunications industry. I am not suggesting that industry giants like Verizon or AT&T will suddenly vanish—that would be absurd. However, I do believe that satellite connectivity will play a far more significant role in the future global communications market than most investors currently anticipate.

Then, of course, there is their launch business. Reusable rockets are not just an impressive engineering feat; they offer a distinct economic advantage. Each successful launch using reusable rockets allows SpaceX to deploy its satellites more efficiently, expand the reach of "Starlink," and potentially lower the operating costs of the entire network. This advantage would become even more pronounced if "Starship" eventually achieves rapid, reliable reusability. Furthermore, SpaceX is expanding into artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, opening up yet another potential growth avenue. The company reported $7.8 billion in revenue for the second quarter—a 92% year-over-year increase. For a company of this scale, such a growth rate is truly remarkable.

Before anyone labels me a "die-hard Elon Musk fan," I should clarify: there are aspects of SpaceX that concern me. The company posted a net loss of $541 million last quarter, and its capital expenditures are immense. Whether it’s the expansion into AI, the development of "Starship," or the build-out of the satellite network, all require massive investment. Based on a price of approximately $148.62 per share, SpaceX’s valuation as of yesterday stood at roughly $2 trillion—a valuation that, even for an exceptional company, could be considered quite "demanding." Additionally, the average revenue per user (ARPU) for Starlink has declined, meaning that growth in user numbers alone is not enough to justify such "blind optimism." I would like to see stronger cash flow, greater capital efficiency, and evidence that these new ventures can achieve sustainable profitability.

So, where do I stand? I remain bullish—and I certainly don’t intend to just add $SPCX to a watchlist and forget about it. I am actively considering establishing an initial position, potentially within the next few trading sessions or sometime next week. I have not made a purchase yet, as I am waiting for an entry price that justifies the level of risk involved. After nearly 30 years in the markets, I know all too well that loving a company is entirely different from loving its stock price. However, should a sufficiently compelling opportunity arise, I am ready to act. When that happens, I will share the actual price at which I enter.

I believe SpaceX has the potential to become one of the most significant infrastructure companies of the next decade. This isn’t because Elon Musk might make cars fly, but because he has built an integrated ecosystem—encompassing satellite communications, launch capabilities, and technical infrastructure—that would be extremely difficult for any competitor to replicate.

**My Stance: BULLISH. Not yet invested, but seriously considering establishing a position soon.**

text:
The offer heard around the world. 

In August 2026, a court filing confirmed Google paid $10 million for Spirit Airlines' data.

Not the airline. Not the routes, the planes, or the brand. Just the data. A company that had gone through bankruptcy, whose physical assets were being picked apart, still had something worth eight figures to one of the largest AI labs in the world.

Most people read that story as a bankruptcy footnote. It's actually a window into how seriously labs are treating data acquisition right now.

The public number you hear most often is that Anthropic spends about $1 billion a year on data. That figure is technically accurate. It's also the smallest honest way to describe the market. Estimates from people inside lab procurement put the real number at $5 to $10 billion per lab per year when you count everything that qualifies as data spend. Seven or eight labs are operating at that scale.

When you're spending at that level, buying a company outright for its records is a strategic procurement decision.

The implication for owners of established businesses is straightforward. The records sitting inside your company, the emails, the workflows, the years of decisions documented across your systems, were built to run your business. They have a second use that didn't exist five years ago. Labs need what you already have.

Most owners find this out by accident, years after the window for their vertical opened. A few find out early enough to do something about it.

If you want to understand what your records might be worth before someone else figures it out first, start at https://t.co/tfu80JG0S4.

🗣️ “With all due respect to Cristiano Ronaldo, I think there is a difference between believing you are the best and allowing your football to demonstrate why you deserve that recognition.

Being a complete footballer also involves creating chances for others, controlling games, dictating the tempo, dribbling past opponents, making the right decisions under pressure and making your entire team better.

“And when I look at Lionel Messi, I see a player who has demonstrated those qualities at the highest level for nearly two decades.

“Look at what Messi has achieved. Eight Ballon d’Or awards. The FIFA World Cup. Multiple Copa América titles. Four Champions League trophies. Numerous domestic league titles, individual awards and records. He has won almost everything a footballer could dream of winning.

“What impresses me most is that Messi has never needed to convince the world of his greatness every time someone questions him. He steps onto the pitch and lets his football answer.

“Of course, Messi has had difficult matches, just as Cristiano has. No footballer plays perfectly every week. But when we discuss the greatest players in history, we must examine more than goals and personal records. We must look at the complete picture: influence, creativity, vision, consistency, trophies and the ability to change a game in ways that statistics cannot fully explain.

“Cristiano is one of the greatest goalscorers this sport has ever seen. His dedication, mentality and longevity deserve enormous respect. But being an incredible goalscorer and being the most complete footballer in history are two different arguments.

“And if we are discussing the greatest overall career, how can we ignore the World Cup? Messi has reached the summit of international football and lifted the biggest trophy the game offers.

“For me, greatness is not determined by how loudly you declare it. It is demonstrated by what you contribute to the game, what you achieve with your team and the memories you leave behind.

“I respect Cristiano Ronaldo, but I will never agree that scoring goals alone settles the debate. Messi’s ability to score, create, dribble, assist, dictate play and decide matches is why I consider him the more complete footballer.

“You can argue about who scores more goals, but when you look at football as a whole, Lionel Messi has a case that goes far beyond statistics.”

text:
Dolly Parton’s offer came with a catch: you could earn $500 for graduating, but your buddy had to graduate too.

The country singer wanted more children in her home county of Sevier, Tennessee, to finish high school. Her foundation, established in 1988, introduced its Buddy Program in 1991, pairing students and giving them a reason to look out for one another.

Both students would receive the money if both completed school. Suddenly, getting to graduation was something a pair could work toward together. A friend had a stake in whether you kept going.

The Dollywood Foundation reports that the dropout rate for the participating classes fell from 35% to 6%. The agreement made each student’s reward depend on a friend reaching the finish line too.

Parton began with students in seventh and eighth grades. They had years of school ahead of them, and a written promise to help each other get through it.

Parton’s education work later grew to include the Imagination Library, which sends books to young children. The Buddy Program addressed a different point in that journey: teenagers who were already in school and needed a reason, and some encouragement, to stay.

Before the books reached millions of children, there were two students with a shared promise: finish together.

Sources: The Dollywood Foundation; Imagination Library.

text:
Day 2 at #TACUSPA2026 brought big ideas, bold conversations, and incredible connections!

From building stronger intergenerational teams to reimagining career readiness, leveraging AI and leading through change, one theme kept rising to the top: people are at the heart of everything we do in higher education.

Dr. Justin McLaughlin challenged us to replace assumptions with curiosity and see generational differences as opportunities for collaboration. Other sessions explored how intentional technology, meaningful reflection, and competency-based learning strengthen career readiness, and how making the hidden curriculum visible helps first-generation students thrive.

We also dug into AI with purpose: streamlining administrative work so student affairs professionals have more time for what matters most, connecting with students.

Dr. Keith Edwards and the Student Affairs NOW panel reminded us that leadership isn’t a title. It’s about building trust, embracing change, and creating opportunities for others to grow.

Congratulations to this year’s award recipients!
- Outstanding New Professional Award: Julian Samarripas, @Trinity_U
- Mid-Level Student Affairs Professional Award: Dr. La’Cresha Moore, @unthealth
- Dissertation of the Year Award: Dr. Shanté Hearst, @tamu
- Faculty Member of the Year Award: Dr. Gabriela Silvestre, @samhoustonstate
- Dr. Adam Peck Research Development Grant: Molly Crespo, @lamaruniversity
- James E. Caswell Distinguished Service Award: Dr. Daniel Maxwell

We also celebrated the Thomas Moorman Fellows, graduate scholarship recipients, and innovative research advancing student success, experiential learning, and career readiness.

 Dr. Maxwell's reflections on nearly four decades in student affairs offered a powerful reminder that our greatest impact isn't measured by awards, but by the lives we touch, the relationships we build, and the opportunities we create for others.

It was great to spend more time with Kim and Texas A&M Community Engagement, including the newly formed #AggielandServes Ambassadors led by student leaders Ella Claire and Tanya. Gig ’em, Aggies! We’re looking forward to partnering with, volunteering with, and serving alongside @tamu, @cityofcs, @CityofBryan, and the broader Brazos County community.

Plus, we got the chance to catch up with @TACUSPA leaders Shelby Hearn and Dr. Lacey Folsom, and close the day with food and fellowship at the President’s Reception, hosted by the Office of the Vice President for Student Affairs at Texas A&M.

Our biggest takeaway? Technology can help us scale our work, but it’s the relationships, experiences, and opportunities we create that drive meaningful impact. We’re proud to be part of a community committed to engagement, belonging, and student success.

At GivePulse, we're energized by the incredible work happening across campuses and proud to be part of a community committed to engagement, belonging, and student success.

Here's to more learning, collaboration, and turning great ideas into action!

text:
Good morning, my amazing X family! ☕️❤️

It's Friday!

On this day in 1987, the world watched as 18 month old Jessica McClure, known as Baby Jessica, was rescued after spending 58 hours trapped 22 feet underground in a narrow well in Texas.

For nearly three days, rescuers worked tirelessly while millions of people hoped and prayed for a miracle.

And on October 16, she was finally brought to safety.

What a beautiful reminder of what humanity can accomplish when we come together, put our differences aside, and refuse to give up on someone.

Sometimes the greatest things we accomplish in life aren't for ourselves. They're for someone who needs us.

So maybe today, be someone's hope. Offer a helping hand. Show a little kindness. You never know how much of a difference you might make in someone's life.

Have an amazing Friday, everyone! ❤️

text:
Elon Musk Says Tesla Roadster Will Finally Enter Production in 2028

Tesla has unveiled its long-delayed next-generation Roadster, and Elon Musk says the company now plans to begin production in 2028.

At the October 15 event at SpaceX’s facility in Texas, Tesla demonstrated a redesigned Roadster equipped with technology developed alongside SpaceX. The car used cold-gas thrusters and aerodynamic systems to perform unusual maneuvers, including lifting off the ground and moving through the air during the demonstration. (TechCrunch)

When asked when customers would actually get the car, Musk replied, “We enter production in 2028. Actually.” The remark drew attention because the second-generation Roadster was first unveiled in 2017 and has been delayed multiple times. (Elon Musk Archive)

Tesla says the Roadster will be offered in multiple configurations, including higher-performance versions using SpaceX-inspired thruster technology. The company has also reopened reservations, although final pricing and delivery timing remain subject to change. (TechCrunch)

For now, 2028 is Tesla’s official production target, but given the Roadster’s long history of delays, customers may still want to treat the timeline cautiously.

Would you wait until 2028 for the new Tesla Roadster?

THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT MUST TAKE IMMEDIATE ACTION TO ENSURE THE LIFE AND SAFETY OF INDIAN SEAFARERS!

STATEMENT

Subject: Request to ensure the safety, rescue and legal rights of Indian seafarers working on cargo ships in the maritime regions of the Middle East and other countries worldwide — reg.

The prevailing war-related tensions, armed attacks and risks of ships being seized in international maritime routes, including the Middle East, the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, pose a serious threat to the lives and safety of Indian seafarers working on cargo ships.

Seafarers play a vital role in India’s economy and international trade. Protecting their lives, health, wages, occupational safety and the welfare of their families is an important responsibility of the Government of India.

LEGAL FRAMEWORK FOR ACTION

1. Article 21 of the Constitution of India

In accordance with the constitutional principles protecting the right to life and personal liberty, necessary measures must be taken to ensure the safety of Indian seafarers.

2. Merchant Shipping Act, 2025

Action must be taken under the applicable provisions and rules concerning the safety, welfare, employment rights and relief for abandoned seafarers.

3. Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 (MLC, 2006)

Ensure that seafarers’ working conditions, medical assistance, wages and repatriation rights are protected in accordance with the obligations applicable to the flag State of the vessel and the relevant legal framework.

4. International Maritime Safety Regulations

Ensure that vessel security measures, risk alerts, emergency response plans and maritime safety procedures are properly implemented.

5. Consular Assistance by the Ministry of External Affairs

Provide emergency assistance, coordinate rescue operations, offer legal guidance and extend financial assistance, subject to eligibility, through Indian embassies and consulates to Indian seafarers stranded in dangerous situations abroad.

DEMANDS TO THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT

1. Continuous Safety Monitoring

Continuously monitor the safety and security status of Indian seafarers working in hazardous maritime regions.

2. Rescue and Emergency Coordination

Coordinate with the relevant countries, shipping companies, the Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard to rescue seafarers facing life-threatening situations.

3. Emergency Helplines and Communication

Establish safety alerts, emergency helplines and 24-hour communication facilities.

4. Legal Action on Complaints

Take appropriate legal action on complaints relating to unpaid wages, denial of medical assistance, shortages of food and drinking water, and abandonment of seafarers on board vessels.

5. Assistance to Families

Assist the families of missing or deceased seafarers in obtaining information, legal assistance, insurance benefits and applicable relief.

6. Accountability of Shipping Companies and Recruitment Agencies

Ensure that shipping companies and recruitment agencies deploying seafarers to high-risk regions comply with the relevant laws and government safety guidelines.

CONCLUSION

The lives and safety of Indian seafarers must not be neglected merely because they work in foreign maritime regions.

Therefore, the Union Ministry of External Affairs, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, and the Directorate General of Shipping must work in coordination and take immediate, practical and lawful measures to safeguard the lives, safety and rights of Indian seafarers.

text:
Between Guadalcanal and Iwo Jima, only one enlisted Marine in the Second World War would earn both the Medal of Honor and the Navy Cross. That man was John Basilone of Raritan, New Jersey.

In October 1942 on Guadalcanal he commanded two sections of heavy machine guns for the 1st Battalion, 7th Marines. When one section was cut down to two men still able to fight, he shifted guns into place, repaired another, and ran ammunition through cut supply lines under fire. The citation credited him with at least 38 enemy dead.

Home meant a parade that filled LIFE magazine and a war bond tour. Offered an officer's commission, he refused. He wanted to return to the line.

Training at Camp Pendleton, he married Lena Riggi, a sergeant in the Marine Corps Women's Reserve. On February 19, 1945, day one on Iwo Jima, he climbed a Japanese blockhouse pinning his company and wrecked it with grenades and demolitions, then led a tank clear of a minefield while under heavy fire. He fell at the edge of Airfield Number 1 at age 28.

Lena kept his name for the rest of her life.

Honor the Marine who went back.

🚨 HELL NO TO HILARIO DOMINGUEZ | 16 CHICAGO ALDERMEN CALL FOR AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATION!

LET’S TALK ABOUT THE BACKSTORY!

In 2017, Hilario Dominguez, a Chicago School Board presidential candidate endorsed by the Chicago Teachers Union (CTU), was accused of inappropriate conduct involving a 17-year-old CPS student working at The Resurrection Project, a Pilsen nonprofit.

The young woman alleged that Dominguez made inappropriate comments about her appearance and dating life, offered her rides home, and engaged in unwanted physical contact.

An internal complaint followed in 2018.

The CPS Office of Inspector General opened an investigation in 2021 and closed it in June 2026, finding insufficient evidence to substantiate the allegations.

BUT HERE’S WHERE THE QUESTIONS BEGIN!

The young woman said the investigation was closed without her being interviewed. Investigators reportedly attempted to contact her in 2022, but she said she was unaware of those attempts.

After she came forward publicly, the CPS Inspector General reopened the investigation in September 2026.

She was interviewed on September 22.

On October 14, the investigation was closed again, with no actionable finding of sexual misconduct or additional CPS policy violations.

Dominguez has denied wrongdoing.

BUT THE STORY DOESN’T END THERE!

During her interview with NBC 5 Chicago’s Mary Ann Ahern, the young woman described another encounter with Dominguez approximately three to four years ago.

She said she was working as a waitress when Dominguez approached her, hugged her, and asked:

“WE’RE GOOD, RIGHT?”

According to her account, she felt unable to react because she was at work and did not want to cause a scene.

Her reaction was disbelief: “Are you serious?”

This alleged encounter occurred years after the original incidents she described from when she was 17 years old.

🚨 OCTOBER 15, 2026 — 16 CHICAGO ALDERMEN SPEAK OUT!

Sixteen Chicago aldermen issued a joint statement calling for an independent investigation into the CPS Office of Inspector General’s handling of the matter.

They questioned whether the investigation was rushed to meet a political deadline publicly demanded by Mayor Brandon Johnson, who has supported Dominguez.

The aldermen are calling on Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul and/or CPS to appoint independent counsel.

The young woman’s attorney has also requested an independent review.

AND LET’S NOT FORGET THE CTU ENDORSEMENT!

The Chicago Teachers Union endorsed Dominguez for Chicago School Board president in June 2026.

CTU has defended Dominguez, maintaining that the investigation was thorough and that its findings support his denial of wrongdoing.

But the concerns surrounding the investigation and the young woman’s account deserve serious examination.

IN THE END… IT’S STILL A HELL NO TO HILARIO DOMINGUEZ!

This is about protecting students, respecting individuals who come forward with allegations, and ensuring that investigations are conducted independently and thoroughly.

The public deserves transparency, accountability, and confidence in the institutions responsible for protecting Chicago’s children.

HERE’S CFR QUESTION:

If 16 Chicago aldermen and the alleged victim’s attorney are questioning the integrity of this investigation, why shouldn’t the public demand an independent review before this matter is considered closed?

Here is a comprehensive, professional, and factual analysis of Tesla’s (TSLA) stock outlook, structured for clear communication and strategic insight.
​Tesla (TSLA) Stock Outlook: Navigating the Shift from EV Pure-Play to AI & Autonomous Ecosystem
​Tesla stands at a critical strategic crossroad. As the company transitions from a traditional automotive manufacturer into an artificial intelligence and robotics enterprise, market sentiments remain polarized. Below is a deep-dive analysis of the core drivers, financial metrics, and risks shaping Tesla's outlook.  
​1. Core Growth Catalysts (The Bull Case)
​Autonomous Driving & Cybercab Deployment:
The long-term valuation anchor for Tesla relies heavily on its Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology and the commercialization of Robotaxis (Cybercabs). Successful scaling of autonomous ride-hailing networks could unlock high-margin recurring software revenue, shifting Tesla’s financial profile closer to a tech-platform model.  
​AI, Robotics, and Energy Infrastructure:
Beyond vehicles, heavy investments in the Optimus humanoid robot, AI training chips, and Energy Storage systems (Megapack) are viewed as high-growth pillars. Energy storage, in particular, offers massive diversification potential despite periodic supply-chain or leadership adjustments.  
​Resilient Delivery Metrics:
Recent quarterly delivery reports have shown solid execution, occasionally beating consensus expectations and demonstrating that consumer demand remains resilient amidst broader macroeconomic headwinds.  
​2. Key Headwinds & Financial Pressures (The Bear Case)
​Margin Compression & Core Automotive Pressures:
While vehicle deliveries remain steady, automotive gross margins (excluding regulatory credits) face continuous pressure from global price competition, shifting EV subsidies, and rising production costs. Maintaining stable long-term margins without one-time regulatory credit boosts remains a core concern for institutional analysts.  
​Heightened Capital Expenditures (Capex):
Tesla’s aggressive spending—projected to exceed $25 billion to fund Cybercabs, Optimus, and advanced AI facilities—has temporarily pressured free cash flow, raising questions about capital efficiency in the near term.  
​Regulatory and Compliance Scrutiny:
The rapid deployment of autonomous features and Cybercabs has drawn increased regulatory oversight (such as NHTSA inquiries regarding self-certification and safety compliance), which could introduce rollout delays in key markets like the U.S. and Europe.  
​3. Valuation and Market Consensus
​Analyst Price Targets: Wall Street consensus 12-month price targets hover around the $395 to $425 range, reflecting a balanced view between near-term auto sector stagnation and long-term AI upside.  
​Trading Multiples: Tesla continues to trade at a high Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio relative to legacy automakers, justified by investors who treat it as a high-growth tech and AI innovator rather than a pure car manufacturer.  
​Summary Action Plan for Investors
​Key Takeaway: Tesla is currently a high-conviction, high-volatility growth asset. Investors should weigh near-term margin and regulatory risks against the multi-year potential of autonomous software and robotics.  
​Monitor Upcoming Earnings: Closely track automotive gross margins excluding regulatory credits and updates on free cash flow during upcoming earnings releases.  
​Track Regulatory Milestones: Watch for updates regarding FSD regulatory approvals in international markets (such as the EU) and resolutions on U.S. autonomous safety reviews.  
​Evaluate Risk Tolerance: Given the stock's sensitivity to macroeconomic sentiment and tech-sector rotations, ensure position sizing aligns with a long-term investment horizon (3–5+ years).

How serious is @amazon about customer service?  READ THIS to understand just how bad they have become:

I purchased a cover/sunshade for a high end drone, "FlySimple" brand from the FHBL Tech Store on Amazon for $34.99. Not a bad price, and it included the shoulder strap. The fun part begins:

Amazon decided to fire all of their English speaking customer service represenattives, and has even moved away from their customer support centers in Mumbai (who do not speak clearly and make everything more difficult), replacing customer service with artificial intelligence.  However, Amazon failed to properly prepare their AI to understand what the phrase "There are parts missing from this item." The AI suggests contacting the seller, but since I had already exhausted a half hour attempting to find a way to contact the seller (including in the sales record where the AI was instructing me to look), I had to tell the AI several times that its proposed solution was irrelevant because there is no link to contact the seller on this transaction record.  The AI then instructed me to CONTACT AMAZON CUSTOMER SERVICE for a solution.  I know this sounds weird being that AI is all rthat Amazon offers for customer service, but I clicked the "Contact Customer Support" link since that seemed to be my only option.

The link directed me to Amazon's AUTOMATED customer service. The automated customer service is different than the AI, as it asks a question then, instead of taking your natural and specific response, gives a multiple choice option for several possible issues that buyers may encounter on Amazon purchases, but, of course, "item is missing parts" is not one of these options, rendering ALL options irrelevant and useless.

Since Amazon and this negligent seller fail to provide any assistance whatsoever for missing parts or even contacting the seller, I proceeded to start the return process, returning the item as defective. I was unable to detail any other issues (missing parts) because the process lacks any way to explain what the actual problem is.  Amazon's system accepted the full return for full refund, all I have to do is return the item.

"Click here for return label and instructions."

Long story short on this chapter, this seller and Amazon only accept returns if the return is DELIVERED to a FEDEX OFFICE STORE, the nearest of which is just over a half hour away from my shopp NOT on my way home. I now fully understand just how pathetically little (not at all) that Amazon cares for the purchaser's experience, time, resources, and frustration as well as the accuracy of orders and timely delivery. It's all a joke to them.

Amazon is now BLACKLISTED for ALL PURCHASES with all of the comapnies and affiliates we work with. Amazon has had FOUR years to straighten out their operation since it went to shit, and instead they instituted an irrelevant AI to replace customer service that just plain made everything worse.

text:
GED STORIES
                          
                        BUS RIDES

 Bruce Lee once said “Mistakes are forgivable if one has the courage to admit them.”

Growing up in a poor neighborhood on the inner city as a kid was rough. I still knew I wanted an education though. At some point in time my friend Mike and his mother helped me get enrolled at a school with Boeing called Opportunity Skyway.
 
The school offered apprenticeship and job training opportunities, that paid students to learn about, and work on planes. There were some Cessna’s and small helicopters at the school that I can remember. 

The school also offered the options and tools needed to get high school diplomas, or GED’s. However I only went to get my GED. The rest of my energy was spent on other activities. 
 
I used to ride bus 150 from Auburn into Seattle. If I was in FederalWay I could catch one of numerous busses next to what was then known as the “Sea-Tac Mall”. I always got off the bus in Seattle next to City Light to transfer busses.
  
The first time I ventured into City Light I was looking for a restroom, but what I found was a break room located extremely close to the entrance of the building. 
 
Being that I was on drugs, and homeless at the time, I was hungry. The fridge had food in it, and every time I went to school I was able to eat.
 
It may not have been the most honest thing to do, and if anyone at City Light ever reads this, I apologize for stealing your food. Just know that it wasn’t wasted, and I think you did a good thing. 
 
The bus that picked me up just outside of City Light was the only transfer. A short ride past the old boot and hat before getting off and walking the rest of the way. 
 
Taking a standard GED “practice test”, to test your skills at the school, was available and encouraged for all students, but because the bus rides took up such a good portion of my day, and because I’m arrogant, I never once took a “practice test”.
 
There were however, two problems with taking an actual test at the time:
1. Testing wasn’t done at the school
2. Tests cost money
 
The teacher at the school was a very generous Christian, sort of light skinned brother. He would not only drive me to where the tests were taken, he would also pay for the tests. 

I don’t remember his name, but if you ever read this I want you to know that your actions in my eyes were very *admirable*,

AD•MI•RA•BLE
:deserving to be admired : very good
:deserving the highest esteem : excellent

Because of your kindness I was able to get an education. I pray that your strong values as a Christian and a teacher will be remembered, and that your family and future generations may be blessed. 
 
The only test I can remember taking (odd enough) is the written test. I only remember it because the test itself involved writing an essay about a famous person I would most like to meet.
  
It sounded like a stupid question to me. I made up some crap about wanting to meet Michael Jackson, and how he was the “king of pop” and “so awesome”, etc. 
 
The writing test, and all of the others, I passed easily. I only think all of this is relevant because for the last few days I’ve been listening to various versions of “Man In The Mirror” on the internet.

text:
📌 🇺🇸🇮🇳 Why is US Secretary of State Rubio heading to Ambani’s Jamnagar refinery ? Energy, trade —or a bigger corporate play ?

The faltering Iran war, increasingly backfiring on the Trump administration, is intensifying global energy-market risks, while the Ukraine war and sanctions continue to complicate global oil and fuel supplies. 

In a striking policy adjustment, the US President Donald Trump has authorised limited transactions involving Russian-origin diesel to ease America’s fuel-price squeeze. The relief is real, but its scale remains uncertain.

Jamnagar matters because it converts crude into globally traded fuels. Reliance has processed Russian crude, including Urals, although its two refineries have different roles and sourcing patterns. Its export-oriented refinery previously said it had stopped processing Russian crude. Not every diesel cargo from Jamnagar can be assumed to originate from Russian oil.

There is another twist : Washington is reshaping Venezuelan oil access, while Reliance has obtained a US licence to buy Venezuelan crude directly. 

The Trump administration is also directing Venezuelan oil towards US refining. This is about supply security, refinery economics and commercial leverage —not American dependence on Ambani.

Rubio meets India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar in Mumbai on October 20, with broader India–US trade and investment negotiations also in play.

The timing is striking : Washington is tightening scrutiny of Indian IT workers even as Rubio heads to Reliance’s industrial heartland. Elon Musk has publicly challenged Mukesh Ambani’s alleged influence over Starlink’s delayed Indian rollout. But there is no evidence that Ambani engineered this visit or that Rubio intends to raise Starlink with him.

America is diversifying its options, not seeking a saviour. Jamnagar offers scale and commercial opportunity. The real test is whether India converts Washington’s interest into reciprocal gains —or merely helps it manage the consequences of its own geopolitical choices.

text:
Danielle Smith and the Abuse of Public Trust

Alberta belongs to its people and its premier must answer for putting its future in play

Imagine a regional executive who spends years telling everyone that head office is the source of the company’s troubles. She cultivates a special relationship with its most powerful customer, publicly rules out using an important bargaining tool against that customer, and then asks employees whether the division should begin a process that could lead to leaving the company.

The board would demand an accounting of her judgment. It would want to know whose interests she was serving and what risks she had created for everyone else.

Albertans should demand that accounting from Danielle Smith before October 19.

We do not need to establish what Smith secretly believes about separation to judge what she has publicly done. She says she supports Alberta remaining in Canada. Take that statement seriously. Then examine the machinery her government has put in motion and ask whether her conduct measures up to her assurance.

In my view, the abuse of public trust lies in making Alberta’s constitutional future an instrument of political management. A premier has every right to challenge Ottawa. She owes the public an explanation when that challenge becomes a government-organized route toward another vote on leaving the country.

The signature is only the beginning

Orders in Council deserve scrutiny, but precision matters. They are established legal instruments used for regulations, appointments and other government decisions. Issuing one while the legislature is not sitting does not, by itself, establish misconduct. These are formal exercises of executive authority, not merely personal memos from the premier. [1]

The serious questions concern the authority used, the substance of the decision and the accountability that follows. What did cabinet authorize? Why was that course necessary? What alternatives did ministers consider? What public explanation accompanied the decision?

The referendum orders identified by Elections Alberta are O.C. 109/2026 and 110/2026, approved March 31, and O.C. 160/2026, approved May 28. Those dates and documents give us something concrete to examine. [2]

A branch manager may have authority to sign a document. That does not settle whether the decision serves the people whose interests she was entrusted to protect. Lawful authority carries a responsibility to justify its use.

Smith should be judged on that responsibility.

The double message is in the public record

In her May 21 address, Smith declared her support for remaining in Canada. In the same address, she attacked the court decision concerning the separatist petition, acknowledged that it remained binding pending a successful appeal, and announced an additional referendum question intended to proceed while that legal dispute continued. She described a route that would seek support for commencing the process toward a binding separation referendum. [3]

That sequence deserves scrutiny even from people who accept her stated preference for Canada. A premier can sincerely favour staying and still exercise profoundly poor judgment by putting departure into play.

Consider the executive who assures the board that she wants the enterprise to succeed while arranging a vote about beginning the process of dismantling her division’s relationship with it. Her assurances do not erase her responsibility for the uncertainty she creates.

This is the double message Albertans should challenge: confidence in Canada from the podium, a government-created pathway toward a separation referendum on the ballot.

Smith’s government owns that choice. It cannot explain away executive decisions as though cabinet were merely watching events unfold.

A ballot should reveal consent clearly

That responsibility extends to the meaning her government assigns to voters’ answers. Consent to a particular proposal cannot reasonably become an endorsement of everything it subsequently chooses to do.

October 19 is not a direct vote to leave Canada. Question 10 offers a choice between remaining and commencing the legal process toward a binding referendum on separation. Its own result is non-binding. Voters select between two options; it is not another yes-or-no question. [2]

That distinction matters because a voter might support another referendum to express anger at Ottawa while opposing independence itself. Political leaders must not later treat those different intentions as interchangeable.

The closing days of this campaign have sharpened the debate over the other nine questions. Prime Minister Mark Carney has urged Albertans to reject the immigration and constitutional proposals. Smith is advocating support for them. Their disagreement deserves scrutiny on its substance, rather than becoming another test of whether someone stands with Alberta or Ottawa. [12][13]

Consider the ballot’s construction. Question 1 combines increased immigration control, lower immigration, economic priorities and employment preferences. Question 4 describes a proposed fee as reasonable without specifying an amount in the question. A voter can agree with one part of a package and reject another. Describing an unspecified charge as reasonable supplies a favourable judgment before voters know its amount. [4]

Imagine a board asking shareholders to approve a motion containing several different business decisions, with management’s preferred description built into the wording. A responsible director would insist on separating the choices and identifying the consequences.

Albertans deserve the same respect.

A person might favour stronger provincial participation in immigration decisions while rejecting restrictions on services. Another might support a particular fee while opposing the government’s constitutional agenda. Those are distinct positions. Each deserves to be represented honestly after the ballots are counted.

Having several questions is not, by itself, evidence of manipulation. Combining their results into a sweeping political endorsement would be. My concern is that a majority on one proposal could be presented as public approval of a much larger confrontation with Ottawa.

The government’s own referendum website frames its proposals through provincial strength, sovereignty and Canadian unity. Those are powerful appeals, but they do not establish that the particular measures are necessary, effective or fair. [14]

A voter can love Alberta and reject the government’s proposals. A voter can support Canada and demand better federal policy. Neither position requires personal allegiance to Danielle Smith.

Precision also matters when discussing authority. Immigration is constitutionally shared between Ottawa and the provinces, with federal law prevailing in the event of a conflict under section 95. Alberta has a legitimate role. Its premier must still explain the legal boundaries of what she proposes and the cooperation required to achieve it. [15]

The constitutional questions seek changes involving judicial selection, the Senate, federal program funding and conflicts between provincial and federal laws. A provincial vote cannot, by itself, deliver those constitutional changes. The government should explain what each result would authorize politically, what it could accomplish legally, and what further decisions would remain. [5]

Smith should state, before the vote, how she will interpret mixed results. Which proposals would she pursue? What further scrutiny would they receive? What would she accept as a refusal?

Albertans own their answers. The premier does not get to enlarge them after the fact.

Elections Alberta must administer the design

The government’s political choices have practical consequences for the people running the vote. Elections Alberta announced ten separate ballots, estimated approximately 34 million ballots would be used, and anticipated needing at least 60,000 election officers. It described a hand-counting process proceeding question by question. [6]

These are substantial administrative demands. They do not establish that the vote is compromised. They establish that cabinet’s design requires staffing, clear instructions, accessible voting and patience from the public.

Elections Alberta also says it may not interpret the government’s questions. Voters seeking their meaning are directed to the government or their MLA. [2]

That places a particular obligation on the politicians who chose the wording. They must explain it plainly. Election workers should not become the targets of frustration over a political design they did not create.

Mar a Lago and the price of access

The same obligation to account for executive judgment applies to Smith’s dealings with the United States.

Smith met Donald Trump at Mar-a-Lago in January 2025 and subsequently gave a public account emphasizing energy and the threat of tariffs. It would be inaccurate to say she told Albertans nothing. The proper question is whether the accounting was sufficient. [7]

What records exist of the discussions? Who participated? Were any undertakings proposed, accepted or rejected? What follow-up occurred? How was Alberta’s approach coordinated with Canada’s negotiating position?

Those are questions for disclosure. The meeting itself does not prove a secret bargain.

But access is not evidence of influence. When a powerful customer threatens your business, a photograph at his property does not tell the board whether you improved its position.

On January 15, 2025, Smith declined to join the other first ministers’ statement and publicly opposed energy export tariffs and cutting off oil and gas exports in retaliation. Protecting Alberta producers is an intelligible objective. Publicly removing bargaining options also gives the other side useful information about the limits of a united response. [8]

What competent sales manager advertises those limits before the negotiation is settled?

Alberta has something America wants. In July 2026, U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra said the United States needed an additional three to four million barrels of oil daily over the following decade and identified Canada as a strong potential supplier. That was his assessment, not a guaranteed purchase commitment. [9]

The business lesson is straightforward: demand for our resources creates potential leverage. Additional market access can strengthen a seller’s choices, although any project must justify its costs. Alberta’s resource policy should be assessed by the value it delivers to Albertans, rather than the warmth of a relationship with an American president.

The half trillion dollar question

Jeffrey Rath’s reported discussions about US$500 billion in financing for an independent Alberta demand serious scrutiny. They do not amount to an approved loan. In January, Rath characterized financing discussions as hypothetical and denied soliciting or receiving foreign funds; American officials said no commitments had been made. Smith also said the United States should respect Canadian sovereignty. [10]

Hoekstra later denied that the administration was meeting or strategizing with Alberta separatists. [11]

These accounts require clarification. They provide no basis for asserting that Smith authorized Rath’s activities or that Washington controls her government.

They do provide ample reason to demand a clear public boundary. Has anyone in the Alberta government received separatist financing proposals, briefings or draft agreements? Have officials discussed the terms with proponents or American representatives? Will the government disclose any such contacts?

Imagine private advocates approaching your company’s largest customer about financing a breakup of the enterprise. Management should establish what happened and whether anyone claimed to speak for the company.

A financing proposal of that scale would invite questions about repayment, security, control and conditions. Calling a future state independent would not answer them. Albertans deserve to know what obligations anyone proposes in their name.

The premier must answer

Before October 19, Smith owes Albertans a plain account of the referendum’s intended consequences, the government’s relevant American contacts and its response to separatists exploring foreign financial support. She should also explain how her commitment to Canada governs the decisions she makes with the powers of her office.

Disagreement with Ottawa is legitimate. Albertans can demand better federal policy without giving any premier an unlimited mandate to put their future into play.

The business analogies have a limit: Alberta is not a branch office, and Canada is not a corporation. The obligation they illuminate is real. People entrusted with authority must answer for risks imposed on those they serve.

Alberta belongs to its people. Smith holds office on their behalf. Before they cast their ballots, she owes them answers clear enough to judge her use of that power.

Sources

[1] Government of Alberta — Orders in Council

[2] Elections Alberta — Referendum questions and orders

[3] Premier Smith — Address to the Province, May 21 2026

[4] Order in Council 110/2026 — Immigration and voting questions, available through Elections Alberta [2]

[5] Order in Council 109/2026 — Constitutional questions, available through Elections Alberta [2]

[6] Elections Alberta — Important Referendum Information, May 29 2026

[7] Daily Hive — Smith discusses her Trump visit, January 13 2025

[8] CityNews — Smith rejects joint tariff response statement, January 15 2025

[9] The Canadian Press via iPolitics — Hoekstra on oil supply, July 20 2026

[10] The Canadian Press via CityNews — Separatist contacts and financing claims, January 29 2026
