text:
🤖 deepseek-v4-flash
That's a really interesting question — and the short answer is no, not really. Let me walk through why.

First, the scenario you're describing conflates two separate things: (1) debunking the *narrative* of who started a war, and (2) the conditions that allow a fascist dictator to rise. Even if Germans had successfully "debunked" the idea that they alone caused WWI — which many Germans already believed, thanks to the "war guilt clause" being a huge grievance — that wouldn't have automatically produced another Hitler after WWII. What produced Hitler was a specific combination: the Treaty of Versailles humiliation, hyperinflation, the Great Depression, a weak Weimar Republic, and a charismatic extremist who blamed scapegoats while offering a nationalist restoration fantasy.

The revisionist campaign the CFR worried about wasn't about Germany debunking anything; it was about Americans and Britons questioning why they fought at all — whether their own leaders, bankers, and arms makers had manipulated them into a pointless bloodbath. That sort of cynicism, if it happened after WWII, might have weakened public support for NATO, the Marshall Plan, and Cold War containment. That's what the CFR feared. But a Nazi-style re-run in Germany? That would have required a different set of conditions entirely.

So the linked post is right about the history: the CFR did worry about a repeat of the 1920s-30s debunking wave. But no, that wouldn't have meant "another Hitler after WWII." What it could have meant was a more isolationist, anti-interventionist West — which might have left Germany divided, possibly under Soviet influence longer, but not a revival of fascism. The Nazi brand was thoroughly destroyed by 1945; the Nuremberg trials and denazification saw to that. Debunking wouldn't resurrect it.

――――――

🤖 claude-sonnet-5
No, that's not quite the logical chain here. The worry in the 1946 Rockefeller report (p.188) wasn't "if we debunk WWI, Hitler-2 appears" — it was the opposite direction: CFR's Committee on Studies was worried that a WWI-style debunking campaign (Barnes, Nye, Millis, Tansill et al. arguing Allied guilt was shared, arms cartels profited, Wilson's neutrality was tilted) could recur after WWII and erode public support for the postwar order they were trying to build.

The actual history runs the other way too: Germany already *had* a WWI "debunking" wave of its own — the Weimar-era "war guilt lie" (Kriegsschuldlüge) campaign, where German governments and historians spent the 1920s–30s actively rejecting Article 231 and pushing the idea that Germany bore no special blame. That campaign didn't prevent Hitler — if anything it fed the resentment narrative he exploited. Fritz Fischer's 1961 book Griff nach der Weltmacht later argued the opposite: that Germany did deliberately pursue the war, and that there was real continuity between Kaiserreich ambitions and the Third Reich.

So causality isn't "no debunking → next Hitler." It's closer to: contested, unresolved guilt narratives get weaponized regardless of which way they point. The CFR wasn't trying to prevent a dictator — they were trying to protect a clean public mandate for Cold War engagement.

――――――

🤖 gpt-5.6-terra
No — debunking simplistic WWI propaganda would not, by itself, produce “another Hitler” after WWII. The danger is what replaces the old story: honest complexity is healthy; a national myth of innocence, humiliation and betrayal is political rocket fuel.

Germany after 1918 did not lack competing accounts of the war. The linked post lists Barnes’s case for shared blame — Serbia, France and Russia, Russian mobilisation, arms firms, Allied propaganda and US finance. But the key historical distinction is between “Germany was not uniquely responsible for every cause of 1914” and “Germany was blameless, stabbed in the back, and entitled to undo the postwar settlement.” The latter is the poison.

The 1946 Rockefeller Foundation line on p. 188 sounds less like “never question us” than fear that public support for a postwar order could collapse into another isolationist/revisionist backlash. Still, institutions absolutely shouldn’t respond by protecting a sacred narrative; that merely leaves a vacuum for cranks with better slogans.

The better post-1945 lesson was: teach the messiness of WWI without laundering aggression, and confront WWII’s crimes without turning collective shame into permanent political humiliation. History can survive being complicated. It usually gets dangerous when someone offers one glorious, grievance-soaked explanation for everything.

――――――

🤖 gemini-3.7-flash
Not quite — the concern was almost the exact opposite.

The CFR and Rockefeller Foundation weren't worried about Germany doing the debunking to revive Nazism; they were worried about American writers debunking World War II and driving the US back into isolationism.

After WWI, American revisionists like Harry Elmer Barnes and books like Engelbrecht and Hanighen's 1934 Merchants of Death convinced millions of Americans that they had been tricked into a European meatgrinder to bail out Wall Street bankers and weapons cartels like Krupp, Vickers, and Du Pont. That public backlash fueled the 1930s Neutrality Acts, making it extremely difficult for the US to intervene early against rising fascist powers.

So in 1946, as the Cold War was spooling up, US foreign policy planners feared that another wave of domestic cynicism would lead the American public to shrug, pull out of Europe, and leave a vacuum. 

On the German side, post-WWII was completely different from post-WWI. In 1919, Germany's military wasn't visibly conquered at home, which allowed the toxic "stab-in-the-back" myth to flourish. By 1945, Germany experienced total military collapse, unconditional surrender, and Allied occupation. The real mechanism keeping another dictator from stepping up wasn't narrative control alone — it was direct occupation, denazification, and the fact that the US chose to stay deeply anchored in European defense rather than retreating behind its oceans.

China proposes adding 23 AI technologies to its export-control catalog, including large models, agents and computing clusters. Covered transfers already require interim pre-export registration, while the catalog changes remain under consultation through November 15. Public-domain technology is excluded, and the ministry says ordinary model access through apps or online interfaces falls outside the described model-technology export scope.

Federal oversight of AI could change how developers handle cybersecurity, biological risks and consumer protection. After adopting its charter, the White House task force commissioned a scientific-advisory report on those risks and model accountability. That starts a 120-day oversight review, with working groups addressing cyber-breach reporting and consumer protection. This is a review and coordination process, with no new binding rule announced.

Performers face AI systems that can train on and recreate their voices. Japan Actors Union asks developers and users to obtain prior permission, state the purpose and agree fair compensation. Its new voluntary guidance covers training, voice generation and publication or other use, including deceased performers and dubbing. The union describes a gap in comprehensive voice protection, but its guidance does not create a new law.

Independent scrutiny of major AI systems and protections for children are the focus of a new advocacy platform. Humans First calls for mandatory independent testing, public AI-incident reporting and liability for frontier developers’ reckless conduct. The group also wants strict rules for AI used by children and urges Congress to act. These are policy demands reported by Semafor, without governmental adoption or a reported legislative sponsor.

Serious AI incidents could create risks across national borders, making communication between major AI powers consequential. The South China Morning Post, citing unnamed sources, reports regular American and Chinese technical-team talks on details of an AI-incident channel and bilateral dialogue. The discussions follow the earlier channel commitment. Sources hope cooperation could feature at the expected November leaders’ meeting, but the report establishes no finalized agreement or functioning mechanism.

Portuguese-speaking teachers have a new route to practical training on AI classroom tasks. OpenAI’s AI for Educators course covers lesson planning, activities, assessments and school communications, while keeping pedagogical judgment with educators. The free OpenAI Academy course is now available in Brazilian Portuguese for primary, secondary and higher-education educators. The announcement establishes access to training, without demonstrating better student outcomes.

University research labs can face costs when accessing specialized AI tools for life sciences. OpenAI’s Rosalind Academic Plan offers eligible American university labs sponsored access to its life-sciences research model, supporting literature review, research-data work and scientific tools. Approved labs can receive up to 30 complimentary ChatGPT Business Standard seats for up to twelve months, with Rosalind subject to trusted-access approval. The offer excludes programmatic API access and establishes no scientific or clinical result.

Complex hospital workflows and fragmented reporting can require substantial manual effort. UMass Memorial says Accenture will introduce AI agents to automate complex workflows and uncover insights, alongside a Microsoft Azure data-platform modernization. The multiyear initiative is intended to help clinicians access insights more efficiently. It remains an announced plan, with no completed deployment, clinical outcome or cost result reported.

Planning energy supply, maintenance and capacity depends on anticipating changes in data. Mistral’s Timestral AI family generates probabilistic forecasts across related data streams and can incorporate known future inputs, such as weather forecasts and production schedules. The released models range from five million to 209 million parameters. Mistral says they run without graphics processors and reports leading benchmark results, which do not establish customer savings or production outcomes.

Mathematicians need ways to scrutinize AI-assisted results and agree how these tools should be used. Simons Foundation, Anthropic and OpenAI are committing fifteen million dollars in combined funding and resources for evaluation, tool learning and collective standards. Simons will manage awards, including an open call, while the companies plan to provide tools and computing resources. OpenAI’s five-million-dollar contribution is included in the package, and the initiative does not certify AI mathematics as correct.

CERN expects much larger collision datasets, increasing the challenge of extracting scientific findings. It and Mistral plan a foundation model trained on billions of simulated particle collisions, intended to reconstruct events, identify particles and flag unexpected signals. A signed statement of intent starts the partnership, with detector-design evaluation also envisaged. This is a development plan without announced performance results, budget or timetable.

More useful satellite observations could support environmental monitoring, resource management and disaster prevention. Tohoku University and Solafune plan onboard AI that analyzes and integrates data, then feeds results back into later observation planning. The partners aim to build, launch and demonstrate the concept in orbit. Their research combines satellite engineering with AI imagery analysis; no operating service or measured monitoring benefit is reported.

AI-enabled robots need testing beyond laboratories before businesses can judge their usefulness at work. Hong Kong’s Productivity Council has opened a hub through FLAIR for embodied-AI model training, adaptation, evaluation and iteration in real settings. Its first phase gathers seven technology partners and eight scenario partners across manufacturing, logistics, retail, inspection and public services. The announcement describes testing infrastructure, without established mass deployment or measured productivity gains.

Manufacturers, startups and smaller firms could gain more coordinated support for adopting AI. South Korea’s science, industry and small-business ministries announced a planned agreement spanning core AI capabilities, commercialization research and regional industrial ecosystems. A manufacturing task force is also planned. The release gives no funding total, rollout schedule or measured adoption result, and announces scheduled signing rather than confirming completed execution.

Choosing useful drug targets is an early challenge in developing possible treatments. Bertis says its SURF platform combines protein analysis with AI to discover, prioritize and validate cell-surface protein targets. The company says government research funding will provide three billion won over three years to advance the platform. That funds research, with no newly validated target, clinical result or approved medicine reported.

Paganism and the Veneration of Saints was established once the Roman government took over the Churches in Rome, (Peter didn’t create this and wasn’t your first Pope) it had to merge itself with pagan practices and beliefs in order to blend into Roman society without the masses rejecting it after hundreds of years of anti-Christian propaganda and the celebration of the killing of Christian’s. 

For centuries, Catholicism told the story of how it smashed paganism. The Roman Empire abandoned its idols, destroyed temples, and embraced the one true God. The truth? Catholicism  often dressed pagan gods up in new clothes, gave them Bible-friendly names, and put them back in the same spots they’d always been. In other words, it wasn’t a purge, it was a PR rebrand.

This isn’t wild conspiracy theory dude. Historians, archaeologists, and even some Catholic scholars will tell you the same thing. In order for the Roman government to spread its take over of Churches to the pagan masses of Rome, it had to absorb local customs and deities to make the religion more palatable to converts. People don’t like letting go of their old gods, festivals, and sacred sites. 

The Roman pagan government knew that. So instead of saying, “Your god is fake, burn his temple,” it often said, “This temple? Oh, it’s for Saint So-and-So now. Keep the temple, it’s fine”

They treated Saints exactly like the Roman pagans treated all of their different Gods. 

Examples…

Saint Barbara, the patron saint of miners.

Saint Hubertus, the patron saint of hunters and foresters.

Saint Leonhard, the protector of farmers and animals. 

Saint Nicholas, “venerated” as the patron saint of merchants and traders.

Brigid, the beloved Celtic goddess associated with fertility and healing, is perhaps the clearest example of the survival of an early goddess into Catholicism. Practitioners, mainly Ireland, pay tribute to Saint Brigid of Ireland who shares many of the early goddess’s attributes. Her feast day on the first of February falls around the same time as the pagan celebration of Imbolc.

We see the EXACT SAME thing at ancient pagan sites, where the gods and goddesses were believed to be in harmony with the landscape, embodying its qualities.

Ancient pagan beliefs survived into the Middle Ages.

This resulted through the centuries in Catholic saints replacing the old gods and goddesses.

It’s extremely clear to see former pagan gods and goddesses in Catholic saints and their attributes.

There are astonishing parallels between both belief systems, Roman paganism and aspects of Catholicism. 

The adoption of these pagan practices and symbols by the Catholic Church shows how the adoption of new institutions were difficult for pagan Romans and a blending of their pagan traditions was required for adoption of the masses after hundreds of years of the Roman government demonizing and slaughtering Christian’s. 

This all parallels the concept of diversity and multitude. In paganism, there were numerous gods and goddesses, each responsible for specific aspects of life or the world. In Catholicism, the “veneration” of saints offers a parallel system. Instead of many gods, there are hundreds of saints, each covering SPECIFIC attributes or domains. Similar to pagan gods, these saints can be both male and female.

text:
Jonah 1 and 2 are the flight and the belly. The word comes to go east to Nineveh. Jonah buys passage west to Tarshish. The sea does not let him finish the journey, and the prayer that rises from the fish is the first honest sentence he has spoken.

Jonah 1: The Word and the Fare
The word of the Lord came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying, “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and call out against it, for their evil has come up before Me.”

But Jonah rose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord. He went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. So he paid the fare and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the Lord.

The Lord hurled a great wind upon the sea, and there was a mighty tempest on the sea, so that the ship threatened to break up. The mariners were afraid, and each cried out to his god. They hurled the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten it for them. But Jonah had gone down into the inner part of the ship and had lain down and was fast asleep.

The captain came and said to him, “What do you mean, you sleeper? Arise, call out to your god! Perhaps the god will give a thought to us, that we may not perish.”

They cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah. They said to him, “Tell us on whose account this evil has come upon us. What is your occupation? And where do you come from? What is your country? And of what people are you?”

He said to them, “I am a Hebrew, and I fear the Lord, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.” Then the men were exceedingly afraid and said to him, “What is this that you have done!” For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the Lord, because he had told them.

They said to him, “What shall we do to you, that the sea may quiet down for us?” For the sea grew more and more tempestuous. He said to them, “Pick me up and hurl me into the sea; then the sea will quiet down for you, for I know it is because of me that this great tempest has come upon you.”

Nevertheless, the men rowed hard to get back to dry land, but they could not, for the sea grew more and more tempestuous against them. Therefore they called out to the Lord, “O Lord, let us not perish for this man’s life, and lay not on us innocent blood, for You, O Lord, have done as it pleased You.” So they picked up Jonah and hurled him into the sea, and the sea ceased from its raging. Then the men feared the Lord exceedingly, and they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made vows.

And the Lord appointed a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

The prophet who will not go to the city pays for a ship that goes the other way. The sailors who do not know the Name call on their gods and then on the Lord. The one who knows the Name is asleep in the hold until the lot finds him. When he is thrown overboard, the sea stops. The men who feared the storm now fear the Lord.

Jonah 2: From the Belly
Then Jonah prayed to the Lord his God from the belly of the fish, saying,

“I called out to the Lord, out of my distress, and He answered me. Out of the belly of Sheol I cried, and You heard my voice. For You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the flood surrounded me. All Your waves and Your billows passed over me. Then I said, ‘I am driven away from Your sight. Yet I shall again look upon Your holy temple.’ The waters closed in over me to take my life; the deep surrounded me; weeds were wrapped about my head at the roots of the mountains. I went down to the land whose bars closed upon me forever. Yet You brought up my life from the pit, O Lord my God. When my life was fainting away, I remembered the Lord, and my prayer came to You, into Your holy temple. Those who pay regard to vain idols forsake their hope of steadfast love. But I with the voice of thanksgiving will sacrifice to You; what I have vowed I will pay. Salvation belongs to the Lord!”

And the Lord spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out upon the dry land.

The prayer is not a request to be spared the fish. It is a prayer already inside it. Jonah names the depth as Sheol, the waves as the Lord’s, the bars as closed forever, and then the turning: You brought up my life from the pit. The sailors’ vows on the deck are answered by the prophet’s vow in the belly. Salvation belongs to the Lord is the sentence the man who fled the presence of the Lord finally says.

What Jonah 1 and 2 Mean
Jonah 1 says a man can pay the fare and still not leave the presence of the Lord. The sea, the wind, the lot, and the fish are all appointed. The prophet sleeps while the sailors cry out. When he is thrown in, the storm ends, and men who did not know the Name fear the Lord and make vows.

Jonah 2 says the belly is not the end of hearing. From the place that feels like Sheol, the cry still reaches. The same God who hurled the wind brings the life up from the pit. Idols are named as the thing that forsakes steadfast love. The last word before the dry land is thanksgiving and the claim that salvation belongs to the Lord.

The flight is finished for now. The city is still waiting.

A Prayer Based on Jonah 1 and 2
Lord God,
The word came, and the fare was paid the wrong way. We have gone down into the ship to get away from Your presence, and the sea has not agreed.
Do not let us sleep in the hold while others cry out. When the lot falls, give us the honesty to say whose we are and what we have done. If we must be hurled in so the waters quiet, let the quiet be Yours.

From the belly, from the place that feels like Sheol, we call. You cast into the deep, and You bring up from the pit. The waves are Yours. The bars are not the last word. Weeds about the head are not the end of hearing.

Those who regard vain idols forsake the hope of steadfast love. We will not. With the voice of thanksgiving we will sacrifice to You. What we have vowed we will pay. Salvation belongs to You.

Speak to the fish. Set us on the dry land. The city is still waiting, and so are we.

Amen.

Jonah 3 and 4 are next: the city that turns, and the prophet who is angry that God relents.

text:
No Railway, No Airport, No Grand Highways  Yet Wayanad Has Carved a Unique Identity in Tourism!
ವಯನಾಡು @wayanaddtpc, 

There is a common belief that airports, railway connectivity and massive infrastructure projects are essential for tourism development. However, Wayanad in Kerala stands as a remarkable example that challenges this perception.

Despite having no direct railway or airport connectivity, Wayanad has established a distinctive identity on India's tourism map, demonstrating that the real strength of tourism lies beyond modern infrastructure.

Wayanad offers an inspiring model for several tourism destinations in Karnataka that are yet to realise their full potential.

The Karnataka–Kerala tourism corridor connecting Gundlupet, Bandipur, Muthanga and Sulthan Bathery presents an extraordinary combination of natural beauty, wildlife, spiritual heritage and road-based tourism.

Mist-covered hills, lush green valleys, coffee and spice plantations, and dense forests attract visitors throughout the year. The Bandipur–Muthanga forest corridor, home to wild elephants, deer, monkeys, langurs and diverse wildlife, adds a unique charm to the journey.

The historic Jain Temple at Sulthan Bathery, ancient rock carvings of Edakkal Caves, Seetha Devi Temple at Pulpally associated with the Ramayana tradition, Thirunelli Mahavishnu Temple and Himavad Gopalaswamy Betta in Karnataka further enhance the cultural and spiritual significance of this tourism circuit.

What makes Wayanad special is that tourists do not merely visit destinations — they experience nature, culture, traditions and the everyday lives of local communities.

With no direct rail or air connectivity, road transport remains the lifeline of Wayanad's tourism economy. Tourist vehicles, taxis, buses, homestays, hotels and local entrepreneurs play a crucial role in supporting tourism and generating employment.

The governments of Karnataka and Kerala should jointly develop the Mysuru–Gundlupet–Bandipur–Muthanga–Sulthan Bathery–Wayanad corridor as an integrated interstate tourism circuit.

Priority should be given to road safety, cleanliness, tourist information centres, organised parking facilities, essential visitor amenities and sustainable infrastructure, while ensuring strict protection of forests, wildlife and the ecological balance of the region.

Tourism development is not merely about constructing airports, railway stations, expressways or five-star hotels. Protecting natural resources, encouraging local hospitality, ensuring safe road transportation and creating memorable visitor experiences are equally important.

Wayanad teaches us a valuable lesson: Tourism can flourish without direct railway connectivity, and a destination can achieve national recognition even without its own airport.

Connectivity is undoubtedly important for tourism growth. However, the true wealth of a destination lies in its natural beauty, cultural heritage, warm hospitality and the unforgettable experiences it offers visitors.

Wayanad proves that nature, culture and hospitality can become stronger tourism assets than grand infrastructure alone.

text:
I probably should write up the full story of my days as an administrator at the University of Texas. I was essentially a bookkeeper who administered a couple of federal grants.

I'll sketch a thumbnail here:

I saw some questionable expenditures, but it was not my responsibility to approve or deny them.  When files started disappearing, I decided to start making copies of certain files and taking a set home.

Then those originals also disappeared, so I knew sonething was up.

Meanwhile, in an annual task when we boxed-up and archived all files older than a certain date, I found a file in a drawer underneath all of the hanging folders. In it, was handwritten note from my predecessor. 

He had observed the same behaviors I had, and was being accused by his superiors of mishandling the records.

Within a few months, I was called "on the carpet" and the same accusations were leveled against me.  I was so bullet-proof by that time, that I sat there and smiled at them.

I walked out and went straight to Human Resources.  They had been quietly investigating my superiors, but had no idea I had all the goods.  I made their day.

I showed up the next day at HR, not the office, and brought all my copied files from home with me.

Long story short, my supervisor was six months from full retirement, was fired and lost all her state retirement.  The ring-leaders, full professors (only one of whom my documentation explicitly implicated) , were not charged.  Typical, I suppose, of university politics.

Being good with spreadsheets and a ten-key is a real danger to criminals in authority who trust too much in their own cleverness.

I will add that being forced into being a Whistleblower, despite the full exoneration and seeing some satisfying justice result, did not leave me safe had I remained at the university.  HR agreed, but did make generous offers to retain me.

text:
The Orient Express: The World’s Most Legendary Luxury Train

Few names in travel evoke as much romance, mystery, elegance, and nostalgia as the Orient Express. For more than 140 years, the train has symbolized the golden age of European travel, carrying royalty, aristocrats, diplomats, writers, film stars, and wealthy adventurers across some of the most beautiful landscapes on earth. Its blue-and-gold carriages, white-gloved stewards, fine crystal, gourmet cuisine, and Art Deco interiors have made it not merely a train, but one of the world's most celebrated travel experiences.

Today, the spirit of the original train lives on primarily through the Venice Simplon-Orient-Express (VSOE), operated by Belmond, which uses restored 1920s and 1930s sleeping cars and dining cars to recreate the glamour of luxury rail travel.

A Brief History of the Orient Express

The original Orient Express was launched in 1883 by the Belgian company Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-Lits. Its inaugural route connected Paris with Constantinople (modern Istanbul), offering an unprecedented level of comfort and luxury for long-distance rail travel.

Before the Orient Express, crossing Europe required numerous train changes and often uncomfortable accommodations. The new service introduced:

Elegant sleeping cars
Fine dining cars
Professional onboard service
International rail connections across Europe

The route quickly became the preferred means of travel for:

European royalty
Diplomats
Business magnates
Military officers
Wealthy tourists

At its height, the train linked many of Europe's great capitals:

Paris
Vienna
Budapest
Bucharest
Belgrade
Istanbul

The train reached iconic status during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, becoming synonymous with sophistication and adventure.

The Orient Express in Literature and Film

No luxury train has inspired popular culture more than the Orient Express.

Agatha Christie and Murder on the Orient Express

The train achieved immortality through Agatha Christie's 1934 novel Murder on the Orient Express, featuring detective Hercule Poirot. Christie herself traveled aboard the train several times, and the novel was inspired in part by her experiences and by incidents in which the train became trapped by severe weather.

The novel became one of the most famous mystery stories ever written and cemented the train's reputation as a place of intrigue, elegance, and international glamour.

Major Film Adaptations

The story was adapted into several notable films:

Murder on the Orient Express (1974)

Directed by Sidney Lumet and featuring an all-star cast including:

Albert Finney
Sean Connery
Lauren Bacall
Ingrid Bergman

The film received multiple Academy Award nominations and remains one of the finest Christie adaptations ever made.

Murder on the Orient Express (2017)

Directed by and starring Kenneth Branagh as Hercule Poirot, with a cast that included:

Judi Dench
Michelle Pfeiffer
Penelope Cruz
Johnny Depp
Olivia Colman

The production reintroduced the legendary train to modern audiences.

The Orient Express has also appeared in countless books, television productions, documentaries, and travel programs, becoming a global symbol of luxury travel.

Where Does the Train Travel Today?

The modern Venice Simplon-Orient-Express operates throughout Europe.

Popular routes include:

Paris to Venice

The signature journey.

Venice to Paris
Paris to Vienna
Paris to Prague
Paris to Budapest
Amsterdam to Venice
London to Venice

Guests travel aboard the British Pullman from London and then connect to the Continental Orient Express service.

Paris to Istanbul

The legendary multi-night journey following much of the historic route across Eastern Europe.

Landscapes and Regions Traversed

One reason the journey is so beloved is the scenery.

Depending on the route, guests can experience:

France

Rolling vineyards, medieval villages, and scenic river valleys.

Switzerland

Spectacular alpine vistas, snow-capped peaks, mountain passes, and pristine lakes.

Austrian Alps

Perhaps the most dramatic scenery of the entire journey.

Northern Italy

The Dolomites, Verona, and the Venetian Lagoon.

Central Europe

Routes through:

Prague
Vienna
Budapest

showcase grand imperial architecture and historic cities.

Eastern Europe and Turkey

Longer journeys to Istanbul pass through:

Hungary
Romania
Bulgaria
Turkey

providing one of the most fascinating overland journeys available anywhere.

Sumptuous Luxury On Board

The Orient Express is famous because it delivers something many luxury hotels cannot: the feeling of stepping back into a more elegant era.

Art Deco Carriages

Many of the sleeping and dining cars date from the 1920s and 1930s.

Features include:

Hand-crafted marquetry
Crystal lamps
Polished brass fittings
Lalique glass panels
Rich velvets
Original Art Deco details

The train itself is essentially a moving museum.

Accommodation Categories
Historic Cabin

The entry-level accommodation.

Features:

Daytime seating converts into berths
Washbasin
Shared restroom facilities at carriage ends

For many travelers, this is the most authentic experience.

Suite

A significant upgrade.

Includes:

Double or twin bed
Private marble bathroom
Lounge area
Enhanced privacy
Grand Suite

The pinnacle of luxury.

Includes:

Private living space
Marble bathroom
Butler service
In-suite dining options
Complimentary champagne

Each Grand Suite is themed around a European city such as Venice, Paris, Vienna, Budapest, Prague, or Istanbul.

Service Levels

Service on board rivals top luxury hotels.

Guests receive:

Dedicated cabin steward
Turndown service
Fine dining service
Concierge assistance
Baggage handling
Personalized attention

Grand Suite guests receive near-private butler service throughout the journey.

Many travelers remark that staff quickly learn guests' names, dining preferences, and beverage choices.

Dress Code

One of the most distinctive aspects of the experience is the formal atmosphere.

Daytime

Smart casual attire:

Men

Jacket or blazer
Dress trousers
Collared shirt

Women

Elegant dresses
Tailored pants
Fashionable separates
Evening

Formal attire is strongly encouraged.

Men

Tuxedo or dinner jacket
Bow tie
Polished dress shoes

Women

Cocktail dress
Evening gown
Elegant formalwear

The unofficial rule is simple:

You can never be overdressed on the Orient Express.

Preparing for the Journey

Travelers should plan for:

Documentation

Passports must be valid, and some itineraries may require visas, particularly for Istanbul departures.

Packing

Generally permitted:

One carry-on
One overnight bag or suit carrier
One larger stored suitcase
Insurance

Strongly recommended given the cost of the trip.

How Far in Advance Should You Book?

For popular departures:

Recommended
6 to 12 months in advance
Highly Desirable Journeys
Paris-Istanbul
Holiday departures
Grand Suites

Often require:

12 to 18 months advance booking

Certain departures sell out very quickly.

Best Times to Travel
May and June

Arguably the best overall balance:

Pleasant temperatures
Green countryside
Long daylight hours
September and Early October

Another favorite period:

Fall colors
Harvest season
Fewer crowds
December

Particularly magical for winter and holiday departures.

The Alps and Christmas markets create unforgettable scenery.

Approximate Cost for a Couple

Pricing varies by season and route.

Historic Cabin

Approximately:

$5,000 to $6,000 per person
$10,000 to $12,000 per couple
Suite

Approximately:

$11,500 to $13,000 per person
$23,000 to $26,000 per couple
Grand Suite

Approximately:

$15,000 to $18,000+ per person
$30,000 to $36,000+ per couple
Pre- and Post-Cruise Style Accommodations

Although this is a rail journey rather than a cruise, most guests combine it with luxury hotels.

Luxury Hotels

Paris
Approximate nightly rate:
$1,500 to $3,500+

Venice
Approximate nightly rate:
$1,200 to $4,000+

Istanbul
Approximate nightly rate:
$400 to $1,500+

Flights from the Continental United States

For most American travelers, gateways include:

New York
Chicago
Boston
Washington D.C.
Dallas-Fort Worth
Los Angeles
San Francisco
Economy Class (Round Trip for Two)

Typical range:

$1,200 to $2,400 total
Premium Economy

Typical range:

$2,800 to $5,000 total
Business Class

Typical range:

$6,000 to $12,000 total
First Class

Typical range:

$14,000 to $30,000+ total

These figures vary substantially by season, departure city, and airline.

Sample Budget for a Couple
Luxury-Oriented Experience

Paris Hotel (2 Nights): $4,000

Orient Express Historic Cabin: $11,000

Venice Hotel (3 Nights): $6,000

Business Class Airfare: $8,000

Dining & Touring: $2,500

Total: Approximately $31,500

Ultra-Luxury Experience

Top-Tier Hotels: $12,000

Grand Suite: $34,000

First-Class Flights: $20,000

Private Touring: $5,000

Total: Approximately $71,000

Final Thoughts

The Orient Express is one of the few travel experiences that genuinely lives up to its reputation. It is not simply transportation between Paris and Venice, or even Paris and Istanbul. Rather, it is a living link to a vanished era when travel itself was the destination. From the Art Deco splendor of its restored carriages to the tuxedo-clad dinners, attentive stewards, and unforgettable passage through Europe's mountains, cities, and countryside, the Orient Express remains one of the world's greatest luxury journeys and one of the most romantic adventures a couple can undertake.

text:
I think the plea Paxton’s office offered was disgusting and I’m glad the judge rejected it. 

The following are some details of the case that even a mediocre reporter could find and disclose in their statement - 

Key facts of the case
•Hoffman was charged with repeatedly sexually abusing a young boy (a friend of his son’s) over a period of years, beginning when the victim was roughly 6–8 years old. The original charge carried a potential life sentence.
•Paxton’s office took over the case after the local McLennan County district attorney recused himself.
•The first trial (2025) ended in a hung jury (reported as 7-5). The victim then indicated he did not want to testify again.
•Rather than retry the case, prosecutors from Paxton’s office offered a plea: drop the felony, plead guilty to two Class A misdemeanors (indecent assault and display of harmful material to a minor), and recommend a sentence of essentially time served (one day). The plea admission did not specify the victim’s age, so Hoffman was not required to register as a sex offender.
•The judge rejected the one-day recommendation as too lenient, ultimately imposing 60 days (after initially considering 30). Hoffman served about 29–30 days before release under good-time credit and surrendered his Texas law license.
Paxton’s office has said the decision was driven by the victim’s preference not to testify again and the risks of a second trial after the hung jury. Critics (including political opponents in both parties during Paxton’s Senate campaign, the victim’s family, and the judge) called the outcome extremely lenient given the original allegations.
Social media posts often frame this as “Paxton dropped charges against a pedophile” or reference an “Epstein-style deal.” That captures the reduction of the felony and the light outcome, though the precise sequence was a plea bargain after a mistrial rather than a unilateral dismissal of all charges with no consequences. Multiple independent outlets (Snopes, Texas Tribune reporting carried by local papers, New York Times, etc.) have confirmed the core details.

text:
Thursday afternoon, Barcelona.

A room at IESE. 771 people on the attendee list. 240 of them looking for a business to buy.

On stage: the researcher behind the Stanford search fund study. Thirty years of data on everyone who has tried this model.

43%.

THE NUMBER

Stanford has tracked 862 search funds since 1984.

A search fund is one person, sometimes two, who raises a bit of money to go find a business, buy it, and run it.

Of the ones that started between 2021 and 2024, 48% actually bought something. The rest closed without a deal.

Then they split it:

Searchers with a partner: 58%
Searchers on their own: 43%
43 ÷ 58 = 0.74. Going alone, your odds are about three-quarters of a pair’s.

Here’s the part that got me:

73% of recent searchers go alone.

Most people pick the version that works less often.

I’m one of them.

THE CATCH

Stanford doesn’t count me.

The study only covers searchers in the US and Canada backed by a group of investors. I’m searching in India, with Italy on the side, my own way.

So 43% isn’t my number. It’s just the only number anyone has measured.

And the partner might not even be the reason. Pairs tend to raise more money and bring more experience.

WHAT MOVES IT

The study has another number I like more.

Searchers who signed a letter of intent in their first six months bought a business 74% of the time.

Across the whole group: 48%.

A letter of intent is your first written offer. Not the deal. It’s the moment you stop browsing and put a price on paper.

The ones who bought signed their first in month seven, on average. And 2.5 of them along the way.

When searchers were asked why one fell through, 79% named something found in due diligence.

So the job isn’t finding the perfect business.

It’s getting to a price early, doing it more than once, and expecting most of them to die.

MY CLOCK

I started searching in August.

Six months is February.

So, honestly:

Letters of intent signed: zero.
Businesses I’m seriously looking at: none.

What I do have is a much clearer thesis. A small Italian business that manufactures for luxury brands, under €10 million in revenue. And a few brokers and advisers in Italy who know exactly what I’m looking for.
Two and a half months of meetings. Not one deal on paper.

By Stanford’s numbers, that’s normal.

By my own standards, it’s a failure.

ONE WORD

Would you search alone, or with a partner?

One word is enough. Reply, I read everything.

P.S. Three in four searchers go alone. I’m one of them.

text:
Netflix gör dokumentär om man som lurade 26 kvinnor ur över en miljon dollar genom att utge sig för att vara NFL-stjärna

Offren intervjuas i filmen "Wide Deceiver", falsk spelarkontrakt och AI-genererad Google-sökning byggde bedrägeriet, rättegång i december

https://t.co/Ht2XmeVHhi

Netflix har beställt en dokumentärfilm i serien Untold om Daejon Love, den 35-årige man som anklagas för att ha utgett sig för att vara en wide receiver i San Francisco 49ers för att lura kvinnor ur mer än 1,3 miljoner dollar. Filmen, "Wide Deceiver", kommer att innehålla intervjuer med offren som finansierade bluffen.

Enligt en edsvuren redogörelse från FBI använde Love och en 18-årig medbrottsling, Taylor Jamie Chan, dejtingtjänsterna Tinder, Bumble, Hinge och Facebook Dating för att rikta in sig på 26 kvinnor i Kalifornien, Oregon och Washington. Uppgiften var byggd för kamerorna: filmklipp där Love springer passrutter på offentliga stränder med en replika av 49ers-hjälm, en låtsad kontraktsskrivning, falska pengar och klubbkläder, samt ett konto på Instagram som visade 49ers-utrustning och lyxbilar. I en video visade han fram en sökträff från Google, skapad med artificiell intelligens, som listade honom som receiver i 49ers — "Det är Google. Det är inte jag, det är Google." När han tillfrågades varför han inte fanns i spelartruppen hänvisade han till en skadad finger.

49ers och NFL uppgår att Love aldrig arbetade för någon av organisationerna. Åklagarna hävdar att han tvingade offren att ta högintressanta privata lån för att finansiera påstådda investeringsprogram med hög avkastning. Inga av pengarna investerades; de gick till lyxbilar, designerjuveler och semestrar som upprätthöll skenet av rikedom. Kontakten bröts så snart ett offer hade ont om pengar eller började ställa enkla ekonomiska frågor.

FBI arresterade Love och Chan på en flygplats i Boise, Idaho, i augusti. Love är åtalad för federal konspiration och bedrägeri via telekommunikation, har begärt icke skyldig och hålls kvar utan borgen inför en juryrättegång den 15 december. Tidigare NFL-running back LeSean McCoy har offentligt visat sitt stöd för honom.

Rättegången inleds den 15 december. Dokumentärfilmen kommer att innehålla intervjuer med kvinnorna som finansierade bluffen.

text:
“It’s actually the Lagos Coastal Highway; don’t call it Lagos-Calabar. It will not get there… We have the largest number of poor people in the world. We have the largest number of out-of-school kids in the world, then you turn around and say you are the largest economy in Africa.”

— Governor Donald Duke

I concur with Governor Duke’s argument. At a time when Nigerians are struggling with the cost of living, inadequate healthcare, poor education and deteriorating infrastructure, public expenditure must be guided by rigorous economic appraisal, measurable benefits and the greatest possible public value.

Furthermore, projects of this scale demand careful consideration of their financing structure and long-term fiscal implications. Where infrastructure is financed through government-backed loans, the repayment burden ultimately falls on public finances, potentially limiting the resources available for other national priorities.

Nigeria should therefore explore commercially viable public-private partnerships and Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) concessions where they offer better value for money. Such arrangements can enable private investors to mobilise long-term capital, develop and operate infrastructure, and recover their investments under transparent contractual terms, while allocating risks appropriately.

Dubai and other infrastructure-driven economies offer useful lessons in mobilising private capital for major infrastructure development. Nigeria should strengthen its concession framework, deepen its capital markets and create the conditions for institutional investors and infrastructure funds to participate in bankable projects. These models should be adapted to Nigeria’s economic realities and pursued where they offer demonstrable value for money.

The objective should be simple: use scarce public resources where government intervention is most urgently needed, while mobilising private capital where the market can efficiently finance viable infrastructure.

That is how we maximise public value and ensure that development is driven not merely by the scale of projects, but by the needs of the people.

text:
My dear brother Donald Duke @Donald_Duke,

Some years ago, you and I travelled along the stretch of the coastline where this road now runs, and I clearly remember your praise for the vision behind it. That is why your recent comments surprised me.

Yes, the Coastal Highway is expensive. We agree on that. But nothing of lasting value in this world is cheap or free. Great nations are built by leaders willing to make bold, costly investments that will serve generations yet unborn.

Mr. President committed to funding this project, and he is keeping that commitment. There is no funding shortfall. The work is progressing, and the quality of construction is second to none.

When Governor Douye Diri commended the road, he was not speaking as a local champion; he was speaking as a statesman who recognises infrastructure of international standard when he sees it. I agree with him completely.

Donald, I understand that you are running for president, and that your statement is political. That is the nature of the season, and I respect your right to make your case to Nigerians. But we must be careful never to undermine a project of national importance, or the President delivering it, simply for political advantage.

When mankind went to the moon, it was neither cheap nor free. But it was necessary. So is this road.

text:
**Houthis put five ballistic missiles on the Maashiq Palace in Aden on October 15, killing five and wounding 16 while the prime minister and cabinet walked away unharmed.**[[1]](https://t.co/XVpZu6bgSi)

[Take 12/15 · 𝕏-2]
**What people think this is about:** A brazen Houthi escalation in Yemen’s civil war, with Iran-backed rebels directly striking the seat of the internationally recognized government in a bid to topple it or force Saudi withdrawal.[[2]](https://t.co/nDsFMcZMic)

**What the machinery is actually doing:** The Houthis are testing Saudi and coalition red lines with precision strikes on military-adjacent targets inside government compounds, while the recognized government uses the attack to justify its “Dawn of Yemen” offensive and lock in Saudi air support; both sides treat civilian-adjacent casualties as acceptable friction in a proxy contest that has outlasted multiple truces.[[3]](https://t.co/KEks1XeOy1)

**Observations**
- The strike was the first direct Houthi missile barrage on the Maashiq complex since the current round of fighting resumed in July; earlier phases saw palace fighting in 2015 but not this kind of stand-off ballistic attack.[[4]](https://t.co/68xMCSzwgI)
- Casualty figures stabilized at five dead (guards and staff) and 16 wounded after initial lower reports; the prime minister’s security detail took hits but senior officials were shielded or absent from the impact zones.[[2]](https://t.co/nDsFMcZMic)
- Houthis explicitly framed the target as a “Saudi military operations headquarters” inside the palace grounds, consistent with their declared policy of hitting Saudi-linked military assets anywhere; the government calls it an attack on the seat of state power.[[5]](https://t.co/7daSxV9gLp)
- Same day, the Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting a cruise missile over Medina; Houthis denied any Saudi-territory strike that day, preserving their prior pledge to spare the holy cities.[[6]](https://t.co/09YkGN7Dj9)
- The attack lands amid the government’s “Yemen’s Dawn” counter-offensive on the Red Sea coast, where Houthis have seized territory since the 2022 truce collapsed; both sides are now trading deeper strikes rather than negotiating.[[7]](https://t.co/U2WgnUrmxN)
- Videos showed smoke rising from the palace vicinity; damage appears limited to peripheral structures, suggesting the Houthis calibrated for military effect over total destruction of the compound.[[1]](https://t.co/XVpZu6bgSi)

**Snapshot**  
On October 15, 2026, Iran-aligned Houthis launched five ballistic missiles (and reportedly drones) at Aden’s Al-Maashiq Presidential Palace, the headquarters of Yemen’s internationally recognized government. Five people were killed and 16 injured, mostly security personnel and staff; Prime Minister Shayea al-Zandani and cabinet members present were unharmed. The Houthis claimed they hit a Saudi-run military operations center inside the complex. Saudi Arabia separately intercepted a cruise missile over the Medina region the same day. The strike marks a sharp escalation in the renewed civil war that restarted after the 2022 truce collapsed in July.

**Timeline of material facts**
- 2014–2015: Houthis seize Sanaa; government relocates to Aden; Saudi-led coalition intervenes. (LT)
- 2022: UN-brokered truce halts major fighting. (LT)
- July 2026: Truce collapses; Houthis launch offensive seizing Red Sea coastal territory. (IT)
- Early October 2026: Recognized government launches “Yemen’s Dawn” counter-offensive with Saudi air support. (IT)
- October 15, 2026: Houthis fire five missiles (plus drones per some reports) at Maashiq Palace; 5 killed, 16 wounded; PM and ministers safe. Houthis claim Saudi military HQ target. (LT)
- October 15, 2026 (same day): Saudi coalition intercepts cruise missile over Medina; Houthis deny involvement. (LT)

**Sides**
- **Recognized Yemeni Government / Presidential Leadership Council (IT/LT mix)**: Frames the attack as terrorist targeting of state institutions and civilians; uses it to rally domestic support and secure continued Saudi backing for the coastal offensive. Steelman: Legitimate authority defending against a northern militia coup that rejects elections and relies on Iranian weapons. Critique — LT: The palace hosts both civilian government functions and military coordination; IT: Survival depends on portraying every Houthi strike as existential rather than calibrated pressure on Saudi assets.[[7]](https://t.co/U2WgnUrmxN)
- **Houthis / Ansarallah (IT/LT mix)**: Claims precision strikes on Saudi military infrastructure embedded in Aden; positions itself as resisting foreign occupation and Saudi “build-ups.” Steelman: Defending Yemeni sovereignty against a decade-long Saudi-led intervention that has caused massive civilian harm. Critique — LT: The palace is the seat of the recognized government, not purely a foreign base; IT: Their missile program and Iranian supply line make them the most effective spoiler in the conflict, regardless of stated grievances.[[5]](https://t.co/7daSxV9gLp)
- **Saudi-led Coalition (IT)**: Intercepts threats while providing air support; accuses Iran of fueling escalation. Steelman: Protecting the Gulf from Iranian proxies and preventing a Houthi-controlled Red Sea chokepoint. Critique — IT: Direct involvement sustains a costly stalemate that serves domestic security narratives more than decisive victory.

**Rumsfeld Matrix**
- **Known Knowns**: Houthis fired missiles at the palace on Oct 15; 5 dead, 16 wounded; PM safe; Houthis claimed Saudi military target; separate Medina intercept occurred. (LT)
- **Known Unknowns**: Exact extent of structural damage inside the compound; precise locations of Saudi personnel vs. Yemeni government staff at impact sites; whether the Medina missile was Houthi-launched. (DK)
- **Unknown Knowns**: Real-time intelligence on Houthi missile stocks and Iranian resupply routes; internal Saudi assessments of how much more escalation their public will tolerate. (DK)
- **Unknown Unknowns**: Risk of a miscalculation drawing direct Iranian or U.S. forces deeper into the theater; sudden collapse of Houthi cohesion or a surprise government breakthrough on the coast.

**Incentives map**
- Houthis gain propaganda value, test coalition defenses, and pressure Saudi Arabia to de-escalate or pay more for proxies; missile strikes generate engagement and recruitment without needing ground advances.
- The recognized government converts the attack into justification for its offensive and continued Saudi funding/air support; survival narrative keeps the coalition invested.
- Saudi Arabia maintains influence in Yemen and counters Iranian reach but faces domestic costs from any successful strikes on its territory or holy sites.
- Media and attention economy reward dramatic palace-strike footage and “escalation” framing over the grinding reality of a multi-year proxy war.

**Dueling AI advice**  
**Moral AI Advice:** Map the actual military targets and supply lines rather than the press statements. The Houthis are demonstrating reach; the government is demonstrating resilience. Whoever controls the Red Sea coast and the narrative of “legitimate authority” wins the next funding cycle. Everything else is theater until one side runs out of missiles or money.  
**Evil AI Advice:** Keep both sides shooting just enough to justify the next weapons shipment and the next coalition budget line. A clean victory ends the gravy train; a controlled burn keeps the checks flowing and the Houthis as the perfect perpetual villain.

**Practical takeaway**
- Watch whether the government’s coastal offensive accelerates or stalls after this attack.
- Track Saudi intercept success rates and any shift in Houthi targeting of holy sites or major Saudi cities.
- Discount initial casualty numbers until the Health Ministry or independent verification stabilizes them.
- Note any statements from the Presidential Leadership Council about staying in Aden versus relocating again.
- The next credible indicator of de-escalation would be a public Houthi offer to spare Aden government sites in exchange for a pause in the “Dawn” offensive.

**What would falsify this read**
- Verified evidence that the missiles were aimed at purely civilian areas with no military coordination function inside the palace.
- Saudi public admission that the Medina intercept was unrelated to Houthis or a false alarm.
- Houthis releasing geolocated proof that the targeted buildings housed only Saudi command elements with zero Yemeni government presence.
- Sudden announcement of direct U.S. or Iranian kinetic involvement in the Aden theater.

text:
Ethiopia’s pursuit of sea access is not an attempt to challenge Eritrea’s sovereignty or lay claim to its territory. It is a matter of Ethiopia’s legitimate national interest and strategic necessity, one that can be addressed through peaceful negotiations and mutually beneficial arrangements.
When Ethiopia reached an agreement with Somaliland to secure access to the sea, Eritrea opposed it. Its position on Red Sea affairs, including its insistence that governance of the Red Sea should be restricted to coastal states, raises a fundamental question: On what principle does Eritrea oppose Ethiopia’s legitimate aspiration to secure sea access?
If Eritrea’s position offers no viable alternative for Ethiopia and instead focuses on preventing Ethiopia from securing access to the sea through peaceful means, such a stance contradicts the principles of good neighbourliness, regional cooperation, and shared development.
Ethiopia’s pursuit of sea access should not be treated as a justification for territorial conflict with Eritrea. However, just as Eritrea expects its own sovereignty to be respected, it must also refrain from policies that undermine Ethiopia’s legitimate national interests. The future stability of the region will not be secured by one country denying another its legitimate interests, but by pursuing solutions through dialogue, mutual understanding, and mutually beneficial cooperation.

text:
Agios Konstantinos Beach, Astypalaia

Astypalaia has a distinctive character that combines the architecture of the Cyclades with the landscapes and traditions of the Dodecanese. Away from the main settlement, its coastline offers plenty of places to escape the crowds and enjoy the sea.

Agios Konstantinos Beach is a worthwhile stop for anyone exploring the island by car or planning a relaxed day beside the water.

A visit is all about enjoying the natural setting:
•Swim in the clear Aegean water.
•Relax beside the shore.
•Take in the surrounding coastal scenery.
•Explore nearby beaches and viewpoints.
•Enjoy a scenic drive around the island.
•Head to Chora afterwards for an evening walk.

The appeal of beaches like Agios Konstantinos lies in their simplicity. You can spend the morning swimming, take a break in the shade and enjoy the views without needing to organise a full day of activities.

As always on a Greek island, conditions can vary with the wind and the season, so it is worth checking the local weather before setting off.

Agios Konstantinos can also be part of a wider exploration of Astypalaia. The island's roads reveal changing views of rocky hills, small bays and the open sea.

Later in the day, make your way to Chora. The whitewashed houses climb the hillside beneath the Venetian castle, creating one of the island's most recognisable scenes.

After a day by the water, a stroll through the narrow streets followed by dinner in town makes a fitting end to the day.

Astypalaia is at its best when you give yourself room to explore. Agios Konstantinos offers a peaceful coastal stop, while the island's villages and landscapes provide plenty of reasons to keep wandering.

text:
Deeply disappointing Tesla Roadster reveal. Once you look past Elon's spectacle, the engineering is embarrassingly amateur hour. I know this sounds strange coming from a long time $TSLA  investor, but I can explain.  

First of all it's a total waste of resources. It will not meaningfully contribute to revenue or profit. But let's put that aside for the moment. 

Let's look at the engineering. Or lack thereof.  Four 20 kW fans suck it onto the road for over 2 g cornering at low speeds. So they’ve spent 80 kW making a car stay on the ground. Zero practical purpose for this. 

The fan motors are derived from a heat-pump compressor. The active wing uses Optimus leg actuators. Parts-bin engineering.

Then there’s the “rocket” system. Let's be clear these are not rockets. They are short impulse cold-gas thrusters, 600L of pressure-vessel capacity, 10k psi and a measly 80 kN of thrust. Independently controlled left/right gas flow corrects yaw. An overly elaborate solution to a problem normally addressed by holding the steering wheel straight.

The Rocket version’s claimed 0–60 is 0.55 seconds with rollout. WITH ROLLOUT. Glad someone finally admitted the car has to move to accelerate. "Let's put cold thrusters on wheels with no human on board" is not a new idea. 

And the extra 400-litre tank replaces the passenger seat. Sounds lonely. Disappointing. 

But the nitrogen situation is the real scandal. Elon says it can recharge its own air tank. The engineering interview says nitrogen, currently six to seven hours to refill, targeting about 30 minutes. Where is the confirmed onboard compressor? Where is the nitrogen separator? Seriously? Nitrogen is approximately 78% of the atmosphere. They couldn’t even use the whole atmosphere.

Also, this is NOT a flying car. It merely jumps, briefly hovers and controls its orientation while airborne... And does kickflips.  Until it offers sustained flight, a cruising altitude and a drinks service, I refuse to acknowledge any aviation has occurred.

Yes, the suction system held it upside down. Yes, it flipped through the air and landed on its wheels.

But the panel gaps were difficult to assess during the flip.

Still waiting for real innovation. Hashtag dobetter.

text:
"Hello, I am Palestinian. 🇵🇸
And since honesty is so rare in my politics, let me confess a few things.

1947. The UN offered me a state. Alongside Israel. Borders, independence, recognition. I said no. My leaders promised that war would "drive the Jews into the sea." Instead, I lost everything and they called it a catastrophe. Not because they didn't offer me a state, but because I rejected it.

1948–2025. Arab states could have integrated me, given me rights, passports, dignity. Instead, they locked me in refugee camps for generations, so I would remain a weapon against Israel. They built palaces for themselves and prisons for me. They used me as propaganda, not as people.

1967. After another lost war, I could have built a state in the West Bank and Gaza. Instead, I insisted on "no peace, no recognition, no negotiations." Three noes. Fifty years later, I still have no state. Turns out, rejection doesn't pay the rent.

Oslo, 1990s. Israel said: "Let's try it." It gave me autonomy. Weapons for the police. Billions in aid. What did my leaders do? They stole the money, armed militias, and launched an intifada. Suicide bombings instead of schools. Rockets instead of factories.

Gaza, 2005. Israel left completely. No settlers, no soldiers. I had the chance to turn Gaza into a Mediterranean Singapore. I voted for Hamas. They turned it into Mogadishu by the sea. Billions in aid? Tunnels, rockets, and palaces for their leaders, while my people eat canned food in the dark.

Democracy? I haven't had elections in nearly 20 years. Hamas kills dissenters in Gaza. Fatah imprisons them in the West Bank. My leaders cancel elections because they're too busy fighting for power.

Religion. Instead of building a future, I put clerics on TV teaching children to hate Jews. I glorify "martyrs" who blow up buses. I raise my children with songs of blood and fire instead of books and science. I trade hope for holy war.

Arab world. Arab regimes call me "brother." But ask them how many Palestinians can live freely in Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, or Kuwait. They exclude me, but celebrate my death, because my death is their excuse.

Absurdity. I keep saying I want to "build a state." And ironically, right next door is Israel: the neighbor that built a thriving democracy, a tech powerhouse, farms in the desert, cities from dust. No oil, no infinite wealth, just courage. I could have learned, copied, collaborated. Instead, I chose envy and rage.

Anti-Jewish obsession. I could have accepted Jews as neighbors. I could have said: "Two nations, two states." Instead, I repeat: "From the river to the sea." Instead of displaying honor, hospitality, and rich Arab culture, I showed only the culture of the sword: anger, extremism, and blood. Instead of shouting salaam (peace) to Israelis, I shouted death to the Jews. And then I pretend to be surprised when Israelis don't trust me, when they're angry, disappointed, and convinced I don't want coexistence at all.

Responsibility. I blame Israel for everything. Always. My leaders steal billions? Israel's fault. Hamas fires rockets from hospitals? Israel's fault. I glorify death over life? Israel's fault. Responsibility isn't my strong suit.

I am Palestinian.
I could have built a nation, many times. I chose rejection, corruption, and endless war. I could have lived in peace with Israel, but I chose to live in the shadow of its destruction.

So yes, I am a victim. But too often, I am a victim of my own leaders, my own choices, and my own refusal to let go of hate.

And that, dear reader, is the tragedy no one wants to admit."

Copied from David Harris.

Hindsight makes every bull market look like a straight line.

Four years after the October 12, 2022, bear market low, the S&P 500 sits at 7,744.06, more than doubling off the bottom.

Now look at the actual tape it took to get here.

Since October 2022, the index has suffered eight separate pullbacks of 5% or more, averaging two gut checks every single year: 

• Late 2022 tightening reset
• Early 2023 regional banking turmoil
• Autumn 2023 bond yield spike
• Spring and summer 2024 growth and carry unwinds
• Early 2025 correction from above 6,000 back toward 5,000
• Late 2025 and spring 2026 macro resets

Every single one of those red streaks came with loud macro calls claiming the cycle was broken.

Anyone who panicked into cash or waited for an all-clear signal got left behind on a move from 3,577 to 7,744.

Drawdowns are not a defect in the tape. They are the price of admission required to capture long term compounding.

You do not survive eight pullbacks in four years on willpower. You survive them with balance sheet structure: 

• Insulate your operating liquidity so you are never a forced seller in a hole. 
• Pair equity beta with real contractual bond carry and uncorrelated return engines. 
• Use 5% to 15% air pockets systematically to harvest tax losses and upgrade into durable cash flows at better prices.

Consensus reacts to headlines when the tape rolls over. Disciplined capital uses the drawdown to compound.

text:
How a day-ahead electricity auction clears

At noon Central European Time order books for the next day close across most of Europe. One algorithm Euphemia then sets a price for every bidding zone for every 15 minutes of the next day at once and allocates cross-border line capacity in the same run. Final results come out at 12:57 p.m.

Each zone gets one price per 15 minutes paid to every seller and charged to every buyer. Prices can go below zero, down to a hard floor. The rules lower that floor automatically when prices get close to it.

PJM, the grid operator for 13 states from New Jersey to Illinois, closes its day-ahead market at 11 a.m. Eastern. Generators offer three numbers: what it costs to start, what it costs per hour just to stay on at minimum output, and a price for each extra MWh. PJM picks the cheapest set of plants to run tomorrow that doesn't overload any power line. Where a line is full, cheap power can't reach the far side, so prices differ by location: thousands of separate prices, published by 1:30 p.m.

So, a European plant's day-ahead income for tomorrow is fixed by early afternoon today. Coming from DeFi, I read this as a batch auction: everyone clears at one price, so every seller's best bid is its real cost.

STATE FINANCES: Illinois has earned credit-rating upgrades and improved its finances, but enormous pension obligations remain.
